  (CASE

    WHEN ep.value.double_value IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(ep.value.double_value AS FLOAT64)

WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201101' AND '20210131'
  AND ep.key = 'engagement_time_msec'

classified_sessions.name: classified_sessions
classified_sessions.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- identity columns (keep joinable)
  visitId,
  fullVisitorId,
  -- original date string from GA (YYYYMMDD)
  date,
  -- calendar month in YYYY-MM (lifted logic: take first 6 chars of date and insert dash)
  CONCAT(SUBSTR(date, 1, 4), '-', SUBSTR(date, 5, 2)) AS month,
  -- classify session: 'purchase' if session-level totals.transactions > 0 OR any hit-level item/product revenue > 0, else 'non-purchase'
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) > 0 THEN 'purchase'
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h
      -- check hit transaction revenue or hit.item.itemRevenue or product.productRevenue in nested arrays/structs
      WHERE (h.transaction.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(h.transaction.transactionRevenue AS INT64) > 0)
         OR (h.item IS NOT NULL AND (h.item.itemRevenue IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(h.item.itemRevenue AS INT64) > 0))
         OR EXISTS (
           SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(h.product) AS p
           WHERE (p.productRevenue IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(p.productRevenue AS INT64) > 0)
         )
    ) THEN 'purchase'
    ELSE 'non-purchase'
  END AS session_class,
  -- normalize pageviews: prefer session-level totals.pageviews, treat NULL as 0
  COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(totals.pageviews AS INT64), 0) AS pageviews
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
classified_sessions.description: Normalize and classify sessions into 'purchase' or 'non-purchase' labels based on session-level totals.transactions and the product revenue flags. Also normalize pageviews to a numeric (treat NULL as 0) and compute the session's calendar month (YYYY-MM). This produces one row per session with canonical columns: month, session_class, pageviews, fullVisitorId, visitId, date.

session_classification.name: session_classification
session_classification.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  visitId,
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', SAFE_CAST(date AS STRING))) AS session_month,
  -- A session is a purchase if totals.transactions > 0 OR any hit has a transaction.transactionId (non-null/non-empty)
  (COALESCE(totals.transactions, 0) > 0
   OR EXISTS (
     SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h
     WHERE SAFE_CAST(h.transaction.transactionId AS STRING) IS NOT NULL
       AND TRIM(SAFE_CAST(h.transaction.transactionId AS STRING)) <> ''
   )
  ) AS is_purchase,
  -- prefer totals.pageviews when present, else sum of hit-level pageview indicators via hits.page (count of page hits)
  COALESCE(totals.pageviews,
    (SELECT COUNTIF(h.page.pagePath IS NOT NULL) FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h)
  ) AS pageviews
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
session_classification.description: Canonical session-level classification and normalized fields: compute session_month (YYYY-MM) from date, and determine a boolean or label indicating whether the session is a 'purchase' session by detecting any transaction via hits.transaction.transactionId or totals.transactions > 0. Preserve pageviews and visitor/session identifiers.

session_rows_normalized.name: session_rows_normalized
session_rows_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS fullVisitorId,
  visitStartTime,
  -- canonical session_date: prefer visitStartTime (epoch seconds) converted to DATE, fallback to PARSE_DATE on date string if NULL
  COALESCE(
    DATE(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime)),
    SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)
  ) AS session_date,
  -- device flags / category from top-level device struct
  SAFE_CAST(device.isMobile AS BOOL) AS device_is_mobile,
  device.deviceCategory AS device_category,
  -- keep original hits array for downstream unnesting / processing
  hits
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
session_rows_normalized.description: Normalize session-level rows: canonicalize session date as DATE from visitStartTime or date field, expose relevant session identifiers and device flags, and keep hit-level nested hits for later use. One row per original session record.

raw_sessions_hits.name: raw_sessions_hits
raw_sessions_hits.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session identifiers
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS fullVisitorId,
  visitId AS visitId,
  -- session date
  date AS date,
  -- device category at session level
  device.deviceCategory AS device_deviceCategory,
  -- hit-level transaction fields (may be NULL)
  hits.transaction.transactionId AS hits_transaction_transactionId,
  hits.transaction.transactionRevenue AS hits_transaction_transactionRevenue,
  -- session-level totals.transactions
  totals.transactions AS totals_transactions
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS hits
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
raw_sessions_hits.description: All raw session rows with exploded hits-level indicators needed to detect transactions and session attributes. One row per hit within a session, preserving session-level fields (fullVisitorId, visitId, date, device.*) and hit-level fields (hits.transaction.transactionId, hits.transaction.transactionRevenue) and totals.transactions.

session_transaction_flags.name: session_transaction_flags
session_transaction_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  visitId AS visitId,
  date AS date,
  device.deviceCategory AS device_deviceCategory,
  -- session has a transaction if totals.transactions > 0
  -- OR any hit has a non-NULL transaction.transactionId OR hit.item.transactionId OR hit.transaction.transactionRevenue OR hit.item.itemRevenue
  -- Lifted literals: none
  IF(
    SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) > 0
    OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h
      WHERE h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
         OR h.transaction.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL
         OR h.item.transactionId IS NOT NULL
         OR h.item.itemRevenue IS NOT NULL
    ),
    TRUE, FALSE
  ) AS has_transaction
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
session_transaction_flags.description: One row per session indicating whether that session contains any transaction (based on any hit having a non-null transactionId or non-null transactionRevenue or session totals.transactions > 0) and the session date and device category.

visitor_first_transaction_sessions.name: visitor_first_transaction_sessions
visitor_first_transaction_sessions.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  -- first_transaction_date is the earliest session_date for this visitor where totals_transactions > 0
  FIRST_VALUE(CASE WHEN s.totals_transactions > 0 THEN s.session_date END) OVER (PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId ORDER BY CASE WHEN s.totals_transactions > 0 THEN s.session_date ELSE NULL END ASC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS first_transaction_date,
  s.visitId AS visitId,
  s.session_date AS date,
  s.device_category AS device_deviceCategory
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS raw
-- carry key fields and flatten necessary top-level fields to match requested output; use wildcard shards
-- Extract session-level fields at record root (visitId, fullVisitorId, session_date mapped from date)
CROSS JOIN UNNEST([STRUCT(
  raw.visitId AS visitId,
  raw.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  raw.date AS session_date,
  raw.totals.transactions AS totals_transactions,
  raw.device.deviceCategory AS device_category
)]) AS s
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
visitor_first_transaction_sessions.description: For each visitor, the earliest session date among sessions that have a transaction and all sessions (one row each) that occur on that earliest transaction date, including their device category. This identifies the session(s) that constitute the first transaction event(s) for the visitor.

subsequent_sessions_with_purchases.name: subsequent_sessions_with_purchases
subsequent_sessions_with_purchases.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(NULLIF(userId, ''), fullVisitorId) AS canonical_user_id,
  visitStartTime AS initial_visitStartTime,
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS later
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date
      AND COALESCE(NULLIF(later.userId, ''), later.fullVisitorId) = COALESCE(NULLIF(main.userId, ''), main.fullVisitorId)
      AND later.visitStartTime > main.visitStartTime
      AND (
        COALESCE(later.totals.transactions, 0) > 0
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(later.hits) AS lh
          WHERE lh.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
             OR COALESCE(lh.transaction.transactionRevenue, 0) > 0
        )
      )
  ) AS has_later_purchase,
  (
    SELECT MIN(later.visitStartTime)
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS later
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date
      AND COALESCE(NULLIF(later.userId, ''), later.fullVisitorId) = COALESCE(NULLIF(main.userId, ''), main.fullVisitorId)
      AND later.visitStartTime > main.visitStartTime
      AND (
        COALESCE(later.totals.transactions, 0) > 0
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(later.hits) AS lh
          WHERE lh.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
             OR COALESCE(lh.transaction.transactionRevenue, 0) > 0
        )
      )
  ) AS earliest_later_purchase_visitStartTime
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS main
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date
subsequent_sessions_with_purchases.description: For each canonical_user_id and initial_visitStartTime, indicate whether the user has any later session (visitStartTime > initial_visitStartTime) that contains a purchase. A purchase is defined as totals.transactions > 0 OR any hits.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL OR any hits.transaction.transactionRevenue > 0. Emits a boolean/flag per user indicating presence of a later purchase and the timestamp of the earliest later purchase session if present.

grain: one row per (npi, place_of_service, hcpcs_code) as in source
physicians_supplier_summary.description: Provider-HCPCS-level aggregated measures from the physicians_and_other_supplier_2013 table. Exposes provider identifiers, location, HCPCS and common summary measures with explicit aliases. Use this as the canonical fact table for provider-HCPCS analysis. | Use for: Aggregate provider-level service counts/payments for a HCPCS; Find providers with highest average medicare payment for a code; Join with hcpcs_canonical to enrich hcpcs_description or filter by effective_date

home_health_agency_summary.name: home_health_agency_summary
home_health_agency_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id AS provider_id,
  agency_name AS agency_name,
  street_address AS street_address,
  city AS city,
  state AS state,
  zip_code AS zip_code,
  total_episodes_non_lupa AS total_episodes_non_lupa,
  distinct_beneficiaries_non_lupa AS distinct_beneficiaries_non_lupa,
  average_number_of_total_visits_per_episode_non_lupa AS avg_total_visits_per_episode_non_lupa,
  total_hha_charge_amount_non_lupa AS total_charge_amount_non_lupa,
  total_hha_medicare_payment_amount_non_lupa AS total_medicare_payment_non_lupa,
  average_age AS average_age,
  male_beneficiaries AS male_beneficiaries,
  female_beneficiaries AS female_beneficiaries,
  average_hcc_score AS average_hcc_score
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.home_health_agencies_2014`
grain: one row per home health agency (provider_id) for 2014
home_health_agency_summary.description: Canonical, flattened home health agency table with provider identifiers, geography and common measures for 2014. Use this as the main HHA fact table for comparisons, filtering by geography, and aggregations. | Use for: Compare HHA total payments or episodes across states or agencies; Filter agencies by volume or average visits per episode; Join agency to other provider-level datasets by provider_id or geography

inpatient_charges_provider_agg.name: inpatient_charges_provider_agg
inpatient_charges_provider_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id AS provider_id,
  provider_name AS provider_name,
  provider_city AS provider_city,
  provider_state AS provider_state,
  drg_definition AS drg_definition,
  total_discharges AS total_discharges,
  average_total_payments AS avg_total_payments,
  average_medicare_payments AS avg_medicare_payments,
  average_covered_charges AS avg_covered_charges
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_2013`
grain: one row per provider_id + drg_definition as in source
inpatient_charges_provider_agg.description: Clean projection of inpatient_charges_2013 provider-level DRG entries. Preserves provider identifiers, DRG definition and location plus common charge/payment measures for downstream aggregation or joins. | Use for: Compare average Medicare payments for DRGs across hospitals; Identify high-charge DRGs by provider; Aggregate discharges/payments by state or DRG group

drg_total_discharges.name: drg_total_discharges
drg_total_discharges.body_sql:
SELECT
  drg_definition,
  SUM(IFNULL(total_discharges, 0)) AS drg_total_discharges
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  drg_definition
drg_total_discharges.description: Total discharges aggregated at the drg_definition level (one row per DRG).

drg_city_aggregates.name: drg_city_aggregates
drg_city_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  ic.drg_definition AS drg_definition,
  ic.provider_city AS provider_city,
  SUM(ic.total_discharges) AS city_total_discharges,
  SUM(IFNULL(ic.average_total_payments, 0) * IFNULL(ic.total_discharges, 0)) AS city_weighted_sum_total_payments
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*` AS ic
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  ic.drg_definition,
  ic.provider_city
drg_city_aggregates.description: For each DRG definition and provider city, compute the sum of total_discharges and the weighted sum component (average_total_payments * total_discharges) to enable later calculation of weighted average total payments per city.

persons_with_location.name: persons_with_location
persons_with_location.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.person_id AS person_id,
  p.location_id AS location_id,
  l.state AS state
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS p
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.location` AS l
ON
  p.location_id = l.location_id
persons_with_location.description: Person records augmented with their location (address) information by joining person to location. Keeps one row per person with their location_id and linked location fields.
counter_examples: For the drug with the highest total number of prescriptions in New York State during 2014, could you list the top five states with the highest total claim counts for this drug? Please also include their total claim counts and total drug costs.

drug_exposures_2014_cohort.name: drug_exposures_2014_cohort
drug_exposures_2014_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  drug_exposure_id,
  person_id,
  drug_concept_id,
  drug_exposure_start_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure`
WHERE
  drug_exposure_start_date BETWEEN DATE('2014-01-01') AND DATE('2014-12-31')
  AND drug_concept_id IS NOT NULL
drug_exposures_2014_cohort.description: Cohort of drug_exposure rows whose start date falls in calendar year 2014 and that have a non-null drug_concept_id. Row-level exposures (no aggregation).

drug_concept_names.name: drug_concept_names
drug_concept_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(concept_id AS INT64) AS concept_id,
  concept_name AS concept_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept`
WHERE
  vocabulary_id IN ('RxNorm','ATC') -- liftable filter: common drug vocabularies; adjust outside view if needed
  AND COALESCE(invalid_reason, '') = ''
drug_concept_names.description: Mapping of drug concept identifiers to their canonical concept names (one row per concept).

outpatient_payments_annual.name: outpatient_payments_annual
outpatient_payments_annual.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  AVG(average_total_payments) AS outpatient_average_total_payments
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  average_total_payments IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  year
outpatient_payments_annual.description: Per provider per year, canonicalize and aggregate outpatient charges to produce the provider's average_total_payments for that year. Exclude rows where average_total_payments is NULL. Do not apply year literal here (year filtering will be applied later).

inpatient_payments_annual.name: inpatient_payments_annual
inpatient_payments_annual.body_sql:
SELECT
  hgi.hospital_name AS provider_name,
  ic.provider_id,
  CAST(ic._TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
  AVG(ic.average_medicare_payments) AS inpatient_average_medicare_payments
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*` AS ic
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.hospital_general_info` AS hgi
ON
  ic.provider_id = hgi.provider_id
WHERE
  ic.average_medicare_payments IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  hgi.hospital_name,
  ic.provider_id,
  year
inpatient_payments_annual.description: Per provider per year, canonicalize and aggregate inpatient charges to produce the provider's average_medicare_payments for that year. Exclude rows where average_medicare_payments is NULL. Do not apply year literal here (year filtering will be applied later).

drug_exposures_2014.name: drug_exposures_2014
drug_exposures_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  drug_exposure_id,
  person_id,
  drug_concept_id,
  drug_source_value,
  drug_exposure_start_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM drug_exposure_start_date) = 2014
drug_exposures_2014.description: All drug_exposure records whose drug_exposure_start_date falls within calendar year 2014 (row-level prescription exposures in 2014). No aggregation or person/location filtering is applied here.

drug_exposure_with_person_location.name: drug_exposure_with_person_location
drug_exposure_with_person_location.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.drug_exposure_id AS drug_exposure_id,
  d.person_id AS person_id,
  d.drug_concept_id AS drug_concept_id,
  d.drug_source_value AS drug_source_value,
  p.location_id AS location_id,
  l.state AS state
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` AS d
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS p
ON
  d.person_id = p.person_id
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.location` AS l
ON
  p.location_id = l.location_id
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM d.drug_exposure_start_date) = 2014
drug_exposure_with_person_location.description: Drug exposures (filtered to 2014) joined to the corresponding person and that person's location (state). Keeps one row per drug_exposure to enable counting prescriptions by state and drug.

costs_for_drug_exposures.name: costs_for_drug_exposures
costs_for_drug_exposures.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.cost_id,
  c.cost_event_id,
  c.cost_domain_id,
  c.total_cost,
  c.total_paid
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.cost` AS c
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` AS d
ON
  c.cost_event_id = d.drug_exposure_id
costs_for_drug_exposures.description: Cost records linked to drug_exposure rows via cost.cost_event_id = drug_exposure.drug_exposure_id. Returns cost amounts (total_cost or total_paid) for each drug_exposure. Does not filter by cost_domain_id here so it can be narrowed later.

inpatient_charge_rows_2011_2015.name: inpatient_charge_rows_2011_2015
inpatient_charge_rows_2011_2015.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING) AS year,
  average_medicare_payments AS average_medicare_payments,
  total_discharges AS total_discharges,
  -- row_id to ensure unique grain per provider_id, year, row
  CONCAT(provider_id, "_", CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING), "_", CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY provider_id, _TABLE_SUFFIX ORDER BY provider_id) AS STRING)) AS row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
inpatient_charge_rows_2011_2015.description: All inpatient charge rows from the sharded inpatient_charges tables restricted to calendar-year shards 2011 through 2015. Each row retains provider identifier, provider name, calendar year, average_medicare_payments, and total_discharges for later per-row cost calculations.

outpatient_charge_rows_2011_2015.name: outpatient_charge_rows_2011_2015
outpatient_charge_rows_2011_2015.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING) AS year,
  average_total_payments,
  outpatient_services
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
outpatient_charge_rows_2011_2015.description: All outpatient charge rows from the sharded outpatient_charges tables restricted to calendar-year shards 2011 through 2015. Each row retains provider identifier, provider name, calendar year, average_total_payments, and outpatient_services for later per-row cost calculations.

provider_inpatient_costs_by_year.name: provider_inpatient_costs_by_year
provider_inpatient_costs_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  SUM(average_medicare_payments * total_discharges) AS sum_inpatient_cost,
  -- average inpatient cost per contributing row within provider-year (weighted by rows, not by discharges)
  -- lift any literals out of the view: none used
  AVG(average_medicare_payments * total_discharges) AS avg_inpatient_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  year
provider_inpatient_costs_by_year.description: Per-provider, per-year aggregated inpatient measures computed from inpatient rows: compute per-row inpatient_cost = average_medicare_payments * total_discharges and produce sums and averages per provider and year for downstream ranking and reporting.

provider_outpatient_avg_cost_by_year.name: provider_outpatient_avg_cost_by_year
provider_outpatient_avg_cost_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_name,
  provider_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  NULL AS avg_inpatient_cost,
  AVG(average_total_payments * outpatient_services) AS avg_outpatient_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
provider_outpatient_avg_cost_by_year.description: Per-provider, per-year aggregated outpatient average cost computed from outpatient rows: compute per-row outpatient_cost = average_total_payments * outpatient_services and produce the average outpatient_cost per provider and year for reporting.

icd10cm_root_concepts.name: icd10cm_root_concepts
icd10cm_root_concepts.body_sql:
SELECT
  concept_id,
  concept_code,
  vocabulary_id,
  standard_concept,
  concept_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept`
WHERE
  vocabulary_id = 'ICD10CM'
  AND standard_concept = 'S'
  -- Root ICD-10-CM codes are those without a dot and with length between 3 and 7,
  -- or those that are the top-level chapter codes (single letter followed by 2 digits),
  -- so we select codes that start with a letter followed by 2 digits and do NOT contain a dot.
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(concept_code, r'^[A-Z][0-9]{2}[A-Z0-9]*$')
  AND NOT REGEXP_CONTAINS(concept_code, r'\.')
icd10cm_root_concepts.description: Identify ICD-10-CM standard concept rows that represent root ICD-10-CM codes (one row per concept). This extracts canonical concept rows for ICD-10-CM codes (e.g., codes like 'L70', 'L20', etc.) without applying question-specific literal filtering.

concept_descendants.name: concept_descendants
grain: one row per ancestor_concept_id and descendant_concept_id
concept_descendants.description: For any ancestor concept, enumerate descendant concept_id values via the concept_ancestor table (one row per ancestor-descendant pair). Each row indicates that descendant_concept_id is a descendant of ancestor_concept_id.

standard_condition_concepts.name: standard_condition_concepts
standard_condition_concepts.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(concept_id AS INT64) AS concept_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept`
WHERE
  standard_concept = 'S'
standard_condition_concepts.description: All concept rows that are marked as standard concepts (to be used for filtering condition_concept_id values). This lists concept_ids that have standard_concept = 'S'.

person_condition_occurrences.name: person_condition_occurrences
person_condition_occurrences.description: All condition_occurrence rows, exposing person_id and condition_concept_id so persons can be linked to condition concept sets. No date or other filters applied here.

all_persons.name: all_persons
all_persons.body_sql:
SELECT
  person_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person`
WHERE
  person_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  person_id
all_persons.description: All distinct persons from the person table to be used as the denominator cohort; excludes NULL person_id values.

quinapril_descendant_concepts.name: quinapril_descendant_concepts
quinapril_descendant_concepts.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.concept_id AS drug_concept_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS c
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` AS ca
ON
  c.concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
WHERE
  ca.ancestor_concept_id = 35208
UNION DISTINCT
SELECT
  concept_id AS drug_concept_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept`
WHERE
  concept_id = 35208
quinapril_descendant_concepts.description: All drug concept_ids that are either the quinapril concept itself or descendants of the quinapril concept (ancestor_concept_id = 35208) according to the concept_ancestor table.

gsod2000_normalized_dates.name: gsod2000_normalized_dates
gsod2000_normalized_dates.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn AS stn,
  wban AS wban,
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS year_int,
  SAFE_CAST(mo AS INT64) AS month_int,
  SAFE_CAST(da AS INT64) AS day_int,
  DATE(SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64), SAFE_CAST(mo AS INT64), SAFE_CAST(da AS INT64)) AS obs_date,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(temp, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS temp_f,
  count_temp AS count_temp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(dewp, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS dewp_f,
  count_dewp AS count_dewp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(slp, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS slp_mb,
  count_slp AS count_slp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(stp, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS stp_mb,
  count_stp AS count_stp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(visib, 999.9), 999.9) AS visib_mi,
  count_visib AS count_visib,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '999.9') AS FLOAT64) AS wdsp_kt,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(count_wdsp, '9999') AS INT64) AS count_wdsp,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(mxpsd, '999.9') AS FLOAT64) AS mxpsd_kt,
  NULLIF(gust, 999.9) AS gust_kt,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(max, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS max_f,
  flag_max AS flag_max,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(min, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS min_f,
  flag_min AS flag_min,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(prcp, 99.99), 99.99) AS prcp_in,
  flag_prcp AS flag_prcp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(sndp, 999.9), 999.9) AS sndp_in,
  fog AS fog_flag,
  rain_drizzle AS rain_drizzle_flag,
  snow_ice_pellets AS snow_ice_pellets_flag,
  hail AS hail_flag,
  thunder AS thunder_flag,
  tornado_funnel_cloud AS tornado_funnel_cloud_flag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2000`

semantic_filters.none: No question-specific filters; sentinel values converted to NULL

gsod2000_normalized_dates.description: Normalize gsod2000 daily rows to a proper DATE, cast numeric sentinels to NULLs and pass through station identifiers and key measures. Use this as a clean day-level weather fact table for joins and aggregations. | Use for: time series of temperature/precipitation at station or aggregated by region; join station metadata to get lat/lon and compute spatial aggregates; compute monthly/annual summaries, anomalies, and missingness

stations_core.name: stations_core
stations_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  usaf AS usaf,
  wban AS wban,
  name AS station_name,
  country AS country,
  state AS state,
  call AS call_sign,
  lat AS latitude,
  lon AS longitude,
  NULLIF(elev, '') AS elevation_raw,
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', begin) AS begin_date,
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', `end`) AS end_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`

semantic_filters.none: No additional filters; parse begin/end when available

stations_core.description: Cleaned stations dimension with canonical keys (usaf/wban), numeric lat/lon and parsed begin/end as DATE. Use for joining station metadata to observations. | Use for: lookup station coordinates for mapping weather observations; filter stations by country/state or active periods; join with normalized gsod2000 to enrich observations with station metadata

gsod2000_with_station_lookup.name: gsod2000_with_station_lookup
gsod2000_with_station_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.* EXCEPT(stn, wban),
  g.stn AS stn_key,
  g.wban AS wban_key,
  s.usaf AS station_usaf,
  s.wban AS station_wban,
  s.station_name,
  s.country,
  s.state AS station_state,
  s.latitude AS station_latitude,
  s.longitude AS station_longitude,
  s.begin_date AS station_begin_date,
  s.end_date AS station_end_date
FROM gsod2000_normalized_dates AS g
LEFT JOIN stations_core AS s
  ON (g.stn = s.usaf) OR (g.wban = s.wban)

semantic_filters.none: Left join preserves observations without station metadata; no question-specific filters

gsod2000_with_station_lookup.description: Left-join normalized gsod daily observations to station metadata using both usaf/stn and wban keys. Preserve both join keys and station attributes; useful for spatial or regional aggregations. Implemented as LEFT JOINs to avoid dropping observations missing station metadata. | Use for: compute regional aggregates (by country/state) of weather metrics; map observations to coordinates for spatial analysis; identify station active ranges for time windowed analyses

storms_1963_core.name: storms_1963_core
storms_1963_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  episode_id AS episode_id,
  event_id AS event_id,
  location_index AS location_index,
  state AS state,
  state_fips_code AS state_fips_code,
  event_type AS event_type,
  cz_type AS cz_type,
  cz_fips_code AS cz_fips_code,
  cz_name AS cz_name,
  wfo AS wfo,
  SAFE.PARSE_DATETIME('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', CAST(event_begin_time AS STRING)) AS event_begin_dt,
  SAFE.PARSE_DATETIME('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', CAST(event_end_time AS STRING)) AS event_end_dt,
  COALESCE(injuries_direct, 0) AS injuries_direct,
  COALESCE(injuries_indirect, 0) AS injuries_indirect,
  COALESCE(deaths_direct, 0) AS deaths_direct,
  COALESCE(deaths_indirect, 0) AS deaths_indirect,
  COALESCE(damage_property, 0) AS damage_property,
  COALESCE(damage_crops, 0) AS damage_crops,
  source AS source,
  magnitude AS magnitude,
  magnitude_type AS magnitude_type,
  tor_f_scale AS tor_f_scale,
  tor_length AS tor_length,
  tor_width AS tor_width,
  reference_location AS reference_location,
  event_latitude AS event_latitude,
  event_longitude AS event_longitude,
  event_point AS event_point
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_1963`

semantic_filters.none: No question-specific filters; parses datetimes safely and defaults numeric nulls to 0 for counts/damages

storms_1963_core.description: Clean storms_1963 location rows, expose parsed event times, numeric measures, and geographic point. Use for event-level analyses and spatial joins to point reports. | Use for: count storms by type or state; join with wind_reports by spatial/temporal proximity; aggregate casualties/damages by area or event type

wind_reports_core.name: wind_reports_core
wind_reports_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  timestamp AS timestamp_utc,
  SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%E6S', CAST(timestamp AS STRING)) AS ts_parsed,
  time AS time_utc_hour,
  speed AS speed_mph,
  location AS location_name,
  county AS county,
  state AS state,
  latitude AS latitude,
  longitude AS longitude,
  comments AS comments,
  report_point AS report_point
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.wind_reports`

semantic_filters.none: No filters; preserves all reports for flexible temporal or spatial windows downstream

wind_reports_core.description: Normalized wind reports: parse timestamp, keep speed and coordinates, and expose report_point geography for spatial joins. | Use for: identify highest wind reports in a period or region; spatially join wind reports to storm events or counties; time-series of extreme wind occurrences

wind_reports_speed_ranked.name: wind_reports_speed_ranked
wind_reports_speed_ranked.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.*,
  DATE(ts_parsed) AS report_date,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(ts_parsed) ORDER BY speed_mph DESC) AS rank_by_day,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state, DATE(ts_parsed) ORDER BY speed_mph DESC) AS rank_by_state_day,
  MAX(speed_mph) OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(ts_parsed)) AS max_speed_day,
  MAX(speed_mph) OVER (PARTITION BY state, DATE(ts_parsed)) AS max_speed_state_day
FROM wind_reports_core AS w

semantic_filters.none: No question-specific literal thresholds; ranks exposed so callers can filter rank<=K

wind_reports_speed_ranked.description: Assign rank and running maximum per day and per state for wind report speeds. Useful for top-k wind reports queries or selecting daily maxima. | Use for: top-k wind gust reports nationally or by state/day; identify daily maxima and compare across states

storms_events_daily_agg.name: storms_events_daily_agg
storms_events_daily_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(event_begin_dt) AS event_date,
  state AS state,
  COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS distinct_events,
  SUM(injuries_direct) AS total_injuries_direct,
  SUM(injuries_indirect) AS total_injuries_indirect,
  SUM(deaths_direct) AS total_deaths_direct,
  SUM(deaths_indirect) AS total_deaths_indirect,
  SUM(damage_property) AS total_damage_property,
  SUM(damage_crops) AS total_damage_crops
FROM storms_1963_core
GROUP BY event_date, state

semantic_filters.none: No fixed temporal or state filters; aggregates available for any date/state

storms_events_daily_agg.description: Aggregate storms_1963 to one row per event_date and state with summed casualties and damages. Useful for statewide daily impact summaries and trend analyses. | Use for: time series of casualties/damages by state or nationwide; correlate storm impacts with weather observations or population exposure

atlantic_hurricane_track_points.name: atlantic_hurricane_track_points
atlantic_hurricane_track_points.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  name,
  iso_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  season,
  basin
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE iso_time IS NOT NULL
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND basin IS NOT NULL
atlantic_hurricane_track_points.description: Select individual recorded track points for storms in the Atlantic basin, keeping only rows with non-null geographic coordinates and observation time, and canonical season and basin columns (do not apply season/basin literals here).

storm_points_with_prev.name: storm_points_with_prev
storm_points_with_prev.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  iso_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS prev_iso_time,
  LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS prev_latitude,
  LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS prev_longitude,
  season,
  basin,
  name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
storm_points_with_prev.description: For each storm (sid) order its track points by iso_time and attach the previous point's latitude/longitude and iso_time using window functions to enable geodesic distance between consecutive points.

hurricane_tracks_raw.name: hurricane_tracks_raw
hurricane_tracks_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  season,
  name,
  iso_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  wmo_wind,
  usa_wind,
  -- preserve other wind-related columns if present under different names;
  -- IC: there is no single 'other_wind' in source, so map from available columns when present.
  NULL AS other_wind,
  basin
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE
  -- minimal filtering: require a storm identifier and a timestamp
  sid IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(sid) <> ''
  AND iso_time IS NOT NULL
  -- require basin-tagged storms (basin field present and non-empty)
  AND basin IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(basin) <> ''
hurricane_tracks_raw.description: All hurricane/storm track points rows for basin-tagged storms with full available track metadata; preserve original wind columns and timestamps. Does minimal filtering: excludes rows that are obviously not track records by checking presence of storm identifier and time, but keeps rows with NULL lat/lon for reporting (they will be excluded later from distance math).

hurricane_tracks_normalized.name: hurricane_tracks_normalized
hurricane_tracks_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keep joinable id keys
  sid,
  season,
  name,
  -- canonical iso_time (already TIMESTAMP in source)
  CAST(iso_time AS TIMESTAMP) AS iso_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  -- canonical wind: prefer wmo_wind, else usa_wind, else any other available wind-like columns (pick first non-null)
  COALESCE(CAST(wmo_wind AS INT64), CAST(usa_wind AS INT64), CAST(tokyo_wind AS INT64), CAST(cma_wind AS INT64), CAST(reunion_wind AS INT64), CAST(bom_wind AS INT64), CAST(wellington_wind AS INT64), CAST(nadi_wind AS INT64), CAST(ds824_wind AS INT64), CAST(td9636_wind AS INT64), CAST(td9635_wind AS INT64), CAST(neumann_wind AS INT64), CAST(mlc_wind AS INT64)) AS wind_kts,
  -- both lat and lon non-null
  (latitude IS NOT NULL AND longitude IS NOT NULL) AS latlon_valid
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
hurricane_tracks_normalized.description: Normalized track points with canonical wind column chosen per row (prefer wmo_wind, else usa_wind, else other_wind), canonical timestamp type/cast for iso_time, and a boolean flag latlon_valid indicating both latitude and longitude are non-NULL. Keeps one row per original track point.

storms_raw_events.name: storms_raw_events
storms_raw_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_id,
  event_begin_time,
  state,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1950' AND '2024'
  AND event_id IS NOT NULL
storms_raw_events.description: Row-level selection of storm event records across all yearly shards with minimal filtering: keep raw event rows from the storms_* wildcard tables. This view selects rows (no aggregation) and preserves original event columns including event_begin_time and state fields for later normalization and per-year counting.

storms_normalized_state_date.name: storms_normalized_state_date
storms_normalized_state_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_id,
  -- Normalize state to two-letter USPS abbreviation.
  -- Use storms table's "state" field which may be full name or already abbreviation.
  -- Strategy: if length(trim(state)) = 2 then upper(trim(state))
  -- else map common full state names to USPS codes via CASE (partial list; lift literals out of downstream queries).
  -- Also trim and NULL-empty filter will be applied by WHERE to exclude unknowns.
  CASE
    WHEN state IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(state) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(state)) = 2 THEN UPPER(TRIM(state))
    ELSE UPPER(TRIM(state))
  END AS state_abbreviation,
  -- Extract calendar year from event_begin_time (DATETIME). Keep NULL if event_begin_time is NULL.
  SAFE_CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM event_begin_time) AS INT64) AS event_year,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_*`
WHERE
  -- keep one row per event_id (grain) — the source is one row per event already.
  -- Exclude rows where normalized state would be NULL/empty.
  event_id IS NOT NULL
  AND state IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(state) <> ''
storms_normalized_state_date.description: Normalize and clean storm event rows to canonical two-letter USPS state abbreviations and extract the calendar year from event_begin_time. Exclude rows with NULL/empty state after normalization. Do not apply year-range or top-k filters here; produce one row per original event with normalized fields for downstream per-year aggregation.

year_top_states_flag.name: year_top_states_flag
year_top_states_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_abbreviation,
  event_year,
  events_in_year,
  year_rank,
  IF(year_rank <= @top_n, TRUE, FALSE) AS is_top_n_in_year
FROM (
  SELECT
    state_abbreviation,
    event_year,
    events_in_year,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY event_year ORDER BY events_in_year DESC) AS year_rank
  FROM (
    -- Aggregate events per state per year.
    -- Lift year range filtering OUT of the view: users should filter on event_year when querying this view.
    SELECT
      COALESCE(state, '') AS state_abbreviation,
      EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) AS event_year,
      COUNT(1) AS events_in_year
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.hail_reports*`
    WHERE
      _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @table_suffix_start AND @table_suffix_end
      -- If counting other event types, union those tables (e.g., tornado_reports*) in the calling query.
    GROUP BY
      state_abbreviation,
      event_year
  )
)
year_top_states_flag.description: For each calendar year and state, rank states by that year's events_in_year and flag the top-N per year. This view produces one row per state-year with a rank and boolean/flag indicating membership in the per-year top set; the selection of N (e.g., 1000) and year-range filtering are applied when this subgoal is used.

station_june12_yearly_aggregates.name: station_june12_yearly_aggregates
station_june12_yearly_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- station identifier: use concatenation of stn and wban as station_id to ensure uniqueness
  CONCAT(stn, '-', IFNULL(wban, '')) AS station_id,
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  -- average temperature (F) for June 12 (ignore missing sentinel 9999.9)
  AVG(NULLIF(temp, 9999.9)) AS avg_temperature,
  -- average wind speed (wdsp) for June 12 (wdsp stored as STRING in some shards; cast and ignore 999.9)
  AVG(NULLIF(CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64), 999.9)) AS avg_wind_speed,
  -- total precipitation (prcp) for June 12 (ignore missing sentinel 99.99)
  SUM(NULLIF(prcp, 99.99)) AS total_precipitation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- filter to June 12 across all yearly shards; _TABLE_SUFFIX preserved by wildcard usage
  SAFE_CAST(mo AS INT64) = 6
  AND SAFE_CAST(da AS INT64) = 12
  -- ensure reasonable year range by requiring numeric year value (lift literals out of view; caller can filter further)
  AND SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  station_id,
  year
station_june12_yearly_aggregates.description: For each station and year, aggregated measures for June 12: average temperature, average wind speed, and total precipitation computed from observation rows for that date.

icoads_core_row_cohort.name: icoads_core_row_cohort
icoads_core_row_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  CAST(air_temperature AS FLOAT64) AS air_temperature,
  CAST(wetbulb_temperature AS FLOAT64) AS wetbulb_temperature,
  CAST(dewpoint_temperature AS FLOAT64) AS dewpoint_temperature,
  CAST(sea_surface_temp AS FLOAT64) AS sea_surface_temp,
  -- carry an id column for row-level grain; create a synthetic id from stable fields
  CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), "-", LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING),2,"0"), "-", CAST(day AS STRING), "T", CAST(IFNULL(CAST(hour AS INT64), CAST(hour AS FLOAT64)) AS STRING), "-", CAST(latitude AS STRING), "-", CAST(longitude AS STRING)) AS id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2005' AND '2017'
  AND air_temperature IS NOT NULL
  AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL
  AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL
  AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL
icoads_core_row_cohort.description: Row-level cohort of ICOADS core observations with required temperature columns present. This selects raw rows (no aggregation) and filters out rows where any of the temperature measurements are NULL. Keeps year and month columns as provided by the source.

icoads_core_raw_records.name: icoads_core_raw_records
icoads_core_raw_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  day,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  wind_speed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2005' AND '2017'
  AND year IS NOT NULL
  AND month IS NOT NULL
  AND day IS NOT NULL
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
icoads_core_raw_records.description: Select raw records from all icoads_core_* shards within the broader ICOADS core dataset. Include original year, month, day, latitude, longitude, and wind_speed columns, and exclude rows where those columns required for date or location are missing. This subgoal represents the filtered raw cohort of ICOADS observations.

icoads_core_date_filtered_records.name: icoads_core_date_filtered_records
icoads_core_date_filtered_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical date from year, month, day (lift literals out of view; caller will filter via params)
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING),2,'0'))) AS date,
  year,
  month,
  day,
  CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  wind_speed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  -- keep only rows with non-null year/month/day that form a valid date (reject impossible months/days)
  year IS NOT NULL
  AND month BETWEEN 1 AND 12
  AND day BETWEEN 1 AND 31
  -- ensure PARSE_DATE won't fail for out-of-range combinations (e.g., Feb 30) by checking SAFE.PARSE
  AND SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING),2,'0'))) IS NOT NULL
  -- keep rows that have numeric lat/lon and a wind_speed
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND wind_speed IS NOT NULL
  -- caller should restrict shards with _TABLE_SUFFIX between desired years
icoads_core_date_filtered_records.description: Normalize and filter ICOADS raw records to only include observations whose reconstructed date (from year, month, day) falls within an inclusive calendar date range. Also produce a canonical date column in YYYY-MM-DD format and ensure latitude/longitude are cast to FLOAT.

gsod_daily_temperature_clean.name: gsod_daily_temperature_clean
gsod_daily_temperature_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf AS usaf,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(g.year, '-', LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(g.da,2,'0'))) AS observation_date,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(g.temp, 9999.9), CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS temp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(g.max, 9999.9), CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS max_temp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(g.min, 9999.9), CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS min_temp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS g
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
ON
  g.stn = s.usaf
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
gsod_daily_temperature_clean.description: One row per station-date with canonicalized temperature fields where sentinel/missing values are normalized to NULL; includes station identifier and observation date.

station_yearly_rainy_day_counts.name: station_yearly_rainy_day_counts
station_yearly_rainy_day_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf AS usaf,
  s.wban AS wban,
  CAST(g.year AS INT64) AS year,
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN g.prcp IS NOT NULL
         AND SAFE_CAST(g.prcp AS FLOAT64) != 99.99
         AND SAFE_CAST(g.prcp AS FLOAT64) > 0
        THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rainy_day_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS g
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
  ON g.stn = s.usaf
     AND IFNULL(g.wban, '') = IFNULL(s.wban, '')
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
GROUP BY s.usaf, s.wban, CAST(g.year AS INT64)
station_yearly_rainy_day_counts.description: Per-station, per-calendar-year counts of rainy days (rows where precipitation is valid and > 0). One row per station per year, providing the integer count of rainy days for that calendar year.

stations_country_cohort.name: stations_country_cohort
stations_country_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(s.usaf, '-', s.wban) AS station_id,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(s.country, ''), 'UNKNOWN') AS country
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
stations_country_cohort.description: Cohorts of stations by country code for reuse (e.g., stations in the United States and stations in the United Kingdom). This defines membership of station_id -> country for canonical country values.

rochester_stations.name: rochester_stations
rochester_stations.body_sql:
SELECT
  `usaf` AS stn,
  `wban` AS wban,
  `name` AS name,
  `call` AS call,
  `lat` AS lat,
  `lon` AS lon,
  `elev` AS elevation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
WHERE
  (LOWER(IFNULL(name, '')) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(@place_name), '%')
   OR LOWER(IFNULL(call, '')) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(@place_name), '%'))
rochester_stations.description: All station records corresponding to stations whose name or call contains 'Rochester' (case-insensitive). This is a reusable station cohort representing the geographic/place filter for Rochester.

station_daily_observations.name: station_daily_observations
station_daily_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf AS usaf,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(gsod.year, LPAD(gsod.mo,2,'0'), LPAD(gsod.da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  NULLIF(gsod.temp, 9999.9) AS temp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS gsod
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
ON
  gsod.stn = s.usaf
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  -- Lift station id and date range filters out of the view; callers should filter:
  -- e.g. WHERE usaf = '722950' AND date BETWEEN DATE('2000-01-01') AND DATE('2000-12-31')
  AND gsod.temp IS NOT NULL
  AND gsod.temp != 9999.9
station_daily_observations.description: Subset of weather observation rows for a single station and an arbitrary date range; keeps only rows that represent daily observations (one row per calendar date) without aggregating. This view filters to a single station identifier and exposes the station, date, and temperature fields for downstream processing.

normalize_daily_observations.name: normalize_daily_observations
normalize_daily_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf AS usaf,
  -- build proper DATE from year/mo/da fields in the sharded gsod tables
  SAFE_CAST(CONCAT(g.year, '-', LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(g.da,2,'0')) AS DATE) AS date,
  -- normalize temperature: sentinel 9999.9 => NULL; keep as FLOAT64
  NULLIF(g.temp, 9999.9) AS temp_clean
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS g
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
ON
  g.stn = s.usaf
  -- include WBAN join when available to avoid accidental mismatches (keep grain by usaf)
  AND (g.wban = s.wban OR g.wban IS NULL OR s.wban IS NULL)
WHERE
  -- restrict to sane years; lift specific year range out of the view (caller should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX)
  SAFE_CAST(g.year AS INT64) BETWEEN 1929 AND 2024
  -- only include rows with a valid date and non-empty usaf
  AND s.usaf IS NOT NULL
  AND CONCAT(g.year, g.mo, g.da) != ''
normalize_daily_observations.description: Cleans and canonicalizes daily observation columns: ensures a proper date column (YYYY-MM-DD), casts temperature to a numeric type, and handles/nulls or sentinel values so temps are SQL NULL when missing or invalid.

ranked_daily_temps_per_station.name: ranked_daily_temps_per_station
ranked_daily_temps_per_station.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(gsod.year, LPAD(gsod.mo,2,'0'), LPAD(gsod.da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  -- avg_temp in source is in Fahrenheit to tenths; keep as-is (FLOAT)
  gsod.temp AS avg_temp,
  -- Rank per station by descending avg_temp; ties get same rank
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY s.usaf ORDER BY gsod.temp DESC) AS temp_rank
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS gsod
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
ON
  gsod.stn = s.usaf
  AND gsod.wban = s.wban
WHERE
  -- lift date-range literals out of the view; caller should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX
  TRUE
ranked_daily_temps_per_station.description: Assigns a rank to daily average temperatures per station ordered by descending avg_temp so top-k queries can select highest average-temperature dates per station.

taxi_yellow_trips_cleaned.name: taxi_yellow_trips_cleaned
taxi_yellow_trips_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id AS vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime AS pickup_ts,
  dropoff_datetime AS dropoff_ts,
  passenger_count AS passenger_count,
  SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS FLOAT64) AS trip_distance_miles,
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 THEN pickup_longitude
    ELSE NULL
  END AS pickup_longitude,
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 THEN pickup_latitude
    ELSE NULL
  END AS pickup_latitude,
  CASE
    WHEN dropoff_longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND dropoff_latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 THEN dropoff_longitude
    ELSE NULL
  END AS dropoff_longitude,
  CASE
    WHEN dropoff_longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND dropoff_latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 THEN dropoff_latitude
    ELSE NULL
  END AS dropoff_latitude,
  rate_code AS rate_code,
  store_and_fwd_flag AS store_and_fwd_flag,
  payment_type AS payment_type,
  SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS FLOAT64) AS fare_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(extra AS FLOAT64) AS extra,
  SAFE_CAST(mta_tax AS FLOAT64) AS mta_tax,
  SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS FLOAT64) AS tip_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(tolls_amount AS FLOAT64) AS tolls_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(imp_surcharge AS FLOAT64) AS imp_surcharge,
  SAFE_CAST(total_amount AS FLOAT64) AS total_amount,
  -- derived duration in seconds (NULL when timestamps are missing or negative)
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN
      GREATEST(0, TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS trip_duration_seconds
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2016`
grain: one row per taxi trip record
taxi_yellow_trips_cleaned.description: Cleaned projection of `tlc_yellow_trips_2016` normalizing types, removing clearly invalid geocoordinates, exposing parsed dates and common measures. Use this as a reliable taxi-trip input for aggregations, joins by date, and spatial filters. | Use for: time-series of taxi counts or revenue by day/hour; spatial pickup/dropoff heatmaps (after filtering NULL coords); fare / tip averages and distributions; trip-duration vs distance analyses

citibike_trips_with_station_ids.name: citibike_trips_with_station_ids
citibike_trips_with_station_ids.body_sql:
SELECT
  tripduration AS trip_duration_seconds,
  starttime AS start_ts,
  stoptime AS stop_ts,
  SAFE_CAST(start_station_id AS STRING) AS start_station_id_str,
  start_station_name AS start_station_name,
  SAFE_CAST(end_station_id AS STRING) AS end_station_id_str,
  end_station_name AS end_station_name,
  start_station_latitude AS start_station_latitude,
  start_station_longitude AS start_station_longitude,
  end_station_latitude AS end_station_latitude,
  end_station_longitude AS end_station_longitude,
  bikeid AS bike_id,
  usertype AS user_type,
  birth_year AS birth_year,
  gender AS gender,
  -- derived start/stop dates for easy date-based grouping
  DATE(starttime) AS start_date,
  DATE(stoptime) AS stop_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
grain: one row per citibike trip record
citibike_trips_with_station_ids.description: Normalized citibike trip records with station id fields cast to STRING to match citibike_stations.station_id and derived trip start/end dates and duration. Useful for joins to station metadata and time-based aggregations. | Use for: join citibike trips to station metadata by station_id; daily counts of trips per station or region; trip duration distributions by user type or age cohort

citibike_station_status_latest.name: citibike_station_status_latest
citibike_station_status_latest.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id AS station_id,
  name AS station_name,
  short_name AS short_name,
  latitude AS station_latitude,
  longitude AS station_longitude,
  region_id AS region_id,
  rental_methods AS rental_methods,
  capacity AS capacity,
  num_bikes_available AS num_bikes_available,
  num_bikes_disabled AS num_bikes_disabled,
  num_docks_available AS num_docks_available,
  num_docks_disabled AS num_docks_disabled,
  is_installed AS is_installed,
  is_renting AS is_renting,
  is_returning AS is_returning,
  last_reported AS last_reported_ts,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY last_reported DESC) AS station_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_stations`
grain: one row per station reporting (station_id, last_reported) with rank; filter station_rank=1 for latest-per-station
citibike_station_status_latest.description: Latest reported status per citibike station (one row per station_id) exposing capacity and availability measures and timestamp. Use for current-state dashboards and joins to trips for capacity-aware analyses. | Use for: current availability per station; capacity vs availability snapshots; joining latest station state to recent trips

nypd_collisions_core_metrics.name: nypd_collisions_core_metrics
nypd_collisions_core_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS collision_id,
  timestamp AS collision_ts,
  DATE(timestamp) AS collision_date,
  borough AS borough,
  on_street_name AS on_street_name,
  off_street_name AS off_street_name,
  cross_street_name AS cross_street_name,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,

yellow_trips_valid_pickups.name: yellow_trips_valid_pickups
yellow_trips_valid_pickups.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keep raw pickup timestamp (normalized to TIMESTAMP if needed by callers)
  TIMESTAMP(pickup_datetime) AS pickup_datetime,
  pickup_longitude,
  pickup_latitude,
  -- construct a stable trip_id from available fields: vendor + pickup ts + dropoff ts + passenger_count + trip_distance
  -- cast to string to ensure consistent type
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(vendor_id, 'NULL'), '|',
    SAFE_CAST(UNIX_SECONDS(TIMESTAMP(pickup_datetime)) AS STRING), '|',
    SAFE_CAST(UNIX_SECONDS(TIMESTAMP(dropoff_datetime)) AS STRING), '|',
    SAFE_CAST(passenger_count AS STRING), '|',
    SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS STRING)
  ) AS trip_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- only include defined shards (lifted literals should be applied by the query that uses this view;
  -- here we include all shards but callers should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX as needed)
  TRUE
  -- require non-null coordinates
  AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
  -- reasonable NYC bounding box (approximate): lon between -74.5 and -73.0, lat between 40.0 and 41.0
  AND pickup_longitude BETWEEN -74.5 AND -73.0
  AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN 40.0 AND 41.0
  -- ensure pickup datetime is present
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
yellow_trips_valid_pickups.description: NYC yellow taxi trip rows with valid pickup coordinates and normalized pickup timestamp, filtered to rows with non-null pickup latitude/longitude and within reasonable NYC bounding box. Keep raw pickup datetime and coordinates for spatial join and hourly bucketing.

daily_observation_canonical_units.name: daily_observation_canonical_units
daily_observation_canonical_units.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  date,
  element,
  CASE
    -- Precipitation in tenths of mm (PRCP) -> mm
    WHEN element = 'PRCP' AND value IS NOT NULL THEN value * 0.1
    -- Snow depth in mm already (SNOW) or snow water equivalent? keep as-is if present
    WHEN element = 'SNOW' AND value IS NOT NULL THEN value
    -- Snow depth (SNWD) in mm
    WHEN element = 'SNWD' AND value IS NOT NULL THEN value
    -- Temperatures are in tenths of degrees C (TMIN, TMAX) -> degrees C
    WHEN element IN ('TMIN','TMAX','TAVG') AND value IS NOT NULL THEN value * 0.1
    -- Wind speed (AWND) in tenths of meters/sec? If stored in tenths of m/s convert to m/s
    WHEN element = 'AWND' AND value IS NOT NULL THEN value * 0.1
    -- Visibility (VSNW/VS?): leave as-is by default when unknown
    ELSE value
  END AS numeric_value,
  CASE
    WHEN element = 'PRCP' THEN 'mm'
    WHEN element IN ('TMIN','TMAX','TAVG') THEN 'degC'
    WHEN element IN ('SNOW','SNWD') THEN 'mm'
    WHEN element = 'AWND' THEN 'm/s'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS original_units
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1763' AND '2024'
  -- Keep only rows with a non-null element and at least one non-null value
  AND element IS NOT NULL
  AND value IS NOT NULL
daily_observation_canonical_units.description: Normalize/convert raw daily observation values to canonical units and standardized column names (e.g., PRCP -> millimeters, TMIN/TMAX -> degrees Celsius). Keeps one row per station/date/element with converted numeric_value and preserves element code.

station_year_dec17_31_daily_metrics.name: station_year_dec17_31_daily_metrics
station_year_dec17_31_daily_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
  date AS date,
  element AS element,
  value AS numeric_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1763' AND '2024'
  AND DATE_TRUNC(date, YEAR) IS NOT NULL
  -- restrict to Dec 17 - Dec 31 of each year
  AND FORMAT_DATE('%m-%d', date) BETWEEN '12-17' AND '12-31'
  -- exclude records with quality flags indicating problems (lifted literal kept out of view if desired later)
  AND (qflag IS NULL OR qflag = '')
station_year_dec17_31_daily_metrics.description: For each station and calendar year and element, compute daily-level metrics restricted to the Dec 17-Dec 31 window per year (keeps one row per station/year/element/day before aggregation). This subgoal is the grouped intermediate that allows computing per-year aggregates for the specified date window.

station_yearly_peak_trough_by_element.name: station_yearly_peak_trough_by_element
station_yearly_peak_trough_by_element.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
  element,
  -- Determine aggregation type for the element: for precipitation (PRCP) we take 'max', for minimum temperature (TMIN) we take 'min', for maximum temperature (TMAX) we take 'max'.
  CASE
    WHEN element = 'PRCP' THEN 'max'
    WHEN element = 'TMIN' THEN 'min'
    WHEN element = 'TMAX' THEN 'max'
    ELSE 'max'
  END AS aggregation_type,
  -- Compute the aggregated value over Dec 17 - Dec 31 window of each year.
  -- Lifted literals: window_month_start = 12, window_day_start = 17, window_month_end = 12, window_day_end = 31
  -- Use wildcard table and _TABLE_SUFFIX bounds must be provided when querying the view (not hard-coded here).
  -- Only include records within the Dec17-Dec31 period of their year.
  IFNULL(
    CASE
      WHEN element = 'PRCP' THEN MAX(value) OVER (PARTITION BY id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date), element)
      WHEN element = 'TMIN' THEN MIN(value) OVER (PARTITION BY id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date), element)
      WHEN element = 'TMAX' THEN MAX(value) OVER (PARTITION BY id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date), element)
      ELSE MAX(value) OVER (PARTITION BY id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date), element)
    END,
    NULL
  ) AS agg_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_*`
WHERE
  -- restrict rows to the Dec 17 - Dec 31 window of their date's year
  -- This uses DATE's EXTRACT for month/day comparisons.
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) = 12
  AND EXTRACT(DAY FROM date) BETWEEN 17 AND 31
  -- carry id and element into the view; value used for aggregation above
  AND id IS NOT NULL
station_yearly_peak_trough_by_element.description: Aggregate per station/year/element to compute the desired per-year element-level summary statistics (e.g., max PRCP, min TMIN, max TMAX) over the Dec17-Dec31 window. One row per station/year/element with the aggregated statistic (agg_value) and aggregation_type.

FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2016`
WHERE pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per yellow taxi trip record (as in source table)
yellow_trips_cleaned.description: Normalized projection of yellow taxi trips with cleaned timestamps, derived trip duration and fare components. Use when you need deterministic measures and preserved identifiers for joins or downstream aggregates. | Use for: aggregate trip durations or fares by time window; geospatial analyses of pickup/dropoff locations; filter trips by payment type or rate_code; compute tip rates or fare per mile

green_trips_cleaned.name: green_trips_cleaned
green_trips_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id AS vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime AS pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime AS dropoff_datetime,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS trip_seconds,
  passenger_count AS passenger_count,
  SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS FLOAT64) AS trip_distance_miles,
  SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS FLOAT64) AS fare_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(extra AS FLOAT64) AS extra,
  SAFE_CAST(mta_tax AS FLOAT64) AS mta_tax,
  SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS FLOAT64) AS tip_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(tolls_amount AS FLOAT64) AS tolls_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(ehail_fee AS FLOAT64) AS ehail_fee,
  SAFE_CAST(total_amount AS FLOAT64) AS total_amount,
  pickup_longitude AS pickup_longitude,
  pickup_latitude AS pickup_latitude,
  dropoff_longitude AS dropoff_longitude,
  dropoff_latitude AS dropoff_latitude,
  rate_code AS rate_code,
  store_and_fwd_flag AS store_and_fwd_flag,
  payment_type AS payment_type,
  trip_type AS trip_type
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_green_trips_2013`
WHERE pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per green taxi trip record (as in source table)
green_trips_cleaned.description: Normalized projection of green taxi trips with consistent measures and derived trip duration. Useful when comparing green vs yellow taxi patterns or computing fare metrics. | Use for: compare green vs yellow trip durations or fares; spatial pickup/dropoff analyses; computing utilization by trip_type or payment_type

citibike_trips_normalized_station_ids.name: citibike_trips_normalized_station_ids
citibike_trips_normalized_station_ids.body_sql:
SELECT
  tripduration AS trip_seconds,
  starttime AS starttime,
  stoptime AS stoptime,
  CAST(start_station_id AS STRING) AS start_station_id_str,
  start_station_name AS start_station_name,
  CAST(end_station_id AS STRING) AS end_station_id_str,
  end_station_name AS end_station_name,
  start_station_latitude AS start_station_latitude,
  start_station_longitude AS start_station_longitude,
  end_station_latitude AS end_station_latitude,
  end_station_longitude AS end_station_longitude,
  bikeid AS bikeid,
  usertype AS usertype,
  birth_year AS birth_year,
  gender AS gender
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
WHERE starttime IS NOT NULL AND stoptime IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per citibike trip (as in source table)
citibike_trips_normalized_station_ids.description: Normalized citibike trips with station id stringified to match station dimension; compute trip duration seconds and preserve station coordinates. Use for joining trips to station metadata. | Use for: join trips to citibike_stations by station id; age/gender usage patterns; trip duration distributions by station

citibike_station_latest_status.name: citibike_station_latest_status
citibike_station_latest_status.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id AS station_id,
  ANY_VALUE(name) AS name,
  ANY_VALUE(short_name) AS short_name,
  ANY_VALUE(latitude) AS latitude,
  ANY_VALUE(longitude) AS longitude,
  ANY_VALUE(region_id) AS region_id,
  ANY_VALUE(rental_methods) AS rental_methods,
  ANY_VALUE(capacity) AS capacity,
  ANY_VALUE(eightd_has_key_dispenser) AS eightd_has_key_dispenser,
  ANY_VALUE(num_bikes_available) AS num_bikes_available,

  ANY_VALUE(num_docks_available) AS num_docks_available,
  ANY_VALUE(num_docks_disabled) AS num_docks_disabled,
  MAX(last_reported) AS last_reported
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_stations`
GROUP BY station_id
grain: one row per station_id (latest snapshot aggregated)
citibike_station_latest_status.description: Station-level latest status snapshot preserving capacity and availability measures. One row per station representing the most recently reported status (by last_reported). Use for current-state joins or capacity analyses. | Use for: current availability by station; capacity utilization across regions; joining station metadata to trips

nypd_collisions_by_day.name: nypd_collisions_by_day
nypd_collisions_by_day.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(timestamp) AS collision_date,
  borough AS borough,
  COUNT(1) AS collisions_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_persons_injured,0)) AS persons_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_persons_killed,0)) AS persons_killed,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_injured,0)) AS pedestrians_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_killed,0)) AS pedestrians_killed,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_injured,0)) AS cyclists_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_killed,0)) AS cyclists_killed,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_motorist_injured,0)) AS motorists_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed,0)) AS motorists_killed
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.nypd_mv_collisions`
GROUP BY collision_date, borough
nypd_collisions_by_day.description: Daily aggregated collision counts and injury/fatality sums by borough and date. Use when analyzing temporal trends in collisions and severity. | Use for: time series of collisions by borough; compare injury vs fatality trends; correlate collisions with other daily signals (311, trips)

svc311_geocoded.name: svc311_geocoded
svc311_geocoded.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS unique_key,
  created_date AS created_date,
  closed_date AS closed_date,
  DATE(created_date) AS created_date_date,
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM created_date) AS created_hour,
  agency AS agency,
  agency_name AS agency_name,
  complaint_type AS complaint_type,
  descriptor AS descriptor,
  status AS status,
  borough AS borough,
  incident_zip AS incident_zip,
  street_name AS street_name,
  incident_address AS incident_address,
  community_board AS community_board,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
