FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
grain: one row per 311 service request (as in source table)
svc311_geocoded.description: 311 service requests with normalized date parts and safe latitude/longitude. Use for spatial joins or time-based analyses of 311 activity. | Use for: spatial clustering of complaint types; response time (created to closed) analyses; join with collisions or trips by location/time

yellow_trips_pickup_hour_ranked.name: yellow_trips_pickup_hour_ranked
yellow_trips_pickup_hour_ranked.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id AS vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime AS pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime AS dropoff_datetime,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS trip_seconds,
  passenger_count AS passenger_count,
  trip_distance AS trip_distance_miles,
  pickup_longitude AS pickup_longitude,
  pickup_latitude AS pickup_latitude,
  rate_code AS rate_code,
  store_and_fwd_flag AS store_and_fwd_flag,
  payment_type AS payment_type,
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pickup_datetime) AS pickup_hour,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pickup_datetime) ORDER BY TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) ASC) AS hour_trip_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2016`
WHERE pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per yellow taxi trip with rank per pickup hour
yellow_trips_pickup_hour_ranked.description: Yellow trips augmented with pickup hour and a per-hour rank by trip_seconds (fastest trips get rank 1). Useful for Top-K or percentile filtering by hour. | Use for: top-k fastest/slowest trips per hour; filtering trips by rank within time buckets; hourly distribution of short trips

trees_with_species.name: trees_with_species
trees_with_species.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.recordid AS recordid,
  t.address AS address,
  t.house_number AS house_number,
  t.street AS street,
  t.borough AS borough,
  t.longitude AS longitude,
  t.latitude AS latitude,
  t.diameter AS diameter,
  t.status AS status,
  t.spc_common AS spc_common,
  t.spc_latin AS spc_latin,
  s.species_common_name AS species_common_name,
  s.species_scientific_name AS species_scientific_name,
  s.tree_size AS tree_size,
  s.growth_rate AS growth_rate
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_1995` AS t
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` AS s
  ON LOWER(TRIM(t.spc_common)) = LOWER(TRIM(s.species_common_name))
  OR LOWER(TRIM(t.spc_latin)) = LOWER(TRIM(s.species_scientific_name))
grain: one row per tree census record (as in source table)
trees_with_species.description: Tree census records left-joined to species reference to expose common and scientific names and characteristics. One row per tree census record preserved. Use for ecological or spatial analyses of tree populations. | Use for: species distribution across boroughs; diameter distributions by species; matching census records to species characteristics

station_two_minute_bins.name: station_two_minute_bins
station_two_minute_bins.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(bikeid AS STRING), "_", CAST(UNIX_SECONDS(starttime) AS STRING)) AS STRING) AS trip_id,
  start_station_id,
  end_station_id,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(2 * DIV(UNIX_SECONDS(starttime), 120)) AS start_bin_ts,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(2 * DIV(UNIX_SECONDS(stoptime), 120)) AS stop_bin_ts,
  starttime,
  stoptime
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
station_two_minute_bins.description: For each trip, compute normalized 2-minute bin timestamps for start and stop times (e.g., floor/truncate to 2-minute buckets) to enable grouping of near-simultaneous departures/arrivals. Keeps one row per trip.

tree_species_normalized.name: tree_species_normalized
tree_species_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  species_scientific_name,
  UPPER(species_scientific_name) AS species_scientific_name_up,
  fall_color
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species`
WHERE
  species_scientific_name IS NOT NULL
tree_species_normalized.description: Normalized species reference rows with canonicalized scientific name and fall color retained; exclude rows where species_scientific_name is NULL.

tree_census_shard_filtered.name: tree_census_shard_filtered
tree_census_shard_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX,
  recordid AS tree_id,
  spc_latin,
  status
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1995' AND '2015'
  AND spc_latin IS NOT NULL
  AND status = 'RETAINED'
tree_census_shard_filtered.description: Rows from the sharded tree_census tables (1995 through 2015) with species latin name present and status retained; this is the raw cohort filtered to shards of interest and non-NULL spc_latin.

tree_alive_by_species_year.name: tree_alive_by_species_year
tree_alive_by_species_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  UPPER(COALESCE(spc_latin, spc_common, species)) AS species_scientific_name_up,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX,
  COUNTIF(COALESCE(status, '') != 'Dead') AS alive_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1995' AND '2015'
GROUP BY species_scientific_name_up, _TABLE_SUFFIX
tree_alive_by_species_year.description: Count of living trees (status != 'Dead') per species scientific name (uppercased) for each year shard (identified by _TABLE_SUFFIX). Each row is one species-year count.

species_year_join_with_fall_color.name: species_year_join_with_fall_color
species_year_join_with_fall_color.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.species_scientific_name AS species_scientific_name,
  UPPER(sp.species_scientific_name) AS species_scientific_name_up,
  t._TABLE_SUFFIX AS _TABLE_SUFFIX,
  COUNTIF(t.status = 'Alive') AS alive_count,
  sp.fall_color AS fall_color
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*` AS t
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` AS sp
ON
  UPPER(sp.species_scientific_name) = UPPER(t.spc_latin)
WHERE
  sp.species_scientific_name IS NOT NULL
  AND t.spc_latin IS NOT NULL
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1995' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  species_scientific_name,
  species_scientific_name_up,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX,
  fall_color
species_year_join_with_fall_color.description: Join species yearly alive counts to the normalized species reference by matching uppercased scientific names, producing per-species per-year alive counts along with fall_color. Exclude species where the join key is NULL on either side.

tree_census_rows_1995_to_2015.name: tree_census_rows_1995_to_2015
tree_census_rows_1995_to_2015.body_sql:
SELECT
  recordid AS tree_id,
  spc_latin,
  status,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1995' AND '2015'
tree_census_rows_1995_to_2015.description: Select raw tree census rows from the per-year shard tables for years in the range 1995–2015 (one row per original record). Do not aggregate; preserve spc_latin and status and include the _TABLE_SUFFIX value so callers can restrict to specific years.

tree_census_rows_1995_and_2015.name: tree_census_rows_1995_and_2015
tree_census_rows_1995_and_2015.body_sql:
SELECT
  recordid AS tree_id,
  spc_latin,
  status,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('1995','2015')
tree_census_rows_1995_and_2015.description: Subset of tree census rows limited to the 1995 and 2015 shards only. Keeps one row per original record and preserves spc_latin and status and the _TABLE_SUFFIX for per-year counting.

citibike_trips_2016_clean.name: citibike_trips_2016_clean
citibike_trips_2016_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(start_station_id AS STRING) AS start_station_id,
  CAST(end_station_id AS STRING) AS end_station_id,
  start_station_name AS start_station_name,
  start_station_latitude AS start_station_latitude,
  start_station_longitude AS start_station_longitude,
  end_station_latitude AS end_station_latitude,
  end_station_longitude AS end_station_longitude,
  starttime AS starttime,
  tripduration AS tripduration
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2016
  AND start_station_id IS NOT NULL
  AND end_station_id IS NOT NULL
  AND start_station_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND start_station_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND end_station_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND end_station_longitude IS NOT NULL
citibike_trips_2016_clean.description: Citi Bike trips from the citibike_trips table restricted to year 2016 and cleaned to exclude rows with NULL start/end station coordinates or station ids. Keep original start/end station ids, names, latitudes, longitudes, starttime, and tripduration.

taxi_trips_yellow_2016_clean.name: taxi_trips_yellow_2016_clean
taxi_trips_yellow_2016_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  pickup_latitude,
  pickup_longitude,
  dropoff_latitude,
  dropoff_longitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2016'
  AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT (pickup_latitude = 0 AND pickup_longitude = 0)
  AND NOT (dropoff_latitude = 0 AND dropoff_longitude = 0)
taxi_trips_yellow_2016_clean.description: Yellow taxi trips from tlc_yellow_trips_* restricted to 2016 (table suffix '2016'), excluding rows with NULL or zero pickup/dropoff coordinates. Keep pickup/dropoff datetimes and pickup/dropoff coordinates.

taxi_routes_by_rounded_coords_agg.name: taxi_routes_by_rounded_coords_agg
taxi_routes_by_rounded_coords_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(pickup_latitude, 3) AS pickup_lat_3,
  ROUND(pickup_longitude, 3) AS pickup_lon_3,
  ROUND(dropoff_latitude, 3) AS dropoff_lat_3,
  ROUND(dropoff_longitude, 3) AS dropoff_lon_3,
  AVG(EXTRACT(SECOND FROM dropoff_datetime - pickup_datetime)
      + 60 * EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM dropoff_datetime - pickup_datetime)
      + 3600 * EXTRACT(HOUR FROM dropoff_datetime - pickup_datetime)
      + 86400 * EXTRACT(DAY FROM dropoff_datetime - pickup_datetime)
     ) AS average_taxi_duration_seconds,
  COUNT(*) AS taxi_trip_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2009' AND '2016'
  AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_longitude IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  pickup_lat_3, pickup_lon_3, dropoff_lat_3, dropoff_lon_3
taxi_routes_by_rounded_coords_agg.description: Aggregate taxi trips by pickup/dropoff coordinates rounded to 3 decimal places, computing average taxi trip duration in seconds and trip counts per rounded coordinate pair. Coordinates rounding is applied here to produce keys for matching with Citi Bike rounded station coordinates.

nyc_311_requests_event_norm.name: nyc_311_requests_event_norm
nyc_311_requests_event_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  created_date,
  DATE(created_date) AS created_date_date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_date) AS created_year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM created_date) AS created_month,
  EXTRACT(DAY FROM created_date) AS created_day,
  EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM created_date) AS created_dow,
  closed_date,
  DATE(closed_date) AS closed_date_date,
  status,
  agency,
  agency_name,
  complaint_type,
  descriptor,
  location_type,
  incident_zip,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(incident_address),''), NULL) AS incident_address,
  street_name,
  city,
  borough,
  community_board,
  CAST(bbl AS INT64) AS bbl,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  location,
  open_data_channel_type,
  resolution_description,
  resolution_action_updated_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_311.311_service_requests`

semantic_filters.status: no filter (preserve all statuses); created_date is assumed populated for events

nyc_311_requests_event_norm.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of 311 service requests with canonical date parts and preserved identifiers. Use when analyzing time-series, joining to spatial data, or aggregating by borough/complaint type. | Use for: time-series counts of 311 requests by borough/complaint_type; spatial joins to map requests to boundaries; average time-to-close (closed_date - created_date) by agency or complaint_type; top complaint types by community board or ZIP

citibike_trips_daily_agg.name: citibike_trips_daily_agg
citibike_trips_daily_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(starttime) AS trip_date,
  SAFE_CAST(start_station_id AS STRING) AS start_station_id,
  start_station_name,
  usertype,
  COUNT(1) AS trip_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(tripduration,0)) AS total_trip_seconds,
  AVG(NULLIF(tripduration,0)) AS avg_trip_seconds,
  APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(bikeid) AS distinct_bikes
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
GROUP BY trip_date, start_station_id, start_station_name, usertype

semantic_filters.starttime: assumes starttime is populated; no date range filter applied

citibike_trips_daily_agg.description: Daily aggregated Citibike trip measures by start station id and usertype. Useful for ridership trends, station-level demand, and joins to station metadata. Preserves start date and station id for joins. | Use for: daily demand per station and user type; identify peak days for a station; compute time series for forecasting or seasonality; join to citibike_stations to get capacity/location

citibike_stations_point.name: citibike_stations_point
citibike_stations_point.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  name AS station_name,
  short_name,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  region_id,
  capacity,
  rental_methods AS rental_methods,
  num_bikes_available,
  num_bikes_disabled,
  num_docks_available,
  num_docks_disabled,
  is_installed,
  is_renting,
  is_returning,
  eightd_has_key_dispenser,
  eightd_has_available_keys,
  last_reported
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_stations`
grain: one row per citibike station (station_id) representing current snapshot

semantic_filters.last_reported: no filter (preserve snapshot row(s)); may represent latest only depending on source

citibike_stations_point.description: Cleaned station-level metadata and latest availability snapshot. Use to join spatially or to enrich trip aggregations. Preserves station_id and last_reported for temporal joins. | Use for: map station locations and capacities; compute bike availability ratios; join to trip aggregates to compute utilization

nypd_collisions_person_counts.name: nypd_collisions_person_counts
nypd_collisions_person_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  timestamp,
  DATE(timestamp) AS collision_date,
  borough,
  on_street_name,
  off_street_name,
  cross_street_name,
  SAFE_CAST(zip_code AS STRING) AS zip_code,
  COALESCE(number_of_persons_injured,0) AS persons_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_persons_killed,0) AS persons_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_injured,0) AS pedestrians_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_killed,0) AS pedestrians_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_injured,0) AS cyclists_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_killed,0) AS cyclists_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_motorist_injured,0) AS motorists_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed,0) AS motorists_killed,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  location
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_mv_collisions.nypd_mv_collisions`

semantic_filters.timestamp: no filter applied; keep all collisions

nypd_collisions_person_counts.description: Per-collision summary of injured/killed counts for different road user types plus total persons. Useful when rolling up injuries/fatalities by time, borough, or contributing factor. | Use for: aggregate injuries/fatalities by borough/date; spatial hotspot mapping of collisions; compare vulnerable road user counts over time

subway_stations_with_complex.name: subway_stations_with_complex
subway_stations_with_complex.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id,
  s.station_name,
  s.complex_id,
  c.complex_name,
  s.division,
  s.line,
  s.station_lat,
  s.station_lon,
  s.borough_name,
  s.daytime_routes,
  s.structure
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.stations` AS s
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_complexes` AS c
ON s.complex_id = c.complex_id
grain: one row per subway station (station_id) as in stations table

semantic_filters.complex_id: no filter (preserve rows without complex match)

subway_stations_with_complex.description: Station-level rows joined to their station complex names. Use to enrich station metadata for display or aggregation by complex. | Use for: group ridership by complex_name; map station complexes with station coordinates; join to station entrances for accessibility analysis

subway_entrances_ada_ranked.name: subway_entrances_ada_ranked
subway_entrances_ada_ranked.body_sql:
SELECT
  division,
  line,
  station_name,
  entrance_lat,
  entrance_lon,
  entry,
  exit_only,
  ada_compliant,
  corner,
  ada_notes,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_name ORDER BY CASE WHEN ada_compliant THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, entrance_lat, entrance_lon) AS entrance_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_entrances`
grain: one row per station entrance with a rank per station_name

semantic_filters.ada_compliant: no filter; ranking favors ada_compliant entrances first

subway_entrances_ada_ranked.description: Entrances with an entrance-level rank per station to allow deterministic selection of a representative entrance (e.g., nearest to centroid or first reported). Exposes entrance_rank for downstream top-K or dedup operations. | Use for: select a representative entrance per station (WHERE entrance_rank=1); analyze ADA coverage across representative entrances; map primary entrance locations for stations

taxi_trips_fare_breakdown.name: taxi_trips_fare_breakdown
taxi_trips_fare_breakdown.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id,

eligible_yellow_trips_for_duration.name: eligible_yellow_trips_for_duration
eligible_yellow_trips_for_duration.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime AS tpep_pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime AS tpep_dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- temporal fields present
  pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  -- positive duration (in seconds)
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
  -- passenger_count constraints: not null and reasonable (lift numeric literals into query using bounds)
  AND passenger_count IS NOT NULL
  AND passenger_count BETWEEN 1 AND 6
  -- trip_distance positive and reasonable
  AND trip_distance IS NOT NULL
  AND trip_distance > 0
  AND trip_distance < 500
  -- both pickup and dropoff in Brooklyn: join to taxi_zone_geom by zone id
  AND pickup_location_id IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_location_id IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` zpu
    WHERE zpu.zone_id = pickup_location_id
      AND LOWER(zpu.borough) = 'brooklyn'
  )
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` zdo
    WHERE zdo.zone_id = dropoff_location_id
      AND LOWER(zdo.borough) = 'brooklyn'
  )

taxi_trips_with_borough_and_tip_rate.name: taxi_trips_with_borough_and_tip_rate
taxi_trips_with_borough_and_tip_rate.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry canonical pickup datetime and location id for grain/joinability
  pickup_datetime,
  pickup_location_id,
  -- canonical pickup borough taken from taxi zone lookup
  COALESCE(z.borough, 'UNKNOWN') AS pickup_borough,
  -- include zone name for context
  z.zone_name AS zone_name,
  -- monetary fields
  tip_amount,
  total_amount,
  -- tip_rate as percentage (0-100). NULL when total_amount is NULL or zero to avoid division by zero.
  CASE
    WHEN total_amount IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN total_amount = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_MULTIPLY(CAST(tip_amount AS FLOAT64) / CAST(total_amount AS FLOAT64), 100)
  END AS tip_rate
FROM
  -- wildcard across both yellow and green trip shards; keep rows from both datasets
  (
    SELECT
      pickup_datetime,
      pickup_location_id,
      tip_amount,
      total_amount
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      pickup_datetime,
      pickup_location_id,
      tip_amount,
      total_amount
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_green_trips_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2014' AND '2023'
  ) AS trips
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS z
ON
  trips.pickup_location_id = z.zone_id

yellow_taxi_raw_trips.name: yellow_taxi_raw_trips
yellow_taxi_raw_trips.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id AS vendorid,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  fare_amount,

  tip_amount,
  tolls_amount,
  imp_surcharge AS improvement_surcharge,
  total_amount,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  -- Construct a stable trip_id from available fields (keep keys in view).
  -- Do not use literals here; this expression is deterministic per row.
  CONCAT(CAST(data_file_year AS STRING), '-', CAST(data_file_month AS STRING), '-', COALESCE(CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING), ''), '-', COALESCE(CAST(dropoff_datetime AS STRING), ''), '-', COALESCE(CAST(fare_amount AS STRING), ''), '-', COALESCE(pickup_location_id, ''), '-', COALESCE(dropoff_location_id, '')) AS trip_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- restrict to the shard range when querying the view (lift specific year ranges out of queries that use the view)
  TRUE
  -- temporal validity: both datetimes present and dropoff after pickup
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime > pickup_datetime
  -- reasonable operating window: pickup and dropoff years between 2009 and 2030 (filters obvious junk)
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM pickup_datetime) BETWEEN 2009 AND 2030
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM dropoff_datetime) BETWEEN 2009 AND 2030
  -- numeric fields are non-negative and not absurdly large
  AND passenger_count IS NOT NULL AND passenger_count BETWEEN 0 AND 20
  AND trip_distance IS NOT NULL AND trip_distance >= 0 AND trip_distance < 1000
  AND fare_amount IS NOT NULL AND fare_amount >= 0 AND fare_amount < 10000
  AND extra IS NOT NULL AND extra >= 0 AND extra < 1000
  AND mta_tax IS NOT NULL AND mta_tax >= 0 AND mta_tax < 100
  AND tip_amount IS NOT NULL AND tip_amount >= 0 AND tip_amount < 10000
  AND tolls_amount IS NOT NULL AND tolls_amount >= 0 AND tolls_amount < 1000
  AND imp_surcharge IS NOT NULL AND imp_surcharge >= 0 AND imp_surcharge < 100
  AND total_amount IS NOT NULL AND total_amount >= 0 AND total_amount < 20000
  -- location ids carried through; allow NULLs but prefer non-empty strings if present

SELECT

  -- normalize borough: trim, upper-case first letter + lower rest, map common variants, NULLs excluded by WHERE
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(borough)) IN ('manhattan') THEN 'Manhattan'
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(borough)) IN ('bronx') THEN 'Bronx'
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(borough)) IN ('brooklyn') THEN 'Brooklyn'
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(borough)) IN ('staten island', 'statenisland', 'staten-island') THEN 'Staten Island'
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(borough)) IN ('queens') THEN 'Queens'
    -- fallback: title-case the cleaned string
    ELSE INITCAP(TRIM(borough))
  END AS borough
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom`
WHERE borough IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(borough) <> ''

trip_time_and_speed_metrics.name: trip_time_and_speed_metrics
trip_time_and_speed_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Use a deterministic trip identifier composed from pickup/dropoff timestamps and vendor_id and fare to keep joinability.
  -- Carry key-like fields out so view remains joinable; here we synthesize trip_id.
  CONCAT(
    vendor_id, '_',
    FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m%d%H%M%S', pickup_datetime), '_',
    FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m%d%H%M%S', dropoff_datetime), '_',
    CAST(FLOOR(total_amount * 100) AS STRING)
  ) AS trip_id,
  -- Preserve pickup/dropoff zone ids requested in required CSV header (renamed below in final SELECT ordering)
  pickup_location_id AS pickup_zone,
  dropoff_location_id AS dropoff_zone,
  -- Trip duration in seconds: use SAFE_CAST to avoid errors; if timestamps missing or negative produce NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_datetime IS NULL OR dropoff_datetime IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS INT64)
  END AS trip_duration_seconds,
  -- Driving speed in miles per hour: trip_distance miles divided by duration in hours.
  -- If duration <= 0 or trip_distance is NULL produce NULL. Use numeric calculation with safe casts.
  CASE
    WHEN trip_distance IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN pickup_datetime IS NULL OR dropoff_datetime IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) <= 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- trip_distance is NUMERIC, convert to FLOAT64 for division and multiply to get mph.
      (SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS FLOAT64) / (SAFE_CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS FLOAT64) / 3600.0))
  END AS driving_speed_mph,
  -- Tip rate percent: tip_amount divided by fare_amount (metered fare) expressed as percent.
  -- If fare_amount is NULL or zero produce NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN tip_amount IS NULL OR fare_amount IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS FLOAT64) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE
      SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS FLOAT64) / SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS FLOAT64) * 100.0
  END AS tip_rate_percent
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- Example suffix filter lifted out of view (caller should supply desired range when querying the view).
  -- Keep all shards by default if caller does not filter; no _TABLE_SUFFIX filter here.
  TRUE
trip_time_and_speed_metrics.description: Normalized per-trip temporal and derived metrics: canonical total trip duration in seconds and driving speed in miles per hour computed from trip_distance and duration. Assumes input rows are individual trips (e.g., from taxi_trips_2016_july_cohort).

bikeshare_trip_events.description: Cleaned bikeshare trip events: one row per trip with canonical start/end datetimes and durations. Use for trip-level analysis, joins to stations, and subscriber segmentation. | Use for: Trip duration distributions and median/mean durations; Origin-destination flow counts by station; Subscriber type comparisons and home-zip analyses

service_requests_events.name: service_requests_events

service_requests_events.description: 311 service requests normalized: one row per request with created/closed timestamps, status, category and spatial columns for temporal or spatial analysis. | Use for: Time-to-close analyses and backlog counts by agency; Spatial clustering of complaint categories; Cross-compare 311 requests with SFPD or SFFD events by time/location

station_daily_trip_aggregates.name: station_daily_trip_aggregates
station_daily_trip_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  start_station_id,
  DATE(start_date) AS trip_date,
  COUNT(1) AS trips_start_count,
  AVG(duration_sec) AS avg_duration_sec,
  SUM(CASE WHEN subscriber_type IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS trips_with_subscriber_info
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
GROUP BY start_station_id, DATE(start_date)
grain: start_station_id + trip_date, one row per station per day
station_daily_trip_aggregates.description: Daily aggregated trips per station (as origin): counts and average duration per day per start_station_id. Use for time-series station activity and trend detection. | Use for: Daily activity trends per station; Detect seasonality or weekday patterns in trips; Compare average trip durations across stations

station_latest_status_rank.name: station_latest_status_rank
station_latest_status_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  bikes_available,
  docks_available,
  time AS sample_time,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn_desc_time
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_status`
grain: station_id + sample_time, one row per status sample (ranked per station)
station_latest_status_rank.description: Latest known status per station using ranking by time. Expose rn_desc_time so consumers can filter to the most recent sample (rn_desc_time = 1). Useful for real-time dashboarding or availability snapshots. | Use for: Select most recent availability per station by filtering rn_desc_time = 1; Show top-N stations by available bikes at latest sample using rn_desc_time = 1 then rank

incidents_weekly_counts_by_category.name: incidents_weekly_counts_by_category
incidents_weekly_counts_by_category.body_sql:

FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.sfpd_incidents`
GROUP BY category, pddistrict, year, iso_week
grain: category + pddistrict + year + iso_week, one row per category-district-week
incidents_weekly_counts_by_category.description: Weekly counts of SFPD incidents by category and police district. Use for trend analysis and seasonal comparison at week granularity. | Use for: Week-over-week incident trends by category or district; Seasonal comparisons across years for a category

bikeshare_stations_canonical.name: bikeshare_stations_canonical
bikeshare_stations_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(station_id AS INT64) AS station_id,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations`
WHERE station_id IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
bikeshare_stations_canonical.description: Canonicalized station records with numeric latitude and longitude fields and a normalized station_id for joins. One row per station; ensure lat/lon are numeric and non-null where possible.

valid_bikeshare_trips.name: valid_bikeshare_trips
valid_bikeshare_trips.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  bike_number,
  start_station_id,
  end_station_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
WHERE
  bike_number IS NOT NULL
  AND start_station_id IS NOT NULL
  AND end_station_id IS NOT NULL
valid_bikeshare_trips.description: Subset of bikeshare trips that have non-null bike_number and non-null start and end station ids. Does not join to stations; preserves trip-level identity.

trip_start_end_stations.name: trip_start_end_stations
trip_start_end_stations.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id AS trip_id,
  t.bike_number AS bike_number,
  t.start_station_id AS start_station_id,
  t.end_station_id AS end_station_id,
  s_start.latitude AS start_latitude,
  s_start.longitude AS start_longitude,
  s_end.latitude AS end_latitude,
  s_end.longitude AS end_longitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips` AS t
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations` AS s_start
  ON t.start_station_id = s_start.station_id
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations` AS s_end
  ON t.end_station_id = s_end.station_id
trip_start_end_stations.description: Trip-level relation joining each valid trip to its start and end station canonical records, producing start/end latitudes and longitudes. Rows where either station is missing in stations are excluded at this stage.

bikeshare_trips_nonnull_times.name: bikeshare_trips_nonnull_times
bikeshare_trips_nonnull_times.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  start_date,
  duration_sec
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
WHERE
  start_date IS NOT NULL
  AND duration_sec IS NOT NULL
bikeshare_trips_nonnull_times.description: One row per trip from bikeshare_trips excluding records with NULL start_date or NULL duration_sec; preserves original timestamp and duration columns for downstream processing.

bikeshare_trip_month_key.name: bikeshare_trip_month_key
bikeshare_trip_month_key.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  start_date,
  duration_sec,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m', start_date) AS year_month
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
bikeshare_trip_month_key.description: Normalize trips to attach a year_month key (string YYYYMM) derived from the start_date timezone-aware value; one row per trip.

bikeshare_trip_month_bounds.name: bikeshare_trip_month_bounds
bikeshare_trip_month_bounds.body_sql:
SELECT
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', start_month) AS year_month,
  MIN(start_month) AS min_start_date,
  MAX(start_month) AS max_start_date,
  MIN(duration_sec) AS min_duration_sec,
  MAX(duration_sec) AS max_duration_sec
FROM (
  SELECT
    TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(start_date, MONTH) AS start_month,
    start_date,
    duration_sec,
    trip_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
)
GROUP BY start_month
ORDER BY start_month
bikeshare_trip_month_bounds.description: Per year_month, compute earliest and latest start_date values and aggregate min/max duration_sec; one row per year_month (rolling/grouping key), intended for computing first/last/min/max measures.

bikeshare_trip_first_last_by_month.name: bikeshare_trip_first_last_by_month
bikeshare_trip_first_last_by_month.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', start_date) AS year_month,
  start_date,
  duration_sec,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', start_date) ORDER BY start_date ASC, trip_id ASC) AS rank_asc,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', start_date) ORDER BY start_date DESC, trip_id ASC) AS rank_desc
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
bikeshare_trip_first_last_by_month.description: Within each year_month, rank trips by start_date to identify the first (earliest) and last (latest) trip rows so their duration_sec can be retrieved; one row per trip with month-level rank values.

svc_requests_core.name: svc_requests_core
svc_requests_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  created_date AS created_ts,
  closed_date AS closed_ts,
  resolution_action_updated_date AS resolution_updated_ts,
  status,
  status_notes,
  agency_name,
  category,
  complaint_type,
  descriptor,
  incident_address,
  supervisor_district,
  neighborhood,
  location,
  source,
  media_url,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  police_district,
  -- derived convenience columns
  CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM created_date) AS DATE) AS created_date_only,
  CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM closed_date) AS DATE) AS closed_date_only,
  -- request duration in seconds when both timestamps present
  SAFE_CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(closed_date, created_date, SECOND) AS INT64) AS duration_seconds
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_311.311_service_requests`
svc_requests_core.description: Cleaned/normalized view of 311 service requests: casts and canonicalizes key columns, extracts dates, and exposes location coordinates and text fields for easy filtering and joins. Use this as the normalized base when analyzing request volumes, times-to-close, neighborhood or district breakdowns, and joins to spatial/neighborhood data. | Use for: time series of 311 requests (daily/monthly); average/median time-to-close by category or agency; spatial distribution of requests using latitude/longitude or neighborhood; counts by status, category, complaint_type, or supervisor_district

Use to join trips, status snapshots, and regions. station_id is kept as STRING to match station_status; casts may be needed when joining to bikeshare_trips which uses INT ids. | Use for: station inventory and capacities; spatial joins to neighborhoods or region-level aggregations; joining to station status snapshots and trips

bikeshare_station_status_snapshots.name: bikeshare_station_status_snapshots
bikeshare_station_status_snapshots.body_sql:
SELECT

bikeshare_station_status_snapshots.description: Aggregated station status snapshots per station report time: exposes measures (bikes/docks available/disabled), booleans (installed/renting/returning), and readable last_reported timestamp. Useful for time-series analysis, capacity checks, and computing availability trends. One row per station_id + last_reported (POSIX epoch) snapshot. | Use for: time series of bikes/docks availability; compute peak/trough availability per station; join latest snapshot per station with station dim

bikeshare_trips_core.name: bikeshare_trips_core
bikeshare_trips_core.body_sql:

FROM

bikeshare_trips_core.description: Normalized bikeshare trips table: preserves trip identifiers, timestamps, station ids (kept as INT64 where provided), coordinates, member attributes, and duration. Use as the canonical trips fact for duration, origin/destination, subscriber analyses, and joining to station dimension (may need cast of station_id). | Use for: trip duration distributions by subscriber type or time of day; origin-destination matrices (start_station_id -> end_station_id); join trips to station dimension after casting station ids

bikeshare_station_latest_status_rank.name: bikeshare_station_latest_status_rank
bikeshare_station_latest_status_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,

  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(last_reported) AS reported_ts,
  num_bikes_available,
  num_docks_available,
  is_installed,
  is_renting,
  is_returning,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY last_reported DESC) AS snapshot_rank
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_status`
grain: one row per station snapshot (station_id + last_reported); ranked per station
bikeshare_station_latest_status_rank.description: Ranked status snapshots per station ordered by report time. Exposes row_rank so downstream queries can select the latest snapshot per station by filtering row_rank = 1. Useful for getting current availability per station without hard-coding time windows. | Use for: select latest status per station (WHERE snapshot_rank = 1); time-aware joins to trips for availability at trip start times (use ranking to pick closest prior snapshot)

sfpd_incidents_core.name: sfpd_incidents_core

sffd_calls_core.description: Normalized SFFD service calls: preserves call identifiers, time fields as timestamps, location coordinates and neighborhood metadata. Use for temporal patterns, priority analyses, and spatial aggregation to neighborhoods or districts. | Use for: counts by call_type or priority; response time analyses using dispatch/response/on_scene timestamps; spatial distribution of calls by neighborhood or coordinates

neighborhoods_geoms.name: neighborhoods_geoms
neighborhoods_geoms.body_sql:

film_locations_core.name: film_locations_core
film_locations_core.body_sql:

film_locations_core.description: Film locations records: preserves title, release year, location text and principal creative cast/crew columns. Use for counts of filmings by neighborhood (text matching) or time-series of filming activity. | Use for: counts of filming locations by year or location text; find films shot in a given neighborhood by text match; aggregate directors/actors with most filmed scenes

bikeshare_station_with_latest_status.name: bikeshare_station_with_latest_status
bikeshare_station_with_latest_status.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id,
  s.name AS station_name,
  s.lat AS station_latitude,
  s.lon AS station_longitude,
  s.region_id,
  s.capacity,
  s.has_kiosk,
  ss.reported_ts AS status_reported_ts,
  ss.num_bikes_available,
  ss.num_docks_available,
  ss.is_installed,
  ss.is_renting,
  ss.is_returning
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` AS s
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    station_id,
    TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(last_reported) AS reported_ts,
    num_bikes_available,
    num_docks_available,
    is_installed,
    is_renting,
    is_returning
  FROM (
    SELECT
      station_id,
      last_reported,
      num_bikes_available,
      num_docks_available,
      is_installed,
      is_renting,
      is_returning,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY last_reported DESC) AS rn
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_status`
  )
  WHERE rn = 1
) AS ss
ON s.station_id = ss.station_id
grain: one row per station (station_id) with latest known status
bikeshare_station_with_latest_status.description: Join station dimension to its latest status snapshot (use snapshot_rank = 1 on bikeshare_station_latest_status_rank). Exposes station static attributes alongside most-recent availability metrics. Useful for current availability dashboards and joins to trips for origin/destination availability comparisons. | Use for: current availability per station; capacity vs available bikes/docks ratios; map stations colored by availability

bikeshare_station_region_map.name: bikeshare_station_region_map
bikeshare_station_region_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id AS station_id,
  s.region_id AS region_id,
  r.name AS region_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` AS s
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_regions` AS r
ON s.region_id = r.region_id
bikeshare_station_region_map.description: Mapping of station_id to its region (region_id and region name) using canonical station info and regions table; one row per station. Does not filter by date or trips.

bikeshare_trips_2017_ended.name: bikeshare_trips_2017_ended
bikeshare_trips_2017_ended.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id AS trip_id,
  t.end_date AS end_date,
  t.duration_sec AS duration_sec,
  t.subscriber_type AS subscriber_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.end_date) = 2017
  AND t.subscriber_type IN ('Subscriber', 'Customer')
bikeshare_trips_2017_ended.description: Subset of cleaned trips that ended in calendar year 2017 (uses end_date timestamp to determine year) and only keeps rows whose subscriber_type is exactly 'Subscriber' or 'Customer'.

monthly_usage_minutes_by_subscriber_type.name: monthly_usage_minutes_by_subscriber_type
monthly_usage_minutes_by_subscriber_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM start_date) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM start_date) AS month,
  subscriber_type,
  SUM(duration_sec) / 60.0 AS total_minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
GROUP BY
  year,
  month,
  subscriber_type
monthly_usage_minutes_by_subscriber_type.description: For each calendar month and subscriber_type, aggregate total usage minutes (sum of duration_sec converted to minutes). One row per month and subscriber_type.

monthly_subscriber_type_pivot.name: monthly_subscriber_type_pivot
monthly_subscriber_type_pivot.body_sql:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(start_date, MONTH)) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM start_date) AS month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN subscriber_type = 'Subscriber' THEN duration_sec/60.0 ELSE 0 END) AS total_minutes_subscriber,
  SUM(CASE WHEN subscriber_type = 'Customer' THEN duration_sec/60.0 ELSE 0 END) AS total_minutes_customer
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
GROUP BY
  year,
  month
monthly_subscriber_type_pivot.description: Pivot monthly totals into columns per subscriber_type (e.g., total_minutes_subscriber, total_minutes_customer) so differences between the two types per month can be computed easily.

stops_canonical.name: stops_canonical
stops_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  stop_id AS stop_id,
  TRIM(stop_name) AS stop_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_transit_muni.stops`
GROUP BY
  stop_id, stop_name
stops_canonical.description: Canonicalized stop records with their stop_id and stop_name (cleaned/trimmed). One row per stop_id.

stop_times_clean.name: stop_times_clean
stop_times_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(st.trip_id AS INT64) AS trip_id,
  CAST(st.stop_id AS INT64) AS stop_id,
  CAST(st.stop_sequence AS INT64) AS stop_sequence,
  st.arrival_time AS arrival_time,
  st.departure_time AS departure_time
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_transit_muni.stop_times` AS st
WHERE
  -- Exclude NULLs
  st.arrival_time IS NOT NULL
  AND st.departure_time IS NOT NULL
  -- arrival_time and departure_time are TIME typed in the source; ensure they are valid by attempting a SAFE_CAST to TIME when formats might vary.
  -- If values are already TIME they pass; if malformed strings exist (unexpectedly), SAFE_CAST will yield NULL and be filtered above.
  AND SAFE_CAST(st.arrival_time AS TIME) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(st.departure_time AS TIME) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  trip_id,
  stop_sequence,
  stop_id,
  arrival_time,
  departure_time
stop_times_clean.description: Cleaned stop_times rows with parsed/validated arrival_time and departure_time as TIME values, excluding rows where arrival_time or departure_time is NULL or malformed. One row per (trip_id, stop_sequence, stop_id).

trips_with_route.name: trips_with_route

bikeshare_trips_with_distance_and_durati.name: bikeshare_trips_with_distance_and_duration
bikeshare_trips_with_distance_and_durati.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id,
  CAST(t.start_station_id AS STRING) AS start_station_id,
  CAST(t.end_station_id AS STRING) AS end_station_id,
  t.start_station_name,
  t.end_station_name,
  s_start.station_geom AS start_station_geom,
  s_end.station_geom AS end_station_geom,
  ST_DISTANCE(s_start.station_geom, s_end.station_geom) AS distance_meters,
  t.duration_sec,
  CASE
    WHEN t.duration_sec > 0 THEN ST_DISTANCE(s_start.station_geom, s_end.station_geom) / CAST(t.duration_sec AS FLOAT64)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS avg_speed_m_per_s
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` AS s_start
  ON CAST(t.start_station_id AS STRING) = s_start.station_id
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` AS s_end
  ON CAST(t.end_station_id AS STRING) = s_end.station_id
WHERE t.duration_sec IS NOT NULL
  AND t.duration_sec != 0
  AND s_start.station_geom IS NOT NULL
  AND s_end.station_geom IS NOT NULL
bikeshare_trips_with_distance_and_durati.description: Bike trips joined to canonical start and end station records, computing geodesic trip distance in meters (from start station_geom to end station_geom) and exposing trip duration in seconds. Excludes trips missing start/end station geometry or missing/zero duration values.

neighborhood_member_counts.name: neighborhood_member_counts
neighborhood_member_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.neighborhood AS neighborhood,
  -- count of bikeshare stations whose station_geom lies within the neighborhood polygon
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.station_id) AS station_count,
  -- count of SFPD incidents whose point (longitude, latitude) lies within the neighborhood polygon
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.unique_key) AS incident_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_neighborhoods.boundaries` AS n
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` AS b
ON
  ST_CONTAINS(n.neighborhood_geom, b.station_geom)
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_sfpd_incidents.sfpd_incidents` AS s
ON
  -- incidents provide latitude/longitude as floats; build a POINT geography for containment test
  ST_CONTAINS(n.neighborhood_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(s.longitude, s.latitude))
GROUP BY
  n.neighborhood
neighborhood_member_counts.description: Counts of bikeshare stations and SFPD incidents per neighborhood by spatially joining station and incident points to neighborhood geometries. Produce one row per neighborhood with counts (but do not filter by count thresholds here).

population_under_20_by_country_year.name: population_under_20_by_country_year
population_under_20_by_country_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  year,
  SUM(population) AS population_under_20
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific`
WHERE
  age BETWEEN 0 AND 19
GROUP BY
  country_code,
  year
population_under_20_by_country_year.description: Total population aged 0-19 aggregated per country_code and year (summing midyear_population_agespecific population for ages 0..19).

country_population_under20_with_midyear.name: country_population_under20_with_midyear
country_population_under20_with_midyear.body_sql:
SELECT
  ay.country_code AS country_code,
  ay.year AS year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ay.age BETWEEN @age_min AND @age_max THEN COALESCE(ay.population,0) ELSE 0 END) AS population_under_20,
  mp.midyear_population AS midyear_population
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific` AS ay
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population` AS mp
ON
  ay.country_code = mp.country_code
  AND ay.year = mp.year
WHERE
  mp.midyear_population IS NOT NULL
  AND mp.midyear_population != 0
GROUP BY
  ay.country_code,
  ay.year,
  mp.midyear_population
country_population_under20_with_midyear.description: Denormalized rows per country_code and year that combine the country's midyear_population and the aggregated population under 20, excluding cases where midyear_population is NULL or zero. This prepares the inputs needed to compute percent_under_20.

age_specific_population_by_country_year_.name: age_specific_population_by_country_year_age

Keep one row per country_code, country_name, year, and age with the population count and any original population metadata. Do not aggregate ages here.

countries_with_both_age_specific_and_tot.name: countries_with_both_age_specific_and_total_population
countries_with_both_age_specific_and_tot.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.country_code AS country_code,
  m.country_name AS country_name,
  m.year AS year,
  -- population under 25 computed from age-specific table by summing ages 0-24
  SUM(CASE WHEN a.age BETWEEN 0 AND 24 THEN a.population ELSE 0 END) AS population_under_25,
  m.midyear_population AS total_population
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population` AS m
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific` AS a
ON
  m.country_code = a.country_code
  AND m.year = a.year
GROUP BY
  m.country_code,
  m.country_name,
  m.year,
  m.midyear_population
countries_with_both_age_specific_and_tot.description: Join the per-country-year population_under_25 measure with the total midyear_population for the same country_code and year to produce one row per country-year that has both values, enabling calculation of percentage under 25.

countries_with_area.name: countries_with_area

countries_with_area_and_migration.name: countries_with_area_and_migration
countries_with_area_and_migration.body_sql:

  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.country_names_area` AS a
RIGHT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.birth_death_growth_rates` AS b
ON
  a.country_code = b.country_code
countries_with_area_and_migration.description: Denormalized one-row-per country_code and year combining country area and name with yearly migration metrics by joining country area info to the yearly migration rates.

daily_location_metrics.description: One-row-per-location-per-date projection exposing core daily epidemiological and vaccination measures plus place identifiers and population. Use this as the base relation for filtering by date ranges, countries, or aggregation levels before downstream aggregates or windowing. | Use for: Filter for country/date ranges and aggregate cases/deaths/vaccinations; Map visualizations using latitude/longitude and recent measures; Per-capita rate calculations after joining population

latest_metrics_per_location.name: latest_metrics_per_location
latest_metrics_per_location.body_sql:
SELECT
  location_key,
  date,
  place_id,
  country_code,
  country_name,
  aggregation_level,
  population,
  cumulative_confirmed,
  cumulative_deceased,
  cumulative_recovered,
  cumulative_tested,
  cumulative_persons_vaccinated,
  cumulative_persons_fully_vaccinated,
  current_hospitalized_patients,
  current_intensive_care_patients,
  current_ventilator_patients,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY location_key ORDER BY date DESC) AS row_rank,
  DATE_DIFF(CURRENT_DATE(), MAX(date) OVER (PARTITION BY location_key), DAY) AS days_since_latest
FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
grain: one row per location_key per ranked row (use WHERE row_rank = 1 externally to get latest snapshot)
latest_metrics_per_location.description: Latest available row per location_key with a deterministic pick of the most recent date. Exposes the latest cumulative and current measures along with a rank and days_since_latest for downstream Top-K, freshness checks, or snapshot analyses. | Use for: Get the most recent snapshot of cases/deaths/vaccinations per location; Identify stale locations by days_since_latest; Compute Top-K locations by cumulative measures by filtering row_rank = 1 then ordering

rolling_7d_rates_by_location.name: rolling_7d_rates_by_location
rolling_7d_rates_by_location.body_sql:
SELECT
  location_key,
  date,
  new_confirmed,
  new_deceased,
  population,
  SUM(COALESCE(new_confirmed,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY location_key ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_7d_confirmed,
  AVG(COALESCE(new_confirmed,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY location_key ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_7d_avg_confirmed,
  SUM(COALESCE(new_deceased,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY location_key ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_7d_deceased,
  AVG(COALESCE(new_deceased,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY location_key ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_7d_avg_deceased,
  SAFE_DIVIDE( SUM(COALESCE(new_confirmed,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY location_key ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) * 100000.0, NULLIF(population,0)) AS rolling_7d_confirmed_per_100k
FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
grain: one row per location_key per date (with rolling window metrics)
rolling_7d_rates_by_location.description: 7-day rolling sums and 7-day average daily new cases/deaths per location. Keeps date and location granularity and exposes rolling_sum, rolling_avg and a rolling_rate_per_100k using population to facilitate time-series smoothing and per-capita comparisons. | Use for: Trend analysis with smoothed new cases/deaths; Per-capita comparisons across locations using rolling rates; Detect recent surges by comparing current rolling_avg to historical baselines

    cumulative_deceased_age_0,cumulative_deceased_age_1,cumulative_deceased_age_2,cumulative_deceased_age_3,cumulative_deceased_age_4,
    cumulative_deceased_age_5,cumulative_deceased_age_6,cumulative_deceased_age_7,cumulative_deceased_age_8,cumulative_deceased_age_9,
    age_bin_0,age_bin_1,age_bin_2,age_bin_3,age_bin_4,age_bin_5,age_bin_6,age_bin_7,age_bin_8,age_bin_9
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
), UNNEST([
  STRUCT(age_bin_0 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_0 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_0 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_0 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_0 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_1 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_1 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_1 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_1 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_1 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_2 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_2 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_2 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_2 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_2 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_3 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_3 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_3 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_3 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_3 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_4 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_4 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_4 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_4 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_4 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_5 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_5 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_5 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_5 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_5 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_6 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_6 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_6 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_6 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_6 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_7 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_7 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_7 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_7 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_7 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_8 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_8 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_8 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_8 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_8 AS cumulative_deceased),
  STRUCT(age_bin_9 AS age_bin, new_confirmed_age_9 AS new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed_age_9 AS cumulative_confirmed, new_deceased_age_9 AS new_deceased, cumulative_deceased_age_9 AS cumulative_deceased)
]) AS unnested
grain: one row per location_key, date, age_bucket
age_bucket_unpivoted.description: Unpivots age-bucketed new and cumulative confirmed and deceased counts into one row per location/date/age_bucket. Useful for age-stratified analyses, population-weighted rates, or combining with age bin labels. | Use for: Age-stratified case/death rates and trends; Compare vaccination or hospitalization by age if age-specific columns are present; Normalize age-bucketed counts by external or inferred age-population shares

covid_country_level_rows.name: covid_country_level_rows
covid_country_level_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  country_name,
  aggregation_level,
  cumulative_confirmed,
  cumulative_recovered
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  aggregation_level = 0
  AND country_name IS NOT NULL
covid_country_level_rows.description: Select rows that represent country-level observations (no subnational aggregation) and have a non-null country name. This is a cohort / row-subset filter for country-level data.

covid_country_counts_normalized.name: covid_country_counts_normalized
covid_country_counts_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  country_name,
  SAFE_CAST(IFNULL(cumulative_confirmed, 0) AS INT64) AS cumulative_confirmed,
  SAFE_CAST(IFNULL(cumulative_recovered, 0) AS INT64) AS cumulative_recovered
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  aggregation_level = 2
  AND country_name IS NOT NULL
covid_country_counts_normalized.description: Normalize and cast key numeric columns for country-level rows (ensure cumulative_confirmed and cumulative_recovered are numeric/integer and handle nulls). Produces a clean, canonical set of columns for downstream calculations.

covid_country_counts_snapshot.name: covid_country_counts_snapshot
covid_country_counts_snapshot.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  country_name,
  SUM(cumulative_confirmed) AS cumulative_confirmed,
  SUM(cumulative_recovered) AS cumulative_recovered
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
GROUP BY
  date,
  country_name
covid_country_counts_snapshot.description: For each country and date, ensure there is a single canonical row (grouped measures per key). This groups/aggregates if the source can contain multiple rows per country/date, producing one row per country/date with summed or maxed cumulative counts as appropriate.

covid_country_recovery_rate.name: covid_country_recovery_rate
covid_country_recovery_rate.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  country_name,
  cumulative_confirmed,
  cumulative_recovered,
  SAFE_MULTIPLY(100.0, SAFE_DIVIDE(cumulative_recovered, NULLIF(cumulative_confirmed, 0))) AS recovery_rate_percent
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  aggregation_level = 0
covid_country_recovery_rate.description: Compute per-country recovery rate as 100.0 * cumulative_recovered / cumulative_confirmed for each country/date row. This produces a measure column (recovery_rate_percent) alongside the country/date counts.

covid_daily_location_records.name: covid_daily_location_records
covid_daily_location_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  dlm.place_id AS location,
  dlm.date AS date,
  dlm.country_name AS country_name,
  dlm.new_confirmed AS new_confirmed,
  dlm.cumulative_confirmed AS cumulative_confirmed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data` AS src
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data` AS dlm
ON
  TRUE
WHERE
  -- base cohort: keep rows with non-null location (place_id or location_key) and date and at least one confirmed metric present
  dlm.date IS NOT NULL
  AND (dlm.place_id IS NOT NULL OR dlm.location_key IS NOT NULL)
  AND (dlm.new_confirmed IS NOT NULL OR dlm.cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL)
covid_daily_location_records.description: Row-level daily COVID-19 observations for locations (one input row per location-date) with basic null filters applied. This isolates the base cohort of records to be used for further calculations.

covid_daily_us_march_april.name: covid_daily_us_march_april
covid_daily_us_march_april.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name AS location,
  date,
  new_confirmed,
  cumulative_confirmed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  country_name = 'United States'
  AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) IN (3, 4)
  AND cumulative_confirmed > 0
covid_daily_us_march_april.description: Subset of daily location records restricted to the United States and to the months of March or April (any year). Keeps rows where cumulative_confirmed > 0 to avoid division by zero.

covid_daily_growth_rate.name: covid_daily_growth_rate
covid_daily_growth_rate.body_sql:
SELECT
  dlm.location_key AS location,
  dlm.date AS date,
  FORMAT_DATE('%m-%d', dlm.date) AS date_mm_dd,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(dlm.new_confirmed, NULLIF(dlm.cumulative_confirmed, 0)) AS growth_rate
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data` AS src
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data` AS dlm
ON
  TRUE
WHERE
  FALSE
covid_daily_growth_rate.description: Per-location-per-date normalized calculation of confirmed-case growth rate defined as new_confirmed / cumulative_confirmed; includes a formatted month-day string of the date for downstream reporting.

covid_country_aggregated_by_country_date.name: covid_country_aggregated_by_country_date
covid_country_aggregated_by_country_date.body_sql:
SELECT

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
GROUP BY
  country_code,
  date
covid_country_aggregated_by_country_date.description: Aggregated COVID-19 measures at the country-date level. For cases where place-level rows exist, roll up cumulative_confirmed to one row per country_code and date (sum or max as appropriate downstream). Produce one row per country_code + date.

jhu_summary_daily_per_location.name: jhu_summary_daily_per_location
jhu_summary_daily_per_location.body_sql:

clean_cast_symptom_value.name: clean_cast_symptom_value
clean_cast_symptom_value.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- date as DATE type (some source tables use STRING, some DATE)
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', COALESCE(t.date, CAST(t.date AS STRING))) AS date,
  t.place_id,
  -- canonicalize country names / codes: standardize common variants for United States as example;
  -- lift literals out of view (so minimal canonicalization here using COALESCE and simple mapping)
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(t.country_region) IN ('united states', 'united states of america', 'us', 'usa') THEN 'United States'
    WHEN LOWER(t.country_region_code) IN ('us','usa') THEN 'United States'
    ELSE t.country_region
  END AS country_region,
  -- preserve country code if present; normalize common variant for US to 'US'
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(t.country_region_code) IN ('united states of america','usa') THEN 'US'
    ELSE t.country_region_code
  END AS country_region_code,
  -- simple canonicalization for sub_region_1 (state) common variants (examples lifted out)
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(t.sub_region_1) IN ('ca','california') THEN 'California'
    WHEN LOWER(t.sub_region_1) IN ('ny','new york state','new york') THEN 'New York'
    ELSE t.sub_region_1
  END AS sub_region_1,
  t.sub_region_2,
  -- symptom name normalized to lowercase and underscores replaced for consistency
  LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(symptom_name, r'[^a-z0-9]+','_')) AS symptom,
  -- cast string-like symptom values to numeric where possible; filter empty/NULL/NaN by returning only valid numbers
  SAFE_CAST(
    -- some tables store numeric as FLOAT; some store as STRING like "0.12" or "<0.01" etc.
    -- remove common non-numeric prefixes/symbols like '<' and whitespace, and treat empty strings as NULL
    NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(value_str, CAST(value_num AS STRING)), r'^\s*<\s*', ''), '') AS NUMERIC
  ) AS value_numeric
FROM (
  -- Union rows from multiple tables and unpivot symptom columns into (symptom_name, value_str/value_num)
  SELECT
    country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_2, place_id, date,
    symptom_name, value_str, NULL AS value_num
  FROM (
    -- country_weekly and similar weekly/daily string-typed tables (many columns named symptom_*)
    SELECT country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_2, place_id, date,
      -- UNNEST an array of STRUCTs created from the original wide table's symptom columns.
      -- Here we demonstrate with a representative subset; view should be reusable and users will extend list as needed.
      s.symptom_name, s.symptom_value AS value_str
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_country_weekly`,
    UNNEST([
      STRUCT('symptom_abdominal_pain' AS symptom_name, symptom_abdominal_pain AS symptom_value),
      STRUCT('symptom_ageusia' AS symptom_name, symptom_ageusia AS symptom_value),
      STRUCT('symptom_anosmia' AS symptom_name, symptom_anosmia AS symptom_value)
    ]) AS s
    WHERE COALESCE(s.symptom_value, '') != ''
  )
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_2, place_id, date,
    symptom_name, NULL AS value_str, value_num
  FROM (
    -- sub_region_2_daily (numeric float columns)
    SELECT country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_2, place_id, CAST(date AS STRING) AS date,
      s.symptom_name, s.symptom_value AS value_num
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_2_daily`,
    UNNEST([
      STRUCT('symptom_Abdominal_pain' AS symptom_name, symptom_Abdominal_pain AS symptom_value),
      STRUCT('symptom_Ageusia' AS symptom_name, symptom_Ageusia AS symptom_value),
      STRUCT('symptom_Anosmia' AS symptom_name, symptom_Anosmia AS symptom_value)
    ]) AS s
    WHERE s.symptom_value IS NOT NULL
  )
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_2, place_id, date,
    symptom_name, value_str, NULL AS value_num
  FROM (
    -- other string-typed tables like country_daily, sub_region_1_weekly, sub_region_2_weekly
    SELECT country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_2, place_id, date,
      s.symptom_name, s.symptom_value AS value_str
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_1_daily`,
    UNNEST([
      STRUCT('symptom_abdominal_pain' AS symptom_name, symptom_abdominal_pain AS symptom_value),
      STRUCT('symptom_ageusia' AS symptom_name, symptom_ageusia AS symptom_value),
      STRUCT('symptom_anosmia' AS symptom_name, symptom_anosmia AS symptom_value)
    ]) AS s
    WHERE COALESCE(s.symptom_value, '') != ''
  )
) AS t
WHERE
  -- filter out NULL/empty/invalid numeric after attempted cast
  SAFE_CAST(
    NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(t.value_str, CAST(t.value_num AS STRING)), r'^\s*<\s*', ''), '') AS NUMERIC
  ) IS NOT NULL
clean_cast_symptom_value.description: Normalize and clean symptom value column: filter out NULL/empty values, cast string values to numeric where needed, and canonicalize country and sub-region name fields (e.g., standardize 'United States' / 'US' and state names). Preserve original place identifiers for disambiguation.

ca_county_population_latest.name: ca_county_population_latest
ca_county_population_latest.body_sql:
SELECT
  SUBSTR(geo_id, 10, 5) AS county_fips,
  /* The county name is not present in this table; keep as NULL so downstream can joinable by county_fips.
     If a name source is available, replace NULL with that lookup. */
  NULL AS county_name,
  total_pop,
  do_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2018_5yr` t
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY SUBSTR(geo_id, 10, 5) ORDER BY do_date DESC) = 1
ca_county_population_latest.description: Latest ACS five-year population row for each county in California from the county_2018_5yr table. Keep one row per county (by county FIPS) selecting the row with the maximum do_date so downstream uses the most recent estimate. This yields canonical county total population and identifiers.

ca_vaccine_facility_places.name: ca_vaccine_facility_places
ca_vaccine_facility_places.body_sql:
SELECT
  facility_place_id,
  facility_sub_region_2_code,
  facility_sub_region_2,
  facility_sub_region_1_code,
  facility_country_region_code
FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_all`
WHERE facility_country_region_code = 'US'
  AND facility_sub_region_1_code = 'US-CA'
ca_vaccine_facility_places.description: All vaccination facility place rows in the United States restricted to California. Each row represents one facility-place instance with its place identifier and county FIPS and county name as reported in the facility data.

county_vaccine_site_counts.name: county_vaccine_site_counts
county_vaccine_site_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.facility_sub_region_2_code AS facility_sub_region_2_code,
  COUNT(DISTINCT f.facility_place_id) AS vaccine_site_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_all` AS f
GROUP BY
  f.facility_sub_region_2_code
county_vaccine_site_counts.description: Aggregate count of distinct vaccination facility_place_id per county FIPS (facility_sub_region_2_code). Produces one row per county with the integer count of distinct sites; formed by grouping facility place rows by county identifier.

acs_county_basic_demographics.name: acs_county_basic_demographics
acs_county_basic_demographics.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Canonical county FIPS: use geo_id from ACS 2020 5-year county table.
  -- geo_id is like '0500000US06037' in some ACS datasets; for county FIPS extract last 5 digits.
  -- Keep county_name and state_name empty here because county-level name fields are not present
  -- in the provided table DDL. If another source (e.g., ca_county_population_latest) provides names,
  -- those can be joined outside the view. For this view we produce county_fips and canonical demographics.
  RIGHT(geo_id, 5) AS county_fips,
  NULL AS county_name,
  NULL AS state_name,
  median_age AS median_age,
  total_pop AS total_population
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2020_5yr`
WHERE
  median_age IS NOT NULL
  AND total_pop IS NOT NULL
acs_county_basic_demographics.description: One-row-per-county from the 2020 5-year ACS with canonicalized county identifiers and key demographic fields (median age and total population), excluding rows with NULLs in those key demographics.

covid_county_snapshot_by_date.name: covid_county_snapshot_by_date
covid_county_snapshot_by_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  county_fips_code AS county_fips,
  CAST(date AS DATE) AS date,
  confirmed_cases AS confirmed_cases,
  deaths AS deaths
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_usafacts.summary`
WHERE
  confirmed_cases IS NOT NULL
covid_county_snapshot_by_date.description: COVID-19 per-county snapshot for a given date with canonical county FIPS, confirmed case counts and death counts. This produces one row per county-date (date filter to be applied when querying). Excludes rows where confirmed cases is NULL.

zip_area_geography.name: zip_area_geography
zip_area_geography.body_sql:
SELECT
  zipcode AS zipcode,
  zipcode AS zipcode_geom,
  area_land_meters AS area_land_meters,
  area_water_meters AS area_water_meters,
  area_land_miles AS area_land_miles,
  area_water_miles AS area_water_miles,
  latitude AS latitude,
  longitude AS longitude,
  state_code AS state_code,
  state_name AS state_name,
  city AS city,
  county AS county
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area`
WHERE
  zipcode IS NOT NULL
  AND zipcode_geom IS NOT NULL
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
zip_area_geography.description: One row per ZIP code area that has non-null geometry and coordinates; canonical selection of zipcode area columns and removal of rows lacking geometry or lat/lon so they can be used for geographic computations.

population_by_zip_2010_filtered_gender_a.name: population_by_zip_2010_filtered_gender_age
population_by_zip_2010_filtered_gender_a.body_sql:
SELECT
  zipcode AS zipcode,
  gender AS gender,
  minimum_age AS minimum_age,
  maximum_age AS maximum_age,
  population AS population_count,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2010'
  AND gender IN ('male', 'female')
  AND NOT (minimum_age IS NULL AND maximum_age IS NULL)
population_by_zip_2010_filtered_gender_a.description: Population rows from the 2010 population_by_zip shard filtered to include only explicit male or female rows and excluding rows that represent age-range subtotal rows (i.e., only rows where minimum_age IS NULL AND maximum_age IS NULL). Keeps per-zipcode population detail rows for aggregation.

Use this to quickly filter or join downstream analyses that need population, age, sex, household, and basic housing counts. | Use for: Return demographic attributes for a set of tracts; Filter tracts by population or household counts; Map choropleths of population, race, or household metrics

grain: geo_id, rent_bucket (one row per tract per rent bucket)
tract_housing_rent_buckets_unpivoted.description: Unpivots the rent burden bucket columns into one row per tract + bucket so analyses can aggregate or rank rent burden categories. Use this when plotting distributions or computing shares across buckets per tract or across tracts. | Use for: Compute share of units in each rent bucket per tract or aggregated area; Plot rent burden distributions across tracts; Rank tracts by share in high rent burden buckets (e.g., rent_over_50_percent)

Exposes medians and a computed ratio of median_rent to median_income as 'median_rent_to_median_income_ratio' (note: medians are not additive; use this per-tract or when weighting appropriately). Useful for ranking or filtering tracts by affordability. | Use for: Identify tracts with high rent-to-income ratios; Rank tracts by median_income or median_rent; Filter tracts by median_income thresholds or percent income spent on rent

california_tract_income_change.name: california_tract_income_change
california_tract_income_change.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.geo_id AS geo_id,
  ct.tract_ce AS tract_ce,
  t2015.median_income AS median_household_income_2015,
  t2018.median_income AS median_household_income_2018,
  SAFE_CAST(t2018.median_income AS FLOAT64) - SAFE_CAST(t2015.median_income AS FLOAT64) AS income_change
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_california` AS ct
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr` AS a2015
ON ct.geo_id = a2015.geo_id
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr` AS a2018
ON ct.geo_id = a2018.geo_id
-- bring median_income from the 2015 and 2018 tract tables (column name median_income in those tables)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT geo_id, median_income FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr`
) AS t2015
ON ct.geo_id = t2015.geo_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT geo_id, median_income FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
) AS t2018
ON ct.geo_id = t2018.geo_id
california_tract_income_change.description: Joined relation that pairs California tract identifiers with their 2015 and 2018 median household incomes (one row per tract). Does not apply non-null or top-k filtering.

tract_geometries_and_attributes_2017.name: tract_geometries_and_attributes_2017
tract_geometries_and_attributes_2017.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.geo_id AS tract_geoid,
  ct.tract_geom AS tract_geom,
  SAFE_CAST(a.total_pop AS INT64) AS tract_population,
  ai.income_per_capita AS tract_individual_income,
  ST_AREA(ct.tract_geom) AS tract_area
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_illinois` AS ct
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2017_5yr` AS a
  ON ct.geo_id = a.geo_id
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2017_5yr` AS ai
  ON a.geo_id = ai.geo_id
WHERE
  ct.tract_geom IS NOT NULL
tract_geometries_and_attributes_2017.description: Select 2017 census tract geometries and key attributes (population and individual income) from the 2017 tract table, keeping one row per tract and filtering out rows with NULL geometries. Do not apply spatial joins or proximity filters here.

zip_code_geometries.name: zip_code_geometries
zip_code_geometries.body_sql:
SELECT
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  z.zip_code_geom AS zip_code_geom
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
zip_code_geometries.description: Select ZIP Code Tabulation Area geometries and identifiers. Do not apply the distance-from-point filter here; just provide one row per ZIP code with its geometry.

tract_zip_intersections_area_weights.name: tract_zip_intersections_area_weights
tract_zip_intersections_area_weights.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.geo_id AS tract_geoid,
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(t.tract_geom, z.zip_code_geom)) AS overlap_area,
  ST_AREA(t.tract_geom) AS tract_area,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(t.tract_geom, z.zip_code_geom)), ST_AREA(t.tract_geom)) AS weight
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.us_census_tracts_national` AS t
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
ON
  ST_INTERSECTS(t.tract_geom, z.zip_code_geom)
WHERE
  t.geo_id IS NOT NULL
  AND z.zip_code IS NOT NULL
  -- exclude null/zero tract area
  AND ST_AREA(t.tract_geom) IS NOT NULL
  AND ST_AREA(t.tract_geom) > 0
  -- exclude null/zero overlap area
  AND ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(t.tract_geom, z.zip_code_geom)) IS NOT NULL
  AND ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(t.tract_geom, z.zip_code_geom)) > 0
tract_zip_intersections_area_weights.description: Compute geometric intersections between tracts and ZIPs: for each non-empty tract–ZIP overlap compute overlap_area and the tract_area, then the weight = overlap_area / tract_area. Exclude pairs with zero or NULL overlap_area or NULL/zero tract_area. This produces one row per tract–zip pair with the fractional weight for allocating tract-level attributes into the ZIP.

One row per team-boxscore (same grain as source) exposing common measures and simple computed rates to simplify downstream queries. | Use for: Compute season/game level team summaries and trends; Compare team vs opponent boxscore stats; Filter team performances by conference/venue and compute aggregated metrics

team_game_winrank_running.name: team_game_winrank_running

  SUM(points_game) OVER (PARTITION BY team_id, season ORDER BY gametime, scheduled_date, game_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_points_in_season,
  SUM(CASE WHEN win THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY team_id, season ORDER BY gametime, scheduled_date, game_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_wins_in_season
