team_game_winrank_running.description: Per-team running game sequence with game-level rank and running totals. One row per team-game identical to mbb_teams_games_sr but with season-game_number (rank by gametime) and cumulative sums for points and wins to support top-K/time-series questions and running aggregates. | Use for: Compute per-team streaks or cumulative season stats; Select top-K games by season_game_number or get first/last N games per team; Plot running totals or compute moving averages per team

scoring_events_flagged.name: scoring_events_flagged
scoring_events_flagged.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_id,
  game_id,
  period,
  elapsed_time_sec,
  game_clock,
  event_description AS event_text,

  -- Prefer explicit points_scored when available in the source; otherwise infer from points_scored field
  -- here points_scored represents points attributed to the event (could be fractional in schema but treated as numeric)
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(points_scored AS NUMERIC) IS NOT NULL THEN
      -- If team_id equals home_id, attribute to home, else to away. If no team_id or home/away unknown, leave 0.
      CASE
        WHEN team_id = home_id THEN SAFE_CAST(points_scored AS INT64)
        ELSE 0
      END
    ELSE 0
  END AS points_scored_by_home,

  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(points_scored AS NUMERIC) IS NOT NULL THEN
      CASE
        WHEN team_id = away_id THEN SAFE_CAST(points_scored AS INT64)
        ELSE 0
      END
    ELSE 0
  END AS points_scored_by_away,

  -- Attempt to parse score from event_description like "12-10" or "12 - 10". If not present, leave NULL.
  -- Extract numeric home/away separated by hyphen where home score is first.
  CAST(
    NULLIF(REGEXP_EXTRACT(event_description, r'\\b(\\d{1,3})\\s*-\\s*(\\d{1,3})\\b'), '') AS INT64
  ) AS score_home,

  CAST(
    NULLIF(REGEXP_EXTRACT(event_description, r'\\b(\\d{1,3})\\s*-\\s*(\\d{1,3})\\b'), '') AS INT64
  ) AS score_away

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
WHERE
  -- Keep rows that are explicit scoring events (points_scored not null or >0) OR contain a visible score change in description
  (
    (points_scored IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(points_scored AS NUMERIC) != 0)
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(event_description, r'\\b\\d{1,3}\\s*-\\s*\\d{1,3}\\b')
  )
scoring_events_flagged.description: Normalized play events filtered to rows that are scoring plays or include a points delta (canonical boolean and numeric points scored by each side). This view standardizes detection of scoring plays using explicit points_home/points_away columns if present, otherwise infers from event_text or score changes between successive events.

pbp_shot_events_cohort.name: pbp_shot_events_cohort
pbp_shot_events_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  game_id,
  event_id,
  event_type,
  type AS event_subtype,
  scheduled_date,
  possession_team_id,
  -- offense_team_id is the team credited with the event (team_id field in source)
  team_id AS offense_team_id,
  -- defense_team_id derived as the opposing team in the same game:
  CASE
    WHEN team_id IS NOT NULL AND home_id IS NOT NULL AND away_id IS NOT NULL THEN
      CASE WHEN team_id = home_id THEN away_id
           WHEN team_id = away_id THEN home_id
           ELSE NULL END
    ELSE NULL
  END AS defense_team_id,
  player_id,
  shot_type,
  -- canonical numeric shot made: 1 for made, 0 for missed, NULL when unknown
  CASE WHEN shot_made = TRUE THEN 1
       WHEN shot_made = FALSE THEN 0
       ELSE NULL END AS shot_made_numeric,
  event_coord_x,
  event_coord_y,
  period,
  home_id AS home_team_id,
  away_id AS away_team_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
WHERE
  -- only shot attempt events (event_type indicates shot attempts in this dataset)
  LOWER(IFNULL(event_type, '')) LIKE '%shot%'
  -- require explicit shot type
  AND shot_type IS NOT NULL
  -- require coordinates
  AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
  AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
  -- require possession and team attribution info
  AND possession_team_id IS NOT NULL
  AND team_id IS NOT NULL
  -- require outcome identifier (shot_made not null) OR points_scored present to infer outcome;
  -- keep rows where at least one of those exists to be "unambiguous"
  AND (shot_made IS NOT NULL OR points_scored IS NOT NULL)
  -- limit to events that occurred before a provided date boundary: lift date boundary out of view
  -- consumer must provide @date_boundary parameter when querying the view; here we use scheduled_date < @date_boundary
  AND scheduled_date < @date_boundary
pbp_shot_events_cohort.description: Row-level subset of play-by-play rows restricted to shot attempt events and to rows that are unambiguous shots (have non-null shot type, non-null event coordinates, necessary possession/outcome identifiers) and limited to events that occurred before a given game date boundary. This cohort does not perform coordinate adjustments or aggregations; it only filters to valid shot attempt events.

shot_type_level_aggregates_per_game_even.name: shot_type_level_aggregates_per_game_event
shot_type_level_aggregates_per_game_even.body_sql:
SELECT
  shot_type AS shot_type,
  COUNT(1) AS attempts_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN shot_made THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS made_count,
  AVG(event_coord_x - 0) AS avg_adjusted_x,
  AVG(event_coord_y - 0) AS avg_adjusted_y
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
WHERE
  event_type = 'shot'
  AND shot_type IS NOT NULL
  AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
  AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  shot_type
shot_type_level_aggregates_per_game_even.description: Aggregate shot-level measures grouped by shot_type to compute counts of attempts and counts of made shots and average adjusted coordinates. This grouping yields the per-shot-type aggregates that can be averaged further or reported directly.

second_period_player_points.name: second_period_player_points
second_period_player_points.body_sql:
SELECT
  pbp.game_id,
  pbp.player_id,
  pbp.team_id,
  pbp.period,
  SUM(COALESCE(pbp.points_scored, 0)) AS points_in_period
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr` AS pbp
WHERE
  -- keep only valid player-attributed scoring events in the second period
  pbp.period = 2
  AND pbp.player_id IS NOT NULL
  AND pbp.points_scored IS NOT NULL
  -- event types that represent scoring (points_scored populated for made shots/plays)
  -- Note: table contains rows for many event types; filtering to rows with non-null points_scored and a player keeps scoring events.
GROUP BY
  pbp.game_id,
  pbp.player_id,
  pbp.team_id,
  pbp.period
second_period_player_points.description: One row per player-game indicating the player's total points scored during period 2 (second half/period) for that game. This filters to valid player-game events and computes per-game period-2 points but does not apply any date or threshold filters.

historical_tournament_games_details.name: historical_tournament_games_details
historical_tournament_games_details.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- historical_game_id: use a stable id from historical tournament table (concatenate season + game_date + win_team + lose_team to ensure uniqueness)
  CONCAT(CAST(season AS STRING), '_', CAST(days_from_epoch AS STRING), '_', COALESCE(win_team_id, ''), '_', COALESCE(lose_team_id, '')) AS historical_game_id,
  -- game_id: there is no direct Sportradar game_id in the historical tournament table, so keep NULL to allow outer joins; consumers can join by season + game_date + teams
  NULL AS game_id,
  season,
  game_date,
  -- Determine home/away by convention: the "win_team_id" and "lose_team_id" don't indicate home/away.
  -- We expose home_team_id and away_team_id as win_team_id / lose_team_id so downstream joins can reassign roles if needed.
  win_team_id AS home_team_id,
  lose_team_id AS away_team_id,
  -- tournament_name: use academic_year + round as a composite tournament identifier to keep literals out of the view
  CONCAT('NCAA_TOURNEY_', CAST(academic_year AS STRING)) AS tournament_name,
  CAST(round AS STRING) AS tournament_round
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
historical_tournament_games_details.description: One row per historical tournament game with game-level details (date, teams, tournament identifiers). This provides the set of tournament games to be filtered by date range and joined to team/market and player-derived cohorts.

bls_qcew_month3_construction_by_county_q.name: bls_qcew_month3_construction_by_county_quarter

county_yearly_avg_month3_construction.name: county_yearly_avg_month3_construction
county_yearly_avg_month3_construction.body_sql:
SELECT

  CAST(SUBSTR(b._TABLE_SUFFIX, 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year,

  AND b.month3_emplvl_23_construction IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  area_fips,
  year
HAVING
  COUNT(DISTINCT _TABLE_SUFFIX) = 4

Use to enrich time-series facts with series-level attributes like seasonal, industry codes, and series_title. Preserve series_id and key code columns for joins. | Use for: Join series metadata to facts to filter by industry/seasonal; list active series; identify series lifespan and attributes

cpsaat18_industry_summary.name: cpsaat18_industry_summary
cpsaat18_industry_summary.body_sql:

grain: one row per (year, sector, subsector, industry_group, industry)
cpsaat18_industry_summary.description: Aggregated summary of employed population by industry from cpsaat18: total employed (thousands) and demographic percentages. Useful for comparisons across years or industry groups and for computing derived demographic counts. | Use for: Compare employment levels by industry/year; compute demographic counts by multiplying percentages by totals; trend analysis across years

qcew_2007_q3_industry_unpivoted.name: qcew_2007_q3_industry_unpivoted
qcew_2007_q3_industry_unpivoted.body_sql:

  SPLIT(col, '_')[SAFE_OFFSET(2)] AS industry_code,
  CAST(val AS FLOAT64) AS metric_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2007_q3`,
UNNEST([
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting' AS col, qtrly_estabs_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_1024_professional_and_business_services' AS col, qtrly_estabs_1024_professional_and_business_services AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_61_educational_services' AS col, qtrly_estabs_61_educational_services AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_53_real_estate_and_rental_and_leasing' AS col, qtrly_estabs_53_real_estate_and_rental_and_leasing AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_1023_financial_activities' AS col, qtrly_estabs_1023_financial_activities AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_31_33_manufacturing' AS col, qtrly_estabs_31_33_manufacturing AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_23_construction' AS col, qtrly_estabs_23_construction AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_1029_unclassified' AS col, qtrly_estabs_1029_unclassified AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_71_arts_entertainment_and_recreation' AS col, qtrly_estabs_71_arts_entertainment_and_recreation AS val),

WHERE val IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per (geoid, column unpivoted) representing a single metric for an industry
qcew_2007_q3_industry_unpivoted.description: Unpivot selected industry columns from the wide QCEW 2007_q3 table into a tall format (industry_code, metric, value). Useful when analyses require comparing the same metric across industries or joining to county-level identifiers. This unpivots any qtrly_estabs_*, avg_wkly_wage_*, month3_emplvl_* columns into rows. | Use for: Compare establishments/employment/wages across industries within a county; join tall QCEW metrics to other geographic tables

bls_tech_industries_percent_by_race_2021.name: bls_tech_industries_percent_by_race_2021
bls_tech_industries_percent_by_race_2021.body_sql:

google_non_intersectional_representation.name: google_non_intersectional_representation_overall_rows

bls_cpsaat18_technology_industries_by_ye.name: bls_cpsaat18_technology_industries_by_year

dar_non_intersectional_representation_ro.name: dar_non_intersectional_representation_rows

overall_workforce_year_values.name: overall_workforce_year_values
overall_workforce_year_values.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(report_year AS INT64) AS report_year,
  workforce,
  AVG(race_asian) AS race_asian,
  AVG(race_black) AS race_black,
  AVG(race_hispanic_latinx) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
  AVG(race_native_american) AS race_native_american,
  AVG(race_white) AS race_white,
  AVG(gender_us_women) AS gender_us_women,
  AVG(gender_us_men) AS gender_us_men,
  AVG(gender_global_women) AS gender_global_women,
  AVG(gender_global_men) AS gender_global_men
FROM (
  -- Combine available normalized representation tables that contain 'Overall' workforce rows.
  SELECT report_year, workforce, race_asian, race_black, race_hispanic_latinx, race_native_american, race_white,
         NULL AS gender_us_women, NULL AS gender_us_men, NULL AS gender_global_women, NULL AS gender_global_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_intersectional_representation`
  WHERE workforce = 'Overall'

  UNION ALL

  SELECT report_year, workforce, race_asian, race_black, race_hispanic_latinx, race_native_american, race_white,
         NULL AS gender_us_women, NULL AS gender_us_men, NULL AS gender_global_women, NULL AS gender_global_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_intersectional_hiring`
  WHERE workforce = 'Overall'

  UNION ALL

  SELECT report_year, workforce, race_asian, race_black, race_hispanic_latinx, race_native_american, race_white,
         gender_us_women, gender_us_men, gender_global_women, gender_global_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation`
  WHERE workforce = 'Overall'
) combined
GROUP BY report_year, workforce
overall_workforce_year_values.description: Aggregate normalized representation rows to one row per report_year and workforce for the 'Overall' cohort by collapsing org/location granularity (e.g., averaging or otherwise combining as appropriate). Produces one row per report_year x workforce with the numeric percentage columns.

crime_events_core.name: crime_events_core
crime_events_core.body_sql:
SELECT

  block,

grain: unique_key (one row per reported crime incident)
crime_events_core.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of the crime table preserving identifiers, timestamps, location and key attributes. Use as a base for aggregations, joins, and time-series analyses of crimes. | Use for: Counts of crimes by time period or area; Filtering crimes by type/attribute and joining to other datasets; Spatial analyses using crime latitude/longitude

crime_counts_by_day_type.name: crime_counts_by_day_type
crime_counts_by_day_type.body_sql:

FROM (

    date AS event_timestamp,
    primary_type,
    community_area,
    district
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
)
GROUP BY day, primary_type, community_area, district
grain: day, primary_type, community_area, district (one row per combination)
crime_counts_by_day_type.description: Daily counts of crimes grouped by date (day) and primary type, preserving community area and district for downstream joins and ranking. Useful for time series, trend detection and top-k by day/type. | Use for: Daily trend of crime counts by type and area; Top crime types per community area or district on a given day (use a rank CTE on top); Moving averages or seasonality analyses at daily granularity

taxi_trips_core.name: taxi_trips_core
taxi_trips_core.body_sql:

Use as a canonical base for trip-level analyses and downstream aggregations or joins. | Use for: Average fare, tips, or trip distance by company or payment type; Time-series of trip counts or revenue; Spatial analyses of pickups/dropoffs by community area

taxi_daily_agg_by_company.name: taxi_daily_agg_by_company
taxi_daily_agg_by_company.body_sql:

  DATE(trip_start_timestamp) AS day,
  company,
  COUNT(1) AS trips_count,

  SUM(IFNULL(fare, 0)) AS total_fare,

FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
GROUP BY day, company
grain: day, company (one row per company per day)
taxi_daily_agg_by_company.description: Daily aggregated metrics per taxi company (or NULL for missing company) including counts, sums and averages for fare, tips, trip_miles and trip_seconds. Useful for revenue/time trend comparisons and ranking companies. | Use for: Rank companies by revenue or trips over time; Compare tipping behavior across companies or days; Compute moving averages or growth rates of company revenue

crime_to_pickup_area_joinable.name: crime_to_pickup_area_joinable

  primary_type,
  community_area AS crime_community_area,
  district,
  latitude AS crime_latitude,
  longitude AS crime_longitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
crime_to_pickup_area_joinable.description: Joinable relation projecting crime records keyed by community_area and date to enable safe aggregation joins with taxi trips by pickup_community_area and day. Designed to be aggregated further to avoid row explosion when joining two event tables. | Use for: Aggregate join with taxi daily pickups by community area and day (e.g., compare counts); Spatial proximity joins using crime_latitude/longitude to pickup coordinates; Time-windowed correlation of crime counts vs taxi activity

taxi_pickups_by_day_area.name: taxi_pickups_by_day_area
taxi_pickups_by_day_area.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(trip_start_timestamp) AS day,
  pickup_community_area,
  COUNT(1) AS trips_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(trip_total, 0)) AS total_revenue,
  AVG(IFNULL(trip_miles, 0)) AS avg_miles
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
GROUP BY day, pickup_community_area
grain: day, pickup_community_area (one row per area per day)
taxi_pickups_by_day_area.description: Daily counts and sums of taxi pickups aggregated by pickup community area, preserving day and area to join with crime aggregates. Keeps measures useful for normalization (trips_count, total_revenue). | Use for: Compare daily taxi activity to daily crime counts by community area; Compute ratios like crimes per taxi trip in an area/day; Identify area-days with unusually high taxi revenue or trip counts

top_crime_types_by_area_rank.name: top_crime_types_by_area_rank
top_crime_types_by_area_rank.body_sql:

  primary_type,
  community_area,
  crimes_count,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY day, community_area ORDER BY crimes_count DESC) AS type_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE(date) AS day,
    primary_type,
    community_area,
    COUNT(1) AS crimes_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  GROUP BY day, primary_type, community_area
)
grain: day, community_area, primary_type (one row per type per area per day)
top_crime_types_by_area_rank.description: Pre-ranked crime type counts by community area and day. Exposes a rank column so downstream queries can select top-N crime types per area/day by filtering rank <= N. Useful for top-k and leaderboard queries. | Use for: Top N crime types per community area on a given day or date range; Leaderboards of crime types for dashboards (use WHERE type_rank <= N)

taxi_company_revenue_rank.name: taxi_company_revenue_rank
taxi_company_revenue_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  company,
  trips_count,
  total_revenue,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY day ORDER BY total_revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE(trip_start_timestamp) AS day,
    company,
    COUNT(1) AS trips_count,
    SUM(IFNULL(trip_total, 0)) AS total_revenue
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`

grain: day, company (one row per company per day)
taxi_company_revenue_rank.description: Ranked daily revenue per taxi company. Provides company daily revenue and rank within each day so consumers can easily filter top companies by revenue for any day. | Use for: Top-N companies by revenue for dashboard daily snapshots; Time-series of rank changes for companies

crime_events_weekly_running_total.name: crime_events_weekly_running_total
crime_events_weekly_running_total.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  primary_type,
  community_area,
  crimes_count,
  SUM(crimes_count) OVER (
    PARTITION BY primary_type, community_area
    ORDER BY day
    ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS running_7day_crimes
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE(date) AS day,
    primary_type,
    community_area,
    COUNT(1) AS crimes_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  GROUP BY day, primary_type, community_area
)
ORDER BY primary_type, community_area, day
grain: day, primary_type, community_area (one row per group per day)
crime_events_weekly_running_total.description: 7-day running total of crimes per primary_type and community_area using event date. Useful for smoothing daily volatility and detecting trends. Exposes running_total so downstream queries can filter or chart moving sums. | Use for: Trend detection using 7-day moving sums; Comparing recent crime activity across areas or types

distinct_crime_types.name: distinct_crime_types

distinct_taxi_companies.name: distinct_taxi_companies
distinct_taxi_companies.body_sql:

FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`

distinct_taxi_companies.description: Distinct list of taxi companies with counts of trips. Useful for UI lists and quick popularity measures. | Use for: Populate company filters in dashboards; Assess company coverage in dataset

spatial_nearest_taxi_pickups.name: spatial_nearest_taxi_pickups
spatial_nearest_taxi_pickups.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS trip_id,
  taxi_id,
  pickup_latitude,
  pickup_longitude,
  pickup_location,
  pickup_community_area,

WHERE pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
grain: trip_id (one row per taxi trip with non-null pickup coordinates)
spatial_nearest_taxi_pickups.description: For each crime event (with latitude/longitude), returns the N nearest taxi pickup locations within a configurable neighborhood when joined with taxi trips aggregated by pickup location. This CTE projects pickup coordinates and preserves taxi identifiers so consumers can perform distance calculations or nearest-neighbor joins downstream. Note: this CTE does not perform the spatial join itself to avoid explosion; it prepares taxi pickup locations for downstream spatial joins using ST_DISTANCE or haversine. | Use for: Spatial nearest-neighbor joins between crimes and taxi pickups; Compute distances from crimes to nearest taxi pickups and analyze temporal proximity

crime_latest_by_case.name: crime_latest_by_case
crime_latest_by_case.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  case_number,
  date,
  primary_type,
  description,
  location_description,
  arrest,
  domestic,
  updated_on,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY case_number ORDER BY updated_on DESC) AS rn
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
grain: case_number, rn (one row per case_number per version; rn=1 is latest)
crime_latest_by_case.description: Latest crime record per case_number using updated_on as the versioning column. Exposes a row_number so downstream consumers can select the most recent record per case_number. Useful when case_number may have multiple updates. | Use for: Select the latest record per case_number for deduplication; Auditing or change-tracking workflows that need the most recent incident data

taxi_trips_filtered_duration.name: taxi_trips_filtered_duration
taxi_trips_filtered_duration.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS trip_id,
  trip_seconds,
  fare
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
WHERE
  trip_seconds IS NOT NULL
  AND fare IS NOT NULL
  -- liftable literals (example typical bounds): keep rows with durations between 60 seconds (1 min) and 6 hours (21600 sec)
  AND trip_seconds BETWEEN 60 AND 21600
taxi_trips_filtered_duration.description: Subset of taxi trips restricted to non-null trips with trip_seconds within a valid range (canonical trip-level cohort). This filters rows to only trips that have trip_seconds and fare values and are within the typical duration bounds; it does not apply any further aggregation or quantile bucketing.

taxi_trips_duration_seconds_normalized.name: taxi_trips_duration_seconds_normalized
taxi_trips_duration_seconds_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS trip_id,
  -- canonicalize trip_seconds to NUMERIC: attempt safe cast, else NULL; also clip to non-negative and a practical upper bound if present as literal variables can be applied downstream.
  -- Here we coerce INT64/FLOAT64/STRING variations to NUMERIC using SAFE_CAST; ensure non-negative by greatest(0,...).
  -- Use NULL when cast fails.
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(trip_seconds AS NUMERIC) IS NOT NULL THEN GREATEST(CAST(0 AS NUMERIC), SAFE_CAST(trip_seconds AS NUMERIC))
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(CAST(trip_seconds AS FLOAT64) AS NUMERIC) IS NOT NULL THEN GREATEST(CAST(0 AS NUMERIC), SAFE_CAST(CAST(trip_seconds AS FLOAT64) AS NUMERIC))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS trip_seconds_numeric,
  -- canonicalize fare to NUMERIC similarly; fares should be non-negative
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(fare AS NUMERIC) IS NOT NULL THEN GREATEST(CAST(0 AS NUMERIC), SAFE_CAST(fare AS NUMERIC))
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(CAST(fare AS FLOAT64) AS NUMERIC) IS NOT NULL THEN GREATEST(CAST(0 AS NUMERIC), SAFE_CAST(CAST(fare AS FLOAT64) AS NUMERIC))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS fare_numeric
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
taxi_trips_duration_seconds_normalized.description: Normalized per-trip projection that ensures trip_seconds is numeric and within the externally constrained bounds (clipping or canonical cast to numeric). This prepares trip-level numeric duration and fare fields for downstream numeric operations (e.g., converting seconds to minutes, averaging). Does not filter out rows by literal bounds; canonicalizes types and nulls.

taxi_trips_in_duration_cohort_0_3600.name: taxi_trips_in_duration_cohort_0_3600
taxi_trips_in_duration_cohort_0_3600.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS trip_id,
  trip_seconds,
  fare
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
WHERE
  trip_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600
taxi_trips_in_duration_cohort_0_3600.description: Cohort of taxi trips with trip_seconds between 0 and 3600 inclusive. This is the question-specific filtered set of trip-level rows to be analyzed (still one row per trip).

taxi_trips_duration_quantiles.name: taxi_trips_duration_quantiles
taxi_trips_duration_quantiles.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS trip_id,
  trip_seconds,
  fare,
  -- quantile_group_id: equal-frequency buckets based on trip_seconds.
  -- NOTE: number_of_quantiles should be provided by downstream query as a literal replacement.
  CAST(NTILE(@number_of_quantiles) OVER (ORDER BY trip_seconds) AS INT64) AS quantile_group_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
taxi_trips_duration_quantiles.description: Assigns each trip into an equal-frequency quantile bucket based on trip_seconds (trip-level window/rank operation). Produces a quantile_group_id per trip for downstream group aggregations. This view does not aggregate beyond assigning the quantile id.

taxi_trips_2018_filtered.name: taxi_trips_2018_filtered
taxi_trips_2018_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS trip_id,
  company,
  trip_start_timestamp,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', trip_start_timestamp) AS trip_month
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
WHERE
  trip_start_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP('2018-01-01')
  AND trip_start_timestamp < TIMESTAMP('2019-01-01')
  AND company IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(company) <> ''
taxi_trips_2018_filtered.description: All taxi trip rows that started in calendar year 2018, excluding trips with NULL or empty company values. Keeps raw trip-level columns and a normalized month string (YYYY-MM) for the trip start timestamp.

trips_duration_filtered.name: trips_duration_filtered
trips_duration_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key into output as trip_id per spec
  unique_key AS trip_id,
  -- preserve original trip_seconds and fare
  trip_seconds,
  fare,
  -- compute whole-minute duration from seconds, integer division
  CAST(FLOOR(GREATEST(0, SAFE_DIVIDE(trip_seconds, 60))) AS INT64) AS duration_minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
WHERE
  -- restrict to trips whose whole-minute duration is between 1 and 50 inclusive
  CAST(FLOOR(GREATEST(0, SAFE_DIVIDE(trip_seconds, 60))) AS INT64) BETWEEN 1 AND 50
trips_duration_filtered.description: Subset of trips_base_cohort that restricts trips to those whose whole-minute duration is between 1 and 50 inclusive.

trips_ntile_by_duration.name: trips_ntile_by_duration
trips_ntile_by_duration.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- lift question-specific literals out of the view (none here)
  tt.unique_key AS trip_id,
  -- duration in minutes from trip_seconds, preserving original precision
  SAFE_DIVIDE(tt.trip_seconds, 60.0) AS duration_minutes,
  tt.fare AS fare,
  -- assign ntile bucket across all trips ordered by duration_minutes
  NTILE(@num_buckets) OVER (ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(tt.trip_seconds, 60.0)) AS ntile_bucket
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips` AS tt
trips_ntile_by_duration.description: Assign an NTILE bucket (1..N) over trips ordered by duration_minutes to partition trips into equal-sized quantiles; preserve original trip-level fare and duration for aggregation.

crime_datetime_normalized.name: crime_datetime_normalized
crime_datetime_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(c.unique_key AS INT64) AS id,
  -- normalize/parse the timestamp to a DATE (date_parsed) preserving timezone if present
  DATE(TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(c.date, DAY)) AS date_parsed,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE(TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(c.date, DAY))) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATE(TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(c.date, DAY))) AS month
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime` AS c
crime_datetime_normalized.description: Normalize and extract calendar date parts from the crime date/timestamp field: ensure a parsed date/datetime and produce year and month integer columns for grouping.

crime_type_cohort.name: crime_type_cohort
crime_type_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS id,
  primary_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
WHERE
  primary_type = @primary_type
crime_type_cohort.description: Subset of crimes for a given primary_type value (cohort per incident). This defines the cohort of incidents by type but does not apply year or month filtering.

monthly_incident_counts.name: monthly_incident_counts
monthly_incident_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  primary_type,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month,
  COUNT(1) AS incident_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
GROUP BY
  primary_type,
  year,
  month
monthly_incident_counts.description: Aggregate incidents to counts per calendar year and month for each primary_type. One row per (primary_type, year, month) with the count of incidents in that bucket.

crime_motor_vehicle_theft_rows.name: crime_motor_vehicle_theft_rows
crime_motor_vehicle_theft_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS id,
  date AS date,
  primary_type AS primary_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
WHERE
  primary_type IN ('MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT')

semantic_filters.primary_type: ILIKE pattern for motor vehicle theft variants (caller will apply exact literals)

crime_motor_vehicle_theft_rows.description: One row per crime event limited to motor vehicle theft related primary_type values; keeps original crime table columns for downstream processing.

crime_date_normalized.name: crime_date_normalized
crime_date_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(c.unique_key AS INT64) AS id,
  c.date AS date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.date) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM c.date) AS month
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime` AS c
crime_date_normalized.description: Normalize and project date-related fields (year and month integers) from crime event rows to enable calendar-based grouping; preserves crime id for one-row-per-crime.

motor_vehicle_theft_events_by_year_month.name: motor_vehicle_theft_events_by_year_month
motor_vehicle_theft_events_by_year_month.body_sql:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month,
  COUNT(1) AS motor_theft_count
FROM

WHERE

GROUP BY
  year,
  month
motor_vehicle_theft_events_by_year_month.description: Count motor vehicle theft events grouped at the calendar year and month level (one row per year-month with event count). Depends on motor-vehicle-theft filtered crime rows and normalized date fields.

trade_row_level_normalized.name: trade_row_level_normalized
trade_row_level_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key column: preserve OrderID as string (nullable)
  CAST(OrderID AS STRING) AS OrderID,

  -- LastPx: ensure numeric (FLOAT64) and NULL when missing/non-numeric
  SAFE_CAST(LastPx AS FLOAT64) AS LastPx,

  -- StrikePrice: ensure numeric (FLOAT64)
  SAFE_CAST(StrikePrice AS FLOAT64) AS StrikePrice,

  -- strategy: canonicalized derived string. We don't apply business filters here;
  -- create a normalized strategy label from TargetCompID and SenderCompID presence.
  -- Lifted literals: none hard-coded for business logic; use simple rule to avoid NULLs.
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(TRIM(CONCAT(
      IFNULL(TargetCompID, ''),
      CASE WHEN TargetCompID IS NOT NULL AND SenderCompID IS NOT NULL THEN '|' ELSE '' END,
      IFNULL(SenderCompID, '')
    )), ''),
    'unknown'
  ) AS strategy,

  -- sides: keep the raw Sides array but canonicalize its nested fields (ensure types and nulls).
  ARRAY(
    SELECT AS STRUCT
      -- Side direction as string
      SAFE_CAST(s.Side AS STRING) AS Side,
      -- OrderID under side (if present) as string
      SAFE_CAST(s.OrderID AS STRING) AS OrderID,
      -- PartyIDs: normalize nested repeated structs
      ARRAY(
        SELECT AS STRUCT
          SAFE_CAST(p.PartyID AS STRING) AS PartyID,
          SAFE_CAST(p.PartyIDSource AS STRING) AS PartyIDSource,
          SAFE_CAST(p.PartyRole AS STRING) AS PartyRole
        FROM UNNEST(s.PartyIDs) AS p
      ) AS PartyIDs
    FROM UNNEST(Sides) AS s
  ) AS sides

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`
trade_row_level_normalized.description: One normalized row per trade capture report row, canonicalizing and exposing scalar fields needed for analysis (e.g., OrderID, LastPx, StrikePrice, strategy, and the raw Sides array). Convert/clean types and ensure NULLs are consistent; do not filter by specific literal values here.

trade_side_exploded.name: trade_side_exploded
trade_side_exploded.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.OrderID,
  OFFSET AS side_index,
  s.Side AS Side,
  s.OrderID AS side_OrderID
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` t,
  UNNEST(t.Sides) AS s WITH OFFSET AS OFFSET
trade_side_exploded.description: Explode the Sides array/struct from trade rows so each output row is one side associated with a trade, exposing the Side value and any side-level OrderID link fields. Keep all side rows (no filtering by side value here).

trade_with_long_side_flag.name: trade_with_long_side_flag
trade_with_long_side_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.OrderID AS OrderID,
  EXISTS(
    SELECT 1
    FROM UNNEST(t.sides) AS s
    WHERE s.Side = 'long' AND (s.OrderID IS NULL OR s.OrderID = t.OrderID)
  ) AS has_long_side
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` AS t
GROUP BY t.OrderID, t.sides
trade_with_long_side_flag.description: For each trade (one row per OrderID), indicate whether the trade has at least one associated side row whose Side = 'long' and (optionally) whose side_OrderID matches the trade OrderID. Do not apply other filters; produce a boolean flag or marker.

trade_intrinsic_values.name: trade_intrinsic_values
trade_intrinsic_values.body_sql:
SELECT
  tr.OrderID AS OrderID,
  CASE
    WHEN tr.LastPx IS NOT NULL AND tr.StrikePrice IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_SUBTRACT(tr.LastPx, tr.StrikePrice)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS intrinsic_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` AS tr
trade_intrinsic_values.description: Per trade row, compute the intrinsic value = (LastPx - StrikePrice) only for rows where both LastPx and StrikePrice are non-NULL. Do not filter by side or strategy here; retain one row per trade with the computed intrinsic value.

trade_reports_unnested_sides.name: trade_reports_unnested_sides
trade_reports_unnested_sides.body_sql:
SELECT
  TradeReportID,
  MaturityDate,
  TargetCompID,
  Symbol,
  LastPx,
  StrikePrice,
  -- Unnest Sides array to produce one row per TradeReportID + Side
  s.Side AS Side
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`,
  UNNEST(Sides) AS s
trade_reports_unnested_sides.description: Unnest Sides (and keep associated PartyIDs if needed) so there is one row per original trade report per side entry. Preserve original trade-level fields for downstream projection.

plot_basic_dim.name: plot_basic_dim
plot_basic_dim.body_sql:
SELECT
  plot_sequence_number,
  survey_sequence_number,
  county_sequence_number,
  previous_plot_sequence_number,
  plot_inventory_year AS inventory_year,
  plot_state_code AS state_code,
  plot_state_code_name AS state_name,
  plot_survey_unit_code AS survey_unit_code,
  plot_county_code AS county_code,
  plot_phase_2_plot_number AS phase_2_plot_number,
  plot_status_code AS status_code,
  plot_status_code_name AS status_name,
  plot_nonsampled_reason_code AS nonsampled_reason_code,
  plot_nonsampled_reason_code_name AS nonsampled_reason_name,
  measurement_year,
  measurement_month,
  measurement_month_name,
  measurement_day,
  remeasurement_period,
  sample_kind_code,
  sample_kind_code_name,
  plot_design_code,
  horizontal_distance_to_improved_road_code AS distance_to_road_code,
  horizontal_distance_to_improved_road_code_name AS distance_to_road_name,
  water_on_plot_code,
  water_on_plot_code_name AS water_on_plot_name,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  elevation,
  type_of_annual_volume_growth_code AS annual_volume_growth_code,
  type_of_annual_volume_growth_code_name AS annual_volume_growth_name,
  type_of_annual_mortality_volume_code AS annual_mortality_volume_code,
  type_of_annual_mortality_volume_code_name AS annual_mortality_volume_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot`
plot_basic_dim.description: Normalized/cleaned plot-level dimension with canonical column names for joining and descriptive filters. Use this as the base plot relation for joins, mapping, and cohort selection. | Use for: Map plots (lat/lon) and join to strata or counties; Filter plots by measurement year, state, status, or sample kind; Aggregate elevation or remeasurement_period by state or survey unit

population_stratum_assign_bridge.name: population_stratum_assign_bridge
population_stratum_assign_bridge.body_sql:
SELECT
  stratum_assign_sequence_number,
  stratum_sequence_number,
  plot_sequence_number,
  state_code,
  inventory_year,
  survey_unit_code,
  county_code,
  phase_2_plot_number,
  region_or_station_code,
  evaluation_identifier,
  estimation_unit,
  stratum_code,
  stratum_assign_created_by,
  stratum_assign_created_date,
  stratum_assign_created_in_instance,
  stratum_assign_modified_by,
  stratum_assign_modified_date,
  stratum_assign_modified_in_instance
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_stratum_assign`
population_stratum_assign_bridge.description: Bridge relation exposing plot-to-stratum assignment records and assignment metadata. Use when you need to relate plots to strata, filter by inventory year, or analyze assignment counts and versions. | Use for: Count plots per stratum or estimation unit by inventory_year; Join with plot_basic_dim to get plot attributes for assigned strata; Identify most-recent assignment per plot using modified_date

plot_with_stratum_join.name: plot_with_stratum_join
plot_with_stratum_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  psa.stratum_assign_sequence_number,
  psa.stratum_sequence_number,
  psa.plot_sequence_number,
  psa.inventory_year AS assignment_inventory_year,
  psa.stratum_code,
  psa.estimation_unit,
  psa.region_or_station_code,
  psa.evaluation_identifier,
  psa.stratum_assign_created_date,
  psa.stratum_assign_modified_date,
  p.plot_sequence_number AS _plot_sequence_number,
  p.survey_sequence_number,
  p.county_sequence_number,
  p.plot_inventory_year AS plot_inventory_year,
  p.plot_state_code AS plot_state_code,
  p.plot_state_code_name AS plot_state_name,
  p.plot_survey_unit_code AS plot_survey_unit_code,
  p.plot_county_code AS plot_county_code,
  p.plot_phase_2_plot_number AS plot_phase_2_plot_number,
  p.plot_status_code AS plot_status_code,
  p.plot_status_code_name AS plot_status_name,
  p.measurement_year,
  p.latitude,
  p.longitude,
  p.elevation,
  p.remeasurement_period
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_stratum_assign` AS psa
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot` AS p
ON psa.plot_sequence_number = p.plot_sequence_number
grain: one row per population_stratum_assign (assignment) with attached plot attributes
plot_with_stratum_join.description: Denormalized join of plots to their stratum assignments. Keeps one row per assignment (bridge grain) and preserves both plot and assignment identifiers and descriptive attributes for downstream aggregation or filtering. | Use for: Spatial distribution of strata (map assignment lat/lon); Compare assignment_inventory_year to plot_inventory_year or measurement_year; Aggregate plot counts by stratum_code, estimation_unit, or state

plots_ranked_by_measurement_year.name: plots_ranked_by_measurement_year
plots_ranked_by_measurement_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  plot_sequence_number,
  measurement_year,
  measurement_month,
  measurement_day,
  -- construct a measurement_date where possible for ordering
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(measurement_year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(measurement_month, 1) AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(measurement_day, 1) AS STRING),2,'0'))) AS measurement_date,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY plot_sequence_number ORDER BY SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(measurement_year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(measurement_month, 1) AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(measurement_day, 1) AS STRING),2,'0'))) DESC NULLS LAST) AS measurement_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot`
grain: one row per plot measurement (plot_sequence_number + original measurement row), ranked by recency
plots_ranked_by_measurement_year.description: Per-plot ranking of measurements by measurement date (most recent first). Useful to pick latest measurement per plot or to filter top-K recent measurements per plot. Exposes rank so downstream queries can apply WHERE measurement_rank <= K. | Use for: Select latest measurement per plot (WHERE measurement_rank = 1); Find plots with multiple measurements and analyze recency distribution; Join latest measurements to stratum assignments

elevation_stats_by_state_surveyunit.name: elevation_stats_by_state_surveyunit
elevation_stats_by_state_surveyunit.body_sql:
SELECT
  plot_state_code AS state_code,
  plot_state_code_name AS state_name,
  plot_survey_unit_code AS survey_unit_code,
  COUNT(*) AS plot_count,
  MIN(elevation) AS min_elevation,
  MAX(elevation) AS max_elevation,
  AVG(elevation) AS avg_elevation,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(elevation, 2)[OFFSET(1)] AS median_elevation_approx
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot`
WHERE elevation IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY plot_state_code, plot_state_code_name, plot_survey_unit_code
elevation_stats_by_state_surveyunit.description: Aggregated elevation statistics (count, min, max, avg, median_approx) per state and survey unit. Use for summary reports and as inputs to maps or stratified analyses. | Use for: Compare elevation distributions across states or survey units; Identify survey units with few sampled plots (low plot_count); Use median/avg elevation as covariates in ecological analyses

evaluation_groups_with_type.name: evaluation_groups_with_type
evaluation_groups_with_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.evaluation_group AS population_evaluation_group_id,
  g.evaluation_group_sequence_number,
  e.evaluation_identifier AS population_evaluation_id,
  t.evaluation_type AS evaluation_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_group` g
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation` e
ON
  g.evaluation_group_sequence_number = e.evaluation_group_sequence_number
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type` t
ON
  e.evaluation_sequence_number = t.evaluation_sequence_number
  AND g.evaluation_group_sequence_number = t.evaluation_group_sequence_number
evaluation_groups_with_type.description: Denormalize evaluation group with its evaluation and evaluation type so each evaluation_group row includes the linked population_evaluation and population_evaluation_type rows (including evaluation_type code).

evaluation_type_lookup.name: evaluation_type_lookup
evaluation_type_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(evaluation_type_sequence_number AS INT64) AS population_evaluation_type_id,
  evaluation_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type`
evaluation_type_lookup.description: Lookup of evaluation type descriptive name by id.

evaluations_expcurr.name: evaluations_expcurr
evaluations_expcurr.body_sql:
SELECT
  pe.evaluation_sequence_number AS evaluation_id,
  pe.evaluation_group_sequence_number AS evaluation_group_id,
  pet.evaluation_type AS evaluation_type,
  pe.report_year_name AS inventory_year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation` AS pe
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type` AS pet
ON
  pe.evaluation_sequence_number = pet.evaluation_sequence_number
WHERE
  pet.evaluation_type = 'EXPCURR'
evaluations_expcurr.description: Select evaluation records that are of type 'EXPCURR' and expose their keys for joining to populations/strata/plots. This defines the set of evaluations to include in all downstream calculations.

population_stratum_expansion_adjustments.name: population_stratum_expansion_adjustments
population_stratum_expansion_adjustments.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- population id: use population.stratum_assign_sequence_number (string) as the population identifier
  psa.stratum_assign_sequence_number AS population_id,
  -- stratum sequence id from the population_stratum table
  ps.stratum_sequence_number AS stratum_sequence_number,
  -- plot sequence number from the stratum assignment bridge (plot linked to stratum)
  psa.plot_sequence_number AS plot_sequence_number,
  -- expansion factor: prefer POP_STRATUM.expansion_factor, fall back to POPULATION.expansion_factor if present
  COALESCE(ps.expansion_factor, pop.expansion_factor) AS expansion_factor,
  -- adjustment factor for subplot: pull from POP_STRATUM.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot (alias to required name)
  ps.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot AS adj_factor_subp,
  -- adjustment factor for macroplot: pull from POP_STRATUM.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot
  ps.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot AS adj_factor_macr,
  -- stratum assignment id (keep the assignment sequence as the unique id for the grain)
  psa.stratum_assign_sequence_number AS stratum_assign_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_stratum_assign` AS psa
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_stratum` AS ps
ON
  psa.stratum_sequence_number = ps.stratum_sequence_number
  AND psa.estimation_unit = ps.estimation_unit
  AND psa.region_or_station_code = ps.region_or_station_code
  AND psa.evaluation_identifier = ps.evaluation_identifier
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population` AS pop
ON
  psa.stratum_assign_sequence_number = pop.stratum_assign_sequence_number
population_stratum_expansion_adjustments.description: Provide expansion and adjustment factors at the stratum/plot level so they can be joined to condition rows: include expansion_factor (expns or expansion_factor), adjustment factor for subplot and macroplot, and stratum/plot sequence identifiers. This view maps each stratum (and its assignment to plots) to the numeric factors used in area calculations.

sterna_paradisaea_occurrences_filtered.name: sterna_paradisaea_occurrences_filtered
sterna_paradisaea_occurrences_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  occurrenceid,
  eventdate,
  scientificname,
  decimallatitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
WHERE
  eventdate IS NOT NULL
  AND decimallatitude > 40
sterna_paradisaea_occurrences_filtered.description: Row-level cohort of occurrences for the species of interest, filtered to records that are valid occurrences (non-null eventdate) and with decimallatitude > 40. Do not apply month or year grouping here.

occurrence_date_and_year_normalized.name: occurrence_date_and_year_normalized
occurrence_date_and_year_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  occurrenceid,
  DATE(eventdate) AS event_date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE(eventdate)) AS year,

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
WHERE
  occurrenceid IS NOT NULL
occurrence_date_and_year_normalized.description: Normalize eventdate into DATE, extract calendar year and month as separate columns and produce a canonical date-only column for grouping. Keep one row per occurrence.

tropical_storm_track_points.name: tropical_storm_track_points
tropical_storm_track_points.body_sql:

WHERE

  -- lift any question-specific literals out of the view (e.g., wind threshold) so none are hard-coded here

variants_core_identifiers.name: variants_core_identifiers
variants_core_identifiers.body_sql:
SELECT
  reference_name,
  start_position,
  end_position,
  reference_bases,
  alternate_bases AS alternate_bases_struct,
  -- AC/AF/nhomalt and raw fields live inside the elements of the alternate_bases ARRAY.
  -- Extract values from the first element of the array when present; use NULLs otherwise.
  (SELECT alt_struct.AC FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS ac,
  (SELECT alt_struct.AF FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS af,
  (SELECT alt_struct.n_alt_alleles FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS nhomalt,
  (SELECT alt_struct.AC_raw FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS ac_raw,
  (SELECT alt_struct.AF_raw FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS af_raw,
  (SELECT alt_struct.nhomalt_raw FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS nhomalt_raw,
  (SELECT alt_struct.allele_type FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS allele_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.gnomAD.v2_1_1_exomes__chr14`
grain: one row per variant locus (reference_name + start_position + end_position + reference_bases + alternate_bases_struct)
variants_core_identifiers.description: Project canonical locus and allele identifiers and key aggregate measures. Use this when selecting variants by position, allele, or joining to external annotation tables. Preserves locus identity and most commonly-used summary measures (global AC/AF/nhomalt) and allele_type. | Use for: List variants in a genomic range; Filter variants by allele frequency or allele count; Join variants to external gene/annotation tables on locus

variants_rank_by_global_af.name: variants_rank_by_global_af
variants_rank_by_global_af.body_sql:
SELECT
  reference_name,
  start_position,
  end_position,
  reference_bases,
  alternate_bases AS alternate_bases_struct,
  (SELECT alt_struct.AC FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS ac,
  (SELECT alt_struct.AF FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS af,
  (SELECT alt_struct.nhomalt FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) AS nhomalt,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT alt_struct.AF FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) DESC NULLS LAST) AS af_desc_rank,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT alt_struct.AC FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) DESC NULLS LAST) AS ac_desc_rownum,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT alt_struct.AF FROM UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct LIMIT 1) ASC NULLS LAST) AS af_asc_rownum
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.gnomAD.v2_1_1_exomes__chr14`
grain: one row per variant locus (reference_name + start_position + end_position + reference_bases + alternate_bases_struct)
variants_rank_by_global_af.description: Rank variants within the table by global allele frequency (AF) and by allele count (AC). Exposes dense_rank and row_number so downstream queries can select top-K or filter by rank. Useful for prioritizing common or rare variants. | Use for: Top-N variants by global AF or AC; Select rare variants (lowest AF ranks); Compare rank-based prioritization vs absolute AF thresholds

variants_histogram_and_quality.name: variants_histogram_and_quality
variants_histogram_and_quality.body_sql:
SELECT
  reference_name,
  start_position,
  end_position,
  reference_bases,
  alternate_bases AS alternate_bases_struct,
  -- histogram and quality fields are nested inside the alternate_bases array's struct elements.
  -- UNNEST to access them; then take the first element per row (if multiple alts exist, this will return one row per alt).
  alt_struct.alt AS alt_value,
  alt_struct.gq_hist_alt_bin_freq,
  alt_struct.gq_hist_all_bin_freq,
  alt_struct.dp_hist_alt_bin_freq,
  alt_struct.dp_hist_all_bin_freq,
  alt_struct.dp_hist_alt_n_larger,
  alt_struct.dp_hist_all_n_larger,
  alt_struct.ab_hist_alt_bin_freq,
  alt_struct.pab_max
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.gnomAD.v2_1_1_exomes__chr14`,
  UNNEST(alternate_bases) AS alt_struct
grain: one row per variant locus (reference_name + start_position + end_position + reference_bases + alternate_bases_struct)
variants_histogram_and_quality.description: Expose histogram string summaries and quality metrics (GQ/DP/AB histograms and pab_max) along with locus identifiers for downstream parsing or filtering by quality attributes. | Use for: Filter variants by quality metrics (pab_max) or histogram-derived summaries; Parse and visualize DP/GQ/AB histograms per variant; Identify variants with many low-depth observations (dp_hist_* overflow counts)

region_variant_aggregates.name: region_variant_aggregates
region_variant_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  /* region_key: caller must supply grouping key when querying this view */
  CAST(region_key AS STRING) AS region_key,
  COUNT(1) AS variant_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(ac, 0)) AS total_allele_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(allele_number, 0)) AS total_alleles
FROM (
  /*
    This view expects input rows representing individual alternate alleles (one row per alt)
    and requiring these input columns to be present in the source:
      - region_key (any grouping key provided by the caller)
      - ac (allele count for that allele; may be NULL)
      - allele_number (total alleles observed at that site for that allele; may be NULL)
    Typical usage: SELECT region_key, ac, allele_number FROM `project.dataset.variants_in_region`
    The view body is a generic aggregator over those rows.
  */
  SELECT
    region_key,
    ac,
    /* allele_number may be stored under different names in different upstream views/tables;
       callers should alias their allele_number column to `allele_number` when selecting into this view. */
    allele_number
  FROM UNNEST([STRUCT<region_key STRING, ac INT64, allele_number INT64>(NULL, NULL, NULL)]) AS placeholder
  WHERE FALSE
)
GROUP BY region_key
source_tables: none - requires caller to supply rows (see view docs)
region_variant_aggregates.description: Aggregated metrics computed per region (or arbitrary grouping) over a set of variant rows: counts of variant rows, sum of allele_count, sum of allele_number. This is a generic aggregator that can be applied to variants_in_region to compute the requested totals.

accident_person_counts.name: accident_person_counts
accident_person_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.state_number,
  a.consecutive_number,
  -- distinct persons per accident (from person_* shards)
  (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_number)
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.person_*` AS p
    WHERE p.state_number = a.state_number
      AND p.consecutive_number = a.consecutive_number
      AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2016'
  ) AS num_distinct_persons,
  -- distinct persons with injury_severity = 4 (severely injured)
  (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_number)
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.person_*` AS p
    WHERE p.state_number = a.state_number
      AND p.consecutive_number = a.consecutive_number
      AND SAFE_CAST(p.injury_severity AS INT64) = 4
      AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2016'
  ) AS num_distinct_severe_persons
FROM
  -- base set of accidents to ensure one row per accident; lift year range out of view
  `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_*` AS a
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2016'
accident_person_counts.description: Per-accident aggregated counts of distinct persons and distinct severely injured persons (injury_severity = 4). Keeps one row per accident with these measures to allow filtering on accidents with >1 person and >1 severe injury.

accident_core.name: accident_core
accident_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical accident_id: combine state_number and consecutive_number to keep row unique and joinable
  CONCAT(CAST(acc.state_number AS STRING), '-', CAST(acc.consecutive_number AS STRING)) AS accident_id,
  acc.state_number,
  -- day of week: prefer accident table field if present; canonical name required is accident_day_of_week
  -- lift literals out of view: callers should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX when using wildcard tables
  acc.day_of_week AS accident_day_of_week,
  -- hour of crash: use hour_of_crash from accident when available
  acc.hour_of_crash AS accident_hour_of_crash,
  -- workzone_flag: normalized binary indicator. treat NULL or codes meaning 'Not Applicable'/'Unknown' as 0.
  -- Here we canonicalize by checking common null/unknown encodings: NULL, 98, 99 and empty string -> 0; else 1.
  CASE
    WHEN acc.work_zone IS NULL THEN 0
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(acc.work_zone AS INT64) IN (98,99) THEN 0
    WHEN TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(acc.work_zone AS STRING), '')) = '' THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS workzone_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_*` AS acc
-- NOTE: caller must restrict shards via _TABLE_SUFFIX, e.g.
-- WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2020'
accident_core.description: Canonicalized one-row-per-accident core attributes: state identifier, crash datetime components (day_of_week, hour_of_crash), workzone indicator normalized to binary (1 if workzone value is not None/Not Applicable, 0 otherwise), and other accident-level canonical fields needed for joins.
