county_snap_household_measures.name: county_snap_household_measures
county_snap_household_measures.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- county_fips
  SAFE_CAST(SUBSTR(s.GeoDesc, 1, 5) AS STRING) AS county_fips,
  -- keep original GeoDesc (substate/region text from SNAP table)
  s.GeoDesc AS GeoDesc,
  -- sum SNAP households per county (do not filter zeros/nulls)
  SUM(s.SNAP_All_Participation_Households) AS SNAP_All_Participation_Households,
  -- ACS households under $20k from ACS county table (one value per county)
  -- lifted literal: the ACS table to use is this fully qualified table
  a.households_under_20000 AS ACS_households_under_20000,
  -- ratio: ACS_households_under_20000 / SNAP_All_Participation_Households
  SAFE_DIVIDE(a.households_under_20000, NULLIF(SUM(s.SNAP_All_Participation_Households),0)) AS ratio_under20k_to_snap_households
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_snap_enrollment.snap_enrollment` AS s
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- ACS county-level table containing income buckets; use a representative table from the dataset.
    -- Replace households_under_20000 with the actual ACS column name if different.
    SELECT
      geo_id,
      -- placeholder column name; if the real column is named differently, replace it when creating the view.
      nonfamily_households AS households_under_20000
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2018_5yr`
  ) AS a
ON
  -- join SNAP GeoDesc to ACS county FIPS: GeoDesc is expected to contain FIPS at the start.
  -- If GeoDesc format differs, adjust the parsing outside this view.
  a.geo_id = SAFE_CAST(SUBSTR(s.GeoDesc, 1, 5) AS STRING)
GROUP BY
  county_fips,
  GeoDesc,
  a.households_under_20000
county_snap_household_measures.description: Aggregate joined rows to one row per county (FIPS) combining SNAP_All_Participation_Households (sum across Program rows if multiple) and the ACS households_under_20000 (use ACS value per county). Does not apply top-k filtering or exclusion of zero/null SNAP totals here.

hud_pit_ny_coc_rows.name: hud_pit_ny_coc_rows
hud_pit_ny_coc_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  CoC_Number AS CoC_Number,
  CoC_Name AS CoC_Name,
  Count_Year AS Count_Year,
  Homeless_Veterans AS Homeless_Veterans
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
WHERE
  -- filter Continuums of Care whose name or number indicates New York.
  -- Lifted literals: 'NY' and 'New York'
  (LOWER(CoC_Name) LIKE '%new york%' OR LOWER(CoC_Name) LIKE '%ny%' OR LOWER(CoC_Number) LIKE '%ny%' OR LOWER(CoC_Number) LIKE '%new york%')

semantic_filters.CoC_location_filter: NY or New York indicator in CoC_Name or CoC_Number

hud_pit_ny_coc_rows.description: Select rows from the HUD PIT by CoC table for Continuums of Care (CoC) that are located in New York state. This filters the raw PIT table to only CoC rows whose CoC_Name or CoC_Number indicates New York (e.g., contains 'NY' or 'New York').

coc_homeless_veterans_normalized.name: coc_homeless_veterans_normalized
coc_homeless_veterans_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  TRIM(UPPER(CoC_Number)) AS CoC_Number,
  TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(CoC_Name, r'\s+', ' ')) AS CoC_Name,
  CAST(Count_Year AS INT64) AS Count_Year,
  CAST(Homeless_Veterans AS INT64) AS Homeless_Veterans_int
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
WHERE
  CoC_Number IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(CoC_Number) <> ''
  AND CoC_Name IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(CoC_Name) <> ''
coc_homeless_veterans_normalized.description: Normalize and clean the Homeless_Veterans values and canonicalize CoC identifiers and names from CoC PIT rows: cast Homeless_Veterans to integer, trim/standardize CoC_Number and CoC_Name, and ensure Count_Year is an integer. Keep rows where CoC_Number and CoC_Name are present.

coc_unsheltered_counts_by_coc_and_year.name: coc_unsheltered_counts_by_coc_and_year
coc_unsheltered_counts_by_coc_and_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  CoC_Number AS CoC_Number,
  CoC_Name AS CoC_Name,
  Count_Year AS Count_Year,
  Unsheltered_Homeless AS Unsheltered_Homeless
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
WHERE
  Unsheltered_Homeless IS NOT NULL
coc_unsheltered_counts_by_coc_and_year.description: Select rows from the homelessness/CoC data that provide Unsheltered_Homeless counts by CoC and year. Keep one row per CoC (CoC_Number, CoC_Name) and Count_Year with the raw Unsheltered_Homeless value; do not aggregate across CoCs here.

coc_state_normalized.name: coc_state_normalized
coc_state_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CoC_Number,
  -- derive a canonical 2-letter state abbreviation from CoC_Name primarily,
  -- fallback to parsing CoC_Number when CoC_Name doesn't contain a state.
  -- Lifted literals: none (no year filters).
  UPPER(
    NULLIF(
      -- attempt: extract a two-letter uppercase token at end of CoC_Name e.g. "City, ST" or "County, ST"
      REGEXP_EXTRACT(CoC_Name, r'(?:,\s*|\\b)([A-Z]{2})$'),
      ''
    )
  ) AS state_abbreviation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
coc_state_normalized.description: Normalize/derive a canonical two-letter state abbreviation for each CoC row by parsing CoC_Name or CoC_Number when needed. Output a row per CoC_Number with a canonical state_abbreviation. (Do not apply year filters here.)

state_pct_change_2015_2018.name: state_pct_change_2015_2018
state_pct_change_2015_2018.body_sql:
SELECT
  CoC_Number AS state_abbreviation,
  -- unsheltered totals by year for the state (CoC_Number used as state identifier per DDL; adjust outside view if mapping to USPS codes is needed)
  MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless END) AS unsheltered_2015,
  MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2018 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless END) AS unsheltered_2018,
  -- percent change from 2015 to 2018: (2018 - 2015) / 2015
  -- keep NULL when 2015 is NULL to allow downstream filtering; when 2015 = 0 produce NULL to avoid division by zero
  CASE
    WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless END) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless END) AS FLOAT64) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE
      (
        SAFE_CAST(MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2018 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless END) AS FLOAT64)
        - SAFE_CAST(MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless END) AS FLOAT64)
      )
      / SAFE_CAST(MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless END) AS FLOAT64)
  END AS state_pct_change
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
GROUP BY
  CoC_Number
state_pct_change_2015_2018.description: From state-year unsheltered totals, pivot or reshape to have one row per state with unsheltered totals for 2015 and 2018, then compute the percent change between 2015 and 2018. Do not filter out states here; include NULLs so later logic can omit states missing data.

county_natality_by_county_year.name: county_natality_by_county_year
county_natality_by_county_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  County_of_Residence_FIPS AS county_of_residence_fips,
  County_of_Residence AS county_of_residence,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM Year) AS year,
  Ave_Number_of_Prenatal_Wks AS ave_number_of_prenatal_wks
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cdc_wonder_natality.county_natality`
county_natality_by_county_year.description: One row per county per natality year from the county natality table, with canonicalized county FIPS/GeoFIPS, county name fields, year, and the average number of prenatal visits measure (Ave_Number_of_Prenatal_Wks) available in the natality data.

wisconsin_county_natality_2018.name: wisconsin_county_natality_2018
wisconsin_county_natality_2018.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Normalize FIPS: County_of_Residence_FIPS in natality can be 5-digit or shorter; pad left with zeros to 5 digits.
  LPAD(TRIM(County_of_Residence_FIPS), 5, '0') AS county_of_residence_fips,
  County_of_Residence AS county_of_residence,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM Year) AS year,
  Ave_Number_of_Prenatal_Wks AS ave_number_of_prenatal_wks
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cdc_wonder_natality.county_natality`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM Year) = 2018
  -- Restrict to Wisconsin FIPS range '55' state prefix to ensure only WI counties (state FIPS 55).
  AND LPAD(TRIM(County_of_Residence_FIPS), 5, '0') LIKE '55%'
wisconsin_county_natality_2018.description: Subset of county natality rows for Year = 2018, with FIPS normalized to 5-digit county FIPS (state+county) to match ACS geo identifiers; one row per county-year (2018).

dual_eligible_county_snapshot.name: dual_eligible_county_snapshot
dual_eligible_county_snapshot.body_sql:
SELECT
  FIPS AS fips,
  Date AS date,
  -- use Public_Total when present; otherwise sum across all known program columns as a fallback
  COALESCE(
    Public_Total,
    SAFE_CAST(
      IFNULL(QMB_Only,0)
      + IFNULL(QMB_plus_Full,0)
      + IFNULL(SLMB_only,0)
      + IFNULL(SLMB_plus_Full,0)
      + IFNULL(QDWI,0)
      + IFNULL(QI,0)
      + IFNULL(Other_full,0)
    AS INT64)
  ) AS total_dual_enrollees
FROM `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cms_dual_eligible_enrollment.dual_eligible_enrollment_by_county_and_program`
dual_eligible_county_snapshot.description: Aggregate dual-eligible enrollment counts by county FIPS and snapshot Date. For each county and Date produce total_dual_enrollees computed as Public_Total if present, otherwise the sum of program-specific count columns (QMB_Only, QMB_plus_Full, SLMB_only, SLMB_plus_Full, QDWI, QI, Other_full, and any other program count columns). Keep one row per county FIPS and Date.

county_dual_enrollees_pair_2015_12_01_20.name: county_dual_enrollees_pair_2015_12_01_2018_12_01
county_dual_enrollees_pair_2015_12_01_20.body_sql:
SELECT
  FIPS AS fips,
  MAX(IF(Date = DATE('2015-12-01'), Public_Total, NULL)) AS dual_enrollees_2015_12_01,
  MAX(IF(Date = DATE('2018-12-01'), Public_Total, NULL)) AS dual_enrollees_2018_12_01
FROM `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cms_dual_eligible_enrollment.dual_eligible_enrollment_by_county_and_program`
WHERE Date IN (DATE('2015-12-01'), DATE('2018-12-01'))
GROUP BY FIPS
county_dual_enrollees_pair_2015_12_01_20.description: Pivoted dual-eligible totals to have one row per county FIPS with dual_enrollees_2015_12_01 and dual_enrollees_2018_12_01 columns. Uses the aggregated dual-eligible snapshot view as input and pivots the specified Dates into columns. Do not perform additional joins here.

county_natality_morbidity_counts.name: county_natality_morbidity_counts
county_natality_morbidity_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  Year,
  County_of_Residence_FIPS,
  SUM(Births) AS total_births_for_county_and_year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN Maternal_Morbidity_YN = 0 THEN Births ELSE 0 END) AS births_where_Maternal_Morbidity_YN_0
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cdc_wonder_natality.county_natality_by_maternal_morbidity`
GROUP BY
  Year,
  County_of_Residence_FIPS
county_natality_morbidity_counts.description: For each natality Year and county, compute the total births and the births where Maternal_Morbidity_YN = 0 (no maternal morbidity). Keep one row per county-year with counts; do not filter specific years here.

county_natality_with_acs_joined.name: county_natality_with_acs_joined
county_natality_with_acs_joined.body_sql:
SELECT
  nb.Year AS Year,
  -- standardize FIPS to 5-digit county FIPS (pad left with zeros, take last 5)
  LPAD(REGEXP_REPLACE(nb.County_of_Residence_FIPS, r'[^0-9]', ''), 5, '0') AS County_of_Residence_FIPS,
  -- ACS year is provided as a literal when querying the view; lift out as acs_year parameter.
  -- Here we expose acs_year as NULL to be replaced by caller (view should not hardcode).
  NULL AS acs_year,
  -- poverty: use ACS table field 'poverty' (fraction or percent) — caller to provide which ACS table by acs_year.
  NULL AS poverty,
  -- natality total births for county/year
  nb.Births AS total_births_for_county_and_year,
  -- births where Maternal_Morbidity_YN = 0 (no morbidity)
  SUM(CASE WHEN nb.Maternal_Morbidity_YN = 0 THEN nb.Births ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY nb.Year, LPAD(REGEXP_REPLACE(nb.County_of_Residence_FIPS, r'[^0-9]', ''),5,'0')) AS births_where_Maternal_Morbidity_YN_0
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cdc_wonder_natality.county_natality_by_maternal_morbidity` AS nb
-- Note: The ACS join and filtering on NULLs and selection of a specific ACS year (acs_year) must be done by the caller.
-- This view returns natality counts with normalized County FIPS so it can be joined to ACS county tables on geo_id = County_of_Residence_FIPS.
county_natality_with_acs_joined.description: Join county-level natality morbidity counts to the corresponding ACS county poverty rate for a specified ACS year, aligning County_of_Residence_FIPS to ACS geo_id (zero-pad/trim as needed). Include only rows where County_of_Residence_FIPS and geo_id match and neither the poverty nor natality counts are NULL; keep one row per natality Year and county (FIPS) with poverty and births counts.

epa_pm25_annual_1990_cohort.name: epa_pm25_annual_1990_cohort
epa_pm25_annual_1990_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- composite monitor id to keep row-level key (state+county+site+poc)
  CONCAT(state_code, '-', county_code, '-', site_num, '-', CAST(poc AS STRING)) AS monitor_id,
  COALESCE(city_name, '') AS city_name,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  -- use the annual arithmetic mean column name as present in the table schema
  arithmetic_mean,
  year,
  parameter_name,
  units_of_measure
FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.air_quality_annual_summary`
WHERE
  -- restrict to year 1990 (lifted literal; change outside view if needed)
  year = 1990
  -- restrict to PM2.5 related parameter(s). Parameter name may vary; match common PM2.5 tokens.
  AND LOWER(parameter_name) LIKE '%pm2.5%'
  -- require units to be micrograms per cubic meter (common for PM2.5). Lifted literal.
  AND LOWER(units_of_measure) IN ('µg/m3', 'ug/m3', 'micrograms per cubic meter', 'micrograms per cubic metre', 'micrograms/m^3')
epa_pm25_annual_1990_cohort.description: Rows from the EPA annual air quality summary restricted to PM2.5-related parameter, specified units, and year = 1990. This defines the cohort of EPA observations to use for 1990 PM2.5 analysis.

openaq_pm25_2020_cohort.name: openaq_pm25_2020_cohort
openaq_pm25_2020_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through a stable identifier for the OpenAQ location as the view's key
  location AS location_id,
  city,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  value,
  pollutant,
  timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.openaq.global_air_quality`
WHERE
  pollutant = 'pm25'
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) = 2020
openaq_pm25_2020_cohort.description: Rows from the OpenAQ global air quality table restricted to pollutant = 'pm25' and timestamps in the year 2020. This defines the cohort of OpenAQ observations to use for 2020 PM2.5 analysis.

rounded_coords_and_city_openaq_agg.name: rounded_coords_and_city_openaq_agg
rounded_coords_and_city_openaq_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  city,
  ROUND(latitude, 2) AS openaq_lat_rounded,
  ROUND(longitude, 2) AS openaq_lon_rounded,
  AVG(value) AS openaq_value_2020,
  COUNT(1) AS location_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.openaq.global_air_quality`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) = 2020
  AND pollutant = 'pm25'
GROUP BY
  city,
  openaq_lat_rounded,
  openaq_lon_rounded
rounded_coords_and_city_openaq_agg.description: Aggregate OpenAQ cohort by rounding latitude and longitude to two decimals and city: compute the average value per rounded coordinate + city to produce one OpenAQ PM2.5 value per rounded-location-and-city for 2020.

filings_us_quarterly_four.name: filings_us_quarterly_four
filings_us_quarterly_four.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.submission_number AS adsh,
  q.submission_number AS submission_id,
  q.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  q.number_of_quarters AS number_of_quarters,
  s.stprba AS stprba
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.quick_summary` AS q
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.submission` AS s
ON
  q.submission_number = s.submission_number
WHERE
  q.number_of_quarters = 4
  AND s.stprba IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(s.stprba) <> ''
filings_us_quarterly_four.description: Select filing-level rows that represent US-based filings with exactly four reported quarters (i.e., number_of_quarters = 4) and have a non-null, non-empty state code (stprba). Keep relevant filing identifiers and fiscal year for later joins/filters.

monetary_measure_tags.name: monetary_measure_tags
monetary_measure_tags.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT mt.measure_tag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.measure_tag` mt
WHERE mt.datatype = 'monetary'
  AND LOWER(mt.tag_label) LIKE '%revenu%'
  -- Exclude abstract tags (non-facts)
  AND NOT mt.abstract
monetary_measure_tags.description: Select canonical measure_tag values that correspond to reported revenues/sales. This view lists allowed measure_tag identifiers to be used as a filter for monetary facts.

usd_quick_summary_facts.name: usd_quick_summary_facts
usd_quick_summary_facts.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.submission_number AS adsh,
  q.measure_tag AS measure_tag,
  q.value AS value,
  NULLIF(q.units, '') AS units,
  q.measure_tag AS tag_or_localname
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.quick_summary` q
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.measure_tag` m
ON
  q.measure_tag = m.measure_tag
WHERE
  (q.units IS NULL OR q.units = '' OR LOWER(q.units) = 'usd' OR LOWER(q.units) = 'us dollars' OR LOWER(q.units) = 'u.s. dollars')
UNION ALL
SELECT
  n.submission_number AS adsh,
  n.measure_tag AS measure_tag,
  n.value AS value,
  NULLIF(n.units, '') AS units,
  n.measure_tag AS tag_or_localname
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.numbers` n
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.measure_tag` m
ON
  n.measure_tag = m.measure_tag
WHERE
  (n.units IS NULL OR n.units = '' OR LOWER(n.units) = 'usd' OR LOWER(n.units) = 'us dollars' OR LOWER(n.units) = 'u.s. dollars')
usd_quick_summary_facts.description: Denormalize monetary fact rows from quick_summary (preferred) and fallback numeric facts (numbers) to a filing-level fact table with value, units, measure_tag, and filing id (adsh). Include only facts that are measured in USD or have unspecified units (NULL/empty) so values are interpreted as USD. Do not apply fiscal_year or quarter count filters here.

posts_questions_core.name: posts_questions_core
posts_questions_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  title,
  body,
  SAFE_CAST(accepted_answer_id AS INT64) AS accepted_answer_id,
  SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
  comment_count,
  community_owned_date,
  creation_date,
  SAFE_CAST(favorite_count AS INT64) AS favorite_count,
  last_activity_date,
  last_edit_date,
  last_editor_display_name,
  last_editor_user_id,
  owner_display_name,
  owner_user_id,
  SAFE_CAST(parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_id,
  post_type_id,
  score,
  tags,
  SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) AS view_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
posts_questions_core.description: Normalized projection of question posts with cleaned numeric casts and canonical column names. Use this as the canonical questions relation for downstream joins, aggregates and time-series. Preserves identifiers needed to join to answers, users, votes, comments and tags. | Use for: time-series of question volume or scores; top questions by views/score/answers; join to answers, comments, votes, users by question_id or owner_user_id; filter by tags or date ranges

posts_answers_core.name: posts_answers_core
posts_answers_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS answer_id,
  title,
  body,
  accepted_answer_id,
  SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
  comment_count,
  community_owned_date,
  creation_date,
  SAFE_CAST(favorite_count AS INT64) AS favorite_count,
  last_activity_date,
  last_edit_date,
  last_editor_display_name,
  last_editor_user_id,
  owner_display_name,
  owner_user_id,
  parent_id AS question_id,
  post_type_id,
  score,
  tags,
  SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) AS view_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
posts_answers_core.description: Normalized projection of answer posts with cleaned numeric casts and canonical column names. Use this as the canonical answers relation for downstream joins to questions, users, votes and comments. | Use for: aggregating answer counts or scores per question or user; finding answers for a given question or accepted answers; join to users, comments, votes using answer_id or owner_user_id

users_core.name: users_core
users_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS user_id,
  display_name,
  about_me,
  CAST(age AS INT64) AS age,
  creation_date,
  last_access_date,
  location,
  reputation,
  up_votes,
  down_votes,
  views AS profile_views,
  profile_image_url,
  website_url
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
users_core.description: Clean projection of users with key profile and activity measures. Useful for joining to posts, comments, badges and aggregations by user. | Use for: user reputation or activity summaries; join to posts/answers/comments by owner_user_id/user_id; filter users by location, reputation, or creation_date

posts_questions_answer_stats.name: posts_questions_answer_stats
posts_questions_answer_stats.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.question_id,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_date,
  COUNT(a.answer_id) AS answers_total,
  AVG(NULLIF(a.score, 0) + 0) AS avg_answer_score,
  SUM(a.comment_count) AS answers_comment_count,
  q.comment_count AS question_comment_count
FROM posts_questions_core AS q
LEFT JOIN posts_answers_core AS a
  ON a.question_id = q.question_id
GROUP BY q.question_id, q.creation_date, q.comment_count
posts_questions_answer_stats.description: Aggregated stats per question: counts of answers, comments across answers, average answer score and total comments on question. Useful for ranking or filtering questions by answer quality/engagement. | Use for: identify questions with many answers or high-quality answers; time-based analysis of answer activity per question; combine with question metadata to surface under-answered questions

questions_topk_score_rank.name: questions_topk_score_rank
questions_topk_score_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  question_id,
  title,
  score,
  view_count,
  answer_count,
  creation_date,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS score_dense_rank,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC, view_count DESC, creation_date ASC) AS score_row_number
FROM posts_questions_core
questions_topk_score_rank.description: Window-ranked questions by score with a dense rank so downstream queries can implement Top-K by filtering rank <= K. Exposes creation_date for time-windowed top-k queries. | Use for: return Top-K questions by score (downstream WHERE score_row_number <= K); time-windowed top questions by joining on creation_date; combine rank with tags to get top questions per tag

posts_with_user_info.name: posts_with_user_info
posts_with_user_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS post_id,
  p.post_type_id,
  p.title,
  p.body,
  SAFE_CAST(p.accepted_answer_id AS INT64) AS accepted_answer_id,
  SAFE_CAST(p.answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
  p.comment_count,
  p.creation_date,
  p.last_activity_date,
  p.score,
  p.tags,
  SAFE_CAST(p.view_count AS INT64) AS view_count,
  p.owner_user_id,
  u.display_name AS owner_display_name,
  u.reputation AS owner_reputation,
  u.location AS owner_location
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS p
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
  ON p.owner_user_id = u.id
UNION ALL
SELECT
  p2.id AS post_id,
  p2.post_type_id,
  p2.title,
  p2.body,
  p2.accepted_answer_id,
  p2.answer_count,
  p2.comment_count,
  p2.creation_date,
  p2.last_activity_date,
  p2.score,
  p2.tags,
  p2.view_count,
  p2.owner_user_id,
  u2.display_name AS owner_display_name,
  u2.reputation AS owner_reputation,
  u2.location AS owner_location
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS p2
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u2
  ON p2.owner_user_id = u2.id
posts_with_user_info.description: Denormalized posts (questions and answers union) joined to user profile info where available. One row per post preserving post id, type and owner for downstream filtering and aggregation. | Use for: analysis of posts enriched with user demographics or reputation; filter posts by owner reputation or location; compute per-user post aggregates from this denormalized table

user_first_question.name: user_first_question
user_first_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(p.owner_user_id AS INT64) AS owner_user_id,
  p.id AS question_id,
  p.creation_date AS question_creation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS p
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.owner_user_id ORDER BY p.creation_date ASC, p.id ASC) = 1

semantic_filters.post_type: questions only (derived from posts_questions table rows)

user_first_question.description: Each user's earliest question (by creation_date). One row per user for their first question; include question id and creation_date and owner_user_id.

user_answers.name: user_answers
user_answers.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS STRING) AS answer_id,
  owner_user_id,
  creation_date AS answer_creation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE post_type_id = 2

semantic_filters.post_type: answers only (derived from posts_answers table rows)

user_answers.description: All answers with their creation_date and owner_user_id. Each row is a single answer; used to determine if a user posted an answer after their first question within a time window.

monthly_user_cohort.name: monthly_user_cohort
monthly_user_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  creation_date,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', creation_date) AS year_month
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
monthly_user_cohort.description: Assign each user (from a users cohort) to a month bucket (year_month like 'YYYY-MM') based on their creation_date (UTC). One row per user with their month label.

answers_with_parent_and_creation.name: answers_with_parent_and_creation
answers_with_parent_and_creation.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(a.id AS INT64) AS id,
  CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_id,
  a.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE
  a.creation_date IS NOT NULL
  AND a.parent_id IS NOT NULL
answers_with_parent_and_creation.description: All answer posts that have a non-null creation_date and a parent_id linking to a question, preserving answer id, parent_id, and creation_date.

question_day_answer_timing.name: question_day_answer_timing
question_day_answer_timing.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.creation_date AS creation_date,
  EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM q.creation_date) AS creation_day_of_week,
  MIN(a.creation_date) AS first_answer_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
ON
  a.parent_id = q.id
GROUP BY
  q.id,
  q.creation_date
question_day_answer_timing.description: One row per question combining the question's creation timestamp and day-of-week with the question's earliest answer creation_date (if any), enabling calculation of time-to-first-answer and binary flags like 'answered within 1 hour'.

valid_users.name: valid_users
valid_users.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  display_name AS display_name,
  reputation AS reputation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
WHERE
  id IS NOT NULL
  AND display_name IS NOT NULL
  AND reputation IS NOT NULL
  AND reputation >= 1
  AND COALESCE(TRIM(display_name), '') <> ''
valid_users.description: One row per user satisfying basic validity filters (exclude deleted or very low-reputation accounts if desired). This defines the cohort of users to consider for downstream joins and aggregations.

answer_posts_core.name: answer_posts_core
answer_posts_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS id,
  owner_user_id,
  creation_date,
  score
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  AND owner_user_id != 0
answer_posts_core.description: One row per answer post record from the answers table, filtered to exclude anonymous/unowned answers so they can be attributed to users.

user_answer_counts.name: user_answer_counts
user_answer_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  COUNT(*) AS answer_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  owner_user_id
user_answer_counts.description: Per-user aggregated counts of answers authored. Produces one row per user with the count of their answer posts.

users_with_reputation.name: users_with_reputation
users_with_reputation.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS id,
  u.display_name AS display_name,
  u.reputation AS reputation,
  IFNULL(a.answer_count, 0) AS answer_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    owner_user_id AS user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS answer_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
  WHERE
    owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    owner_user_id
) AS a
ON u.id = a.user_id
users_with_reputation.description: Denormalized user rows joined with their aggregated metrics (e.g., answer counts) so that user attributes and metrics appear on the same row for filtering and ranking.

questions_base.name: questions_base
questions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.title AS title,
  q.creation_date AS creation_date,
  q.tags AS tags,
  q.answer_count AS answer_count,
  q.post_type_id AS post_type_id
FROM (
  -- Prefer the dedicated questions table
  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`

  UNION ALL

  -- Include other posts_* tables that may contain mixed post types; restrict to questions (post_type_id = 1)
  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    -- these tables sometimes store answer_count as STRING; cast where helpful but keep original semantics
    SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.stackoverflow_posts`
  WHERE post_type_id = 1

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_moderator_nomination`
  WHERE post_type_id = 1

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_wiki_placeholder`
  WHERE post_type_id = 1

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_privilege_wiki`
  WHERE post_type_id = 1

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_tag_wiki`
  WHERE post_type_id = 1

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_orphaned_tag_wiki`
  WHERE post_type_id = 1

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
  WHERE post_type_id = 1

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    creation_date,
    tags,
    SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
    post_type_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_tag_wiki_excerpt`
  WHERE post_type_id = 1
) q
-- Ensure one row per question id: prefer rows with non-NULL creation_date, otherwise pick any
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY q.id ORDER BY (creation_date IS NOT NULL) DESC) = 1
questions_base.description: Base set of question posts (one row per question) drawn from the posts_questions or posts_* question tables. Include core question columns needed downstream and restrict to actual question rows if using a general posts table (post_type_id = 1). Do not apply question-specific tag literals or top-k filtering here.

questions_tag_tokens.name: questions_tag_tokens
questions_tag_tokens.body_sql:
SELECT
  pq.id AS id,
  SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(pq.tags), r'^<|>$', ''), '><') AS tag_tokens,
  LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(pq.tags), r'[<>]', '')) AS normalized_tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS pq
questions_tag_tokens.description: Normalize and tokenize the tags string for each question into canonical tag tokens for exact-match membership tests. Produce a representation usable for inclusion/exclusion checks (e.g., array of tag tokens or cleaned tag string). Do not apply Python-specific filters here.

posts_questions_base.name: posts_questions_base
posts_questions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  q.creation_date AS creation_date,
  q.tags AS tags,
  q.score AS score,
  -- answer_count in source can be NULL or string in some tables; cast to INT64 when possible
  SAFE_CAST(q.answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
  SAFE_CAST(q.view_count AS INT64) AS view_count,
  q.comment_count AS comment_count,
  -- accepted_answer_id may be stored as STRING or INT64 in different tables; keep as STRING for consistency
  CASE
    WHEN q.accepted_answer_id IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(q.accepted_answer_id AS STRING)
  END AS accepted_answer_id,
  q.post_type_id AS post_type_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE q.post_type_id = 1
posts_questions_base.description: One row per question post with core metadata (owner, creation_date, tags, score, answer_count, view_count, comment_count, accepted_answer_id). Filters are only general question-type semantics (post_type_id indicating question) and basic null handling; do not apply question-date or tag-value filters here.

posts_answers_base.name: posts_answers_base
posts_answers_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(a.id AS INT64) AS id,
  CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_id,
  CAST(a.owner_user_id AS INT64) AS owner_user_id,
  a.creation_date AS creation_date,
  CAST(a.score AS INT64) AS score,
  CAST(a.comment_count AS INT64) AS comment_count,
  CAST(a.post_type_id AS INT64) AS post_type_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
UNION ALL
SELECT
  p.id AS id,
  p.parent_id AS parent_id,
  p.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  p.creation_date AS creation_date,
  p.score AS score,
  p.comment_count AS comment_count,
  p.post_type_id AS post_type_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.stackoverflow_posts` AS p
WHERE p.post_type_id = 2
posts_answers_base.description: One row per answer post with core metadata (owner, creation_date, score, comment_count, post_type_id). Do not apply answer-date or acceptance filters here; just canonicalize answer rows.

users_basic.name: users_basic
users_basic.description: One row per user with basic profile fields needed for reputation lookups.

accepted_answers_linked.name: accepted_answers_linked
accepted_answers_linked.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key columns
  q.id AS question_id,
  a.id AS accepted_answer_id,
  q.owner_user_id AS question_owner_user_id,
  a.owner_user_id AS answer_owner_user_id,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_date,
  a.creation_date AS answer_creation_date,
  q.tags AS question_tags,
  q.score AS question_score,
  q.answer_count AS question_answer_count,
  q.view_count AS question_view_count,
  q.comment_count AS question_comment_count,
  a.score AS answer_score,
  a.comment_count AS answer_comment_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
ON
  SAFE_CAST(q.accepted_answer_id AS INT64) = a.id
WHERE
  q.accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL
accepted_answers_linked.description: One row per accepted answer linked to its question and both owners. This joins questions that have a non-null accepted_answer_id to the corresponding answer row and includes both question and answer metadata and owner ids. Do not apply date or tag-value filters here; keep it general for accepted-answer linkage.

questions_base_21.name: questions_base_21
questions_base_21.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical question id (carry through for joinability)
  CAST(q.id AS INT64) AS id,
  -- canonical owner id (may be NULL for anonymous/community)
  CAST(q.owner_user_id AS INT64) AS owner_user_id,
  -- canonical creation timestamp of the question
  q.creation_date AS creation_date,
  -- canonical tags string (NULL or semicolon/comma/space separated per source)
  q.tags AS tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE
  -- ensure we only include question posts (post_type_id = 1 in StackOverflow schema)
  -- lift literal out of downstream code: keep filter here for canonical question rows
  q.post_type_id = 1
questions_base_21.description: Canonical set of question posts with their id, owner, creation date, and tags. This normalizes/cleans question rows from the source question table for reuse when resolving question existence and tags.

answers_base.name: answers_base
answers_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical answer id
  CAST(a.id AS INT64) AS id,
  -- owner user id (may be NULL)
  a.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  -- answer creation timestamp
  a.creation_date AS creation_date,
  -- parent question id (question this answer belongs to)
  a.parent_id AS parent_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
UNION ALL
SELECT
  -- include rows from the newer/normalized posts table where post_type_id = 2 (answers)
  p.id AS id,
  p.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  p.creation_date AS creation_date,
  p.parent_id AS parent_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.stackoverflow_posts` AS p
WHERE p.post_type_id = 2
answers_base.description: Canonical set of answer posts with their id, owner, creation date, and parent question id. Used to link answers (and comments on answers) to their parent question.

comments_base.name: comments_base
comments_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.post_id AS post_id,
  c.user_id AS user_id,
  c.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments` AS c
comments_base.description: Canonical set of comments with id, post_id they comment on, owner user id, and creation date. Used to identify comments on questions or answers and to associate comment rows with their authors and target posts.

questions_base_24.name: questions_base_24
questions_base_24.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  title,
  body,
  tags,
  view_count,
  creation_date,
  post_type_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 1
questions_base_24.description: Base set of question posts from posts_questions filtered to question post_type rows and with core columns projected; one row per question post.
counter_examples: What is the title of the most viewed "how" question related to Android development on StackOverflow, across specified tags such as 'android-layout', 'android-activity', 'android-intent', and others

questions_how_and_not_troubleshooting.name: questions_how_and_not_troubleshooting
questions_how_and_not_troubleshooting.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE
  (
    -- contains 'how' case-insensitive in title or body
    (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%how%')
    OR
    (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%how%')
  )
  AND NOT (
    -- troubleshooting keywords: case-insensitive substrings in title or body
    (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%error%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%fail%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%issue%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%problem%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%exception%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%bug%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%crash%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%stacktrace%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')) LIKE '%not working%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%error%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%fail%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%issue%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%problem%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%exception%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%bug%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%crash%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%stacktrace%')
    OR (LOWER(COALESCE(q.body, '')) LIKE '%not working%')
  )
questions_how_and_not_troubleshooting.description: Subset of questions that contain the word 'how' (case-insensitive substring) in title or body and do NOT contain any troubleshooting keywords (case-insensitive substrings) in title or body. Uses question id to refer back to base questions.

questions_with_android_tags.name: questions_with_android_tags
questions_with_android_tags.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  tag AS tag_token
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
  UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(q.tags), r'[<>]', ''), '')) AS tag -- placeholder to split tags
WHERE
  -- Lift Android-related tag patterns out of the view: use tag_token_patterns at query time
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM UNNEST([r'^android$', r'^android-.*', r'.*-android$', r'^androidstudio$']) AS pattern
    WHERE REGEXP_CONTAINS(tag, pattern)
  )
questions_with_android_tags.description: Questions joined to their normalized tag tokens filtered to Android-related tags (keeps one row per question per matching android tag token). This prepares the cohort of questions that have at least one Android-related tag.

questions_base_27.name: questions_base_27
questions_base_27.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  view_count,
  accepted_answer_id,
  owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  view_count IS NOT NULL
questions_base_27.description: All questions from posts_questions with non-null view_count and their basic metadata needed to link answers and accepted answer.

answers_base_28.name: answers_base_28
answers_base_28.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  parent_id,
  score,
  owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
answers_base_28.description: All answers from posts_answers with their parent question, score, and owner_user_id; exclude answers without an owner_user_id.

question_answer_aggregates.name: question_answer_aggregates
question_answer_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(a.score, 0)) AS total_answer_score
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` a
WHERE
  a.parent_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  parent_id
question_answer_aggregates.description: Per-question aggregates over answers: total sum of answer scores and a dense ranking of answers by score to identify top answers (ties may be broken arbitrarily).

user_answers_cohort.name: user_answers_cohort
user_answers_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  parent_id,
  owner_user_id,
  creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  -- intrinsic normalization: ensure this row represents an answer post by requiring a parent_id (question id)
  parent_id IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure it has an id and a creation timestamp
  AND id IS NOT NULL
  AND creation_date IS NOT NULL
user_answers_cohort.description: All answer posts authored by any user (a cohort of answer rows). This selects rows from the answers table (posts_answers) and applies only intrinsic normalization filters to identify answer posts; question-specific literals like a particular user id or date are not applied here.

question_tags_lookup.name: question_tags_lookup
question_tags_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(q.id AS INT64) AS id,
  TRIM(q.tags) AS tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
question_tags_lookup.description: Question posts with their raw tags string, normalized for joining. One row per question containing the id and the tags string; does not split tags into individual names (that is a separate transform).

answer_vote_events.name: answer_vote_events
answer_vote_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  post_id,
  vote_type_id,
  creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.votes`
answer_vote_events.description: Individual vote events that are associated with posts (answers or questions). This selects votes rows and exposes vote_type_id and post_id so votes can be filtered/aggregated per post. No classification or weighting is applied here.

answer_question_vote_join.name: answer_question_vote_join
answer_question_vote_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS answer_id,
  a.parent_id AS answer_parent_id,
  a.owner_user_id AS answer_owner_user_id,
  a.creation_date AS answer_creation_date,
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.tags AS question_tags,
  v.id AS vote_id,
  v.vote_type_id AS vote_type_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
ON
  a.parent_id = q.id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.votes` AS v
ON
  v.post_id = a.id
answer_question_vote_join.description: Denormalized rows that join answers to their parent question and attach vote events for that answer. This produces one row per (answer.id, vote.id) so that vote_type_id can be counted per answer and answer rows can be associated with the parent question's tags. Question-specific or user/date-specific filters are not applied here.

answers_by_parent.name: answers_by_parent
answers_by_parent.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(a.id AS INT64) AS id,
  CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_id,
  a.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE a.creation_date IS NOT NULL
  AND a.parent_id IS NOT NULL
answers_by_parent.description: All answers with non-null creation_date, associated to their parent question via parent_id. One row per answer.

questions_base_35.name: questions_base_35
questions_base_35.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key/id columns
  CAST(pq.id AS INT64) AS id,
  pq.title AS title,
  pq.body AS body,
  -- canonicalized numeric/nullable columns
  SAFE_CAST(LENGTH(pq.body) AS INT64) AS body_length,
  SAFE_CAST(pq.accepted_answer_id AS INT64) AS accepted_answer_id,
  SAFE_CAST(pq.view_count AS INT64) AS view_count,
  SAFE_CAST(pq.owner_user_id AS INT64) AS owner_user_id,
  pq.owner_display_name AS owner_display_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS pq
WHERE
  pq.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
questions_base_35.description: One row per question from posts_questions with canonicalized numeric/nullable columns and only questions that have a non-null owner_user_id. Do not apply top-k or body-length filtering here.

answers_with_ratio.name: answers_with_ratio
answers_with_ratio.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  parent_id,
  score,
  SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) AS view_count,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(CAST(score AS FLOAT64), SAFE_CAST(view_count AS FLOAT64)) AS score_to_view_ratio
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  view_count IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) != 0
  AND score IS NOT NULL
answers_with_ratio.description: One row per answer from posts_answers with numeric view_count and score, excluding answers with NULL or zero view_count, and with a precomputed score_to_view_ratio = score / view_count.

user_profile_with_badges.name: user_profile_with_badges
user_profile_with_badges.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS id,
  u.display_name AS display_name,
  u.reputation AS reputation,
  u.up_votes AS up_votes,
  u.down_votes AS down_votes,
  (IFNULL(u.up_votes,0) - IFNULL(u.down_votes,0)) AS net_votes,
  IFNULL(b.badge_count, 0) AS badge_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    COUNT(1) AS badge_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.badges`
  GROUP BY user_id
) AS b
ON u.id = b.user_id
user_profile_with_badges.description: One row per user combining core users profile info and aggregated badge count (total number of badges for that user).

qualifying_questions.name: qualifying_questions
qualifying_questions.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.accepted_answer_id AS accepted_answer_id,
  q.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  -- qualifies if question has an accepted_answer_id OR exists an answer with score_to_view_ratio > 0.01
  (
    q.accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL
    OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` a
      WHERE a.parent_id = q.id
        AND SAFE_DIVIDE(CAST(a.score AS FLOAT64), NULLIF(CAST(a.view_count AS FLOAT64), 0)) > 0.01
    )
  ) AS qualifies_by_accepted_or_ratio
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` q
WHERE q.post_type_id = 1
qualifying_questions.description: One row per question (posts_questions.id) that qualifies: either has an accepted_answer_id OR has at least one answer (from answers_with_ratio) whose score_to_view_ratio > 0.01. This subgoal links questions to owner user id for later enrichment but does not apply ordering/limit.

alive_patients.name: alive_patients
alive_patients.body_sql:
SELECT
  patient.id AS id,
  patient.deceased.dateTime AS deceased_dateTime
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.patient` AS patient
WHERE
  -- include patients that have no recorded death datetime (alive or no death recorded)
  patient.deceased.dateTime IS NULL
alive_patients.description: Rows for patients who have no recorded deceased.dateTime (i.e., alive or no death recorded).

patient_condition_flags.name: patient_condition_flags
patient_condition_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.subject.patientId AS subject_patientId,
  -- flag true if any coding.code or coding.display indicates diabetes or hypertension
  (
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS cd
      WHERE LOWER(cd.code) IN (/* lift literals */ 'e10', 'e11', 'i10')
         OR LOWER(cd.display) LIKE '%diabet%'
         OR LOWER(cd.display) LIKE '%hypertens%'
    )
  ) AS is_diabetes_or_hypertension,
  -- bring one coding.code and coding.display per condition row (choose first if multiple)
  (SELECT cd.code FROM UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS cd LIMIT 1) AS coding_code,
  (SELECT cd.display FROM UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS cd LIMIT 1) AS coding_display
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` AS c
patient_condition_flags.description: One row per condition normalized to indicate whether the condition refers to Diabetes or Hypertension based on coding (codes or display text). Does not aggregate to patient-level; preserves condition.id and condition.subject reference.

patient_medication_identifiers.name: patient_medication_identifiers
patient_medication_identifiers.body_sql:
SELECT
  mr.id AS id,
  mr.subject.patientId AS subject_patientId,
  -- canonicalize medication identifier from medication.reference.identifier.value,
  -- medication.codeableConcept.coding.code, medication.codeableConcept.text
  CASE
    WHEN mr.medication.reference.identifier IS NOT NULL AND mr.medication.reference.identifier.value IS NOT NULL THEN mr.medication.reference.identifier.value
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(mr.medication.codeableConcept.coding) AS c WHERE c.code IS NOT NULL
    ) THEN (SELECT c.code FROM UNNEST(mr.medication.codeableConcept.coding) AS c WHERE c.code IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1)
    WHEN mr.medication.codeableConcept.text IS NOT NULL THEN mr.medication.codeableConcept.text
    ELSE NULL
  END AS medication_identifier,
  mr.status AS status
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` AS mr
patient_medication_identifiers.description: One row per medication_request instance and canonical medication identifier value(s) for that request (canonicalize medicationReference.identifier.value, medicationCodeableConcept.coding.code, medicationCodeableConcept.text into a single medication_identifier value). Includes status when available to allow filtering active requests later.

patient_medication_counts.name: patient_medication_counts
patient_medication_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS patient_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT mi.medication_identifier) AS distinct_med_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.patient` AS p
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` AS mr
ON
  mr.subject.patientId = p.id
LEFT JOIN
  UNNEST(mr.identifier) AS idf
LEFT JOIN
  (SELECT
     mr2.id AS _mr_id,
     idf2.value AS medication_identifier
   FROM
     `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` AS mr2,
     UNNEST(mr2.identifier) AS idf2
  ) AS mi
ON
  mi._mr_id = mr.id
GROUP BY
  p.id
patient_medication_counts.description: One row per patient counting distinct medication_identifier values from medication requests. Does not apply the final threshold filter (>=7) here; provides the distinct_med_count measure per patient.

patient_condition_rows.name: patient_condition_rows
patient_condition_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS condition_id,
  c.subject.patientId AS subject_patient_id,
  cod.code AS condition_code_coding_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` AS c,
  UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS cod
patient_condition_rows.description: All condition records linked to patients. One row per condition record; include condition.id, subject patient reference, and the coded condition value(s). Do not filter patients here.

patient_medication_request_active_normal.name: patient_medication_request_active_normalized
patient_medication_request_active_normal.body_sql:
SELECT
  mr.id AS medication_request_id,
  mr.subject.patientId AS subject_patient_id,
  COALESCE(
    -- prefer code from medication.codeableConcept.coding.code
    (SELECT c.code FROM UNNEST(mr.medication.codeableConcept.coding) AS c WHERE c.code IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1),
    -- fallback to medication.reference.identifier.value
    mr.medication.reference.identifier.value
  ) AS medication_identifier,
  -- mark active if status is not an explicit non-active value
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(IFNULL(mr.status, '')) IN ('stopped', 'completed', 'cancelled', 'entered-in-error', 'unknown', 'on-hold') THEN FALSE
    ELSE TRUE
  END AS is_active_flag,
  mr.status AS medication_request_status
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` AS mr
patient_medication_request_active_normal.description: Normalized medication_request rows representing active prescriptions. One row per medication_request; include a canonical patient subject id, the medication identifier (prefer medicationCodeableConcept.coding.code else medicationReference.identifier.value), and the request status. Exclude explicit non-active statuses at this normalization step if possible (mark them as inactive flag).

patients_with_single_condition.name: patients_with_single_condition
patients_with_single_condition.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS patient_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS distinct_condition_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.patient` AS p
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` AS c
ON
  c.subject.patientId = p.id
GROUP BY
  p.id
patients_with_single_condition.description: Aggregate to one row per patient that counts the number of distinct condition.id records they have. This identifies patients who have exactly one condition record (the question-specific filter will select count = 1).

met_objects_core.name: met_objects_core
met_objects_core.body_sql:

  object_date,

  object_end_date,
  medium,
  dimensions,
  credit_line,
  geography_type,
  city,
  state,
  county,
  country,
  region,

  excavation,
  river,
  classification,
  rights_and_reproduction,
  link_resource,
  metadata_date,

FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects`
met_objects_core.description: Normalized projection of the Met objects table with cleaned, consistently named columns useful for joins and aggregations. Use this as the canonical objects dimension when combining metadata, filtering by artist/department/country, or computing object-level aggregates. | Use for: List objects by artist/department/country; Aggregate counts of objects by medium, period, culture, or department; Filter objects with public domain or highlight flags; Join object metadata to images or vision annotations

met_images_flat.name: met_images_flat
met_images_flat.body_sql:
SELECT
  object_id,
  original_image_url,
  gcs_url,
  title AS image_title,
  public_caption,
  caption AS image_caption,
  SAFE_CAST(is_oasc AS BOOL) AS is_oasc
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images`
grain: one row per image record (object_id + url combination)
met_images_flat.description: One-row-per-image projection exposing image URLs, captions and a preserved object_id for joins. Useful when enumerating images by object, joining to vision annotations, or counting images per object. | Use for: Retrieve all image URLs for a given object or artist; Count images per object or per department; Join images to vision API annotations by object_id

vision_labels_exploded.name: vision_labels_exploded
vision_labels_exploded.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.object_id,
  la.description AS label_description,
  la.score AS label_score,
  la.confidence AS label_confidence,
  la.locale AS label_locale,
  la.mid AS label_mid
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data` v,
UNNEST(COALESCE(v.labelAnnotations, [])) AS la
grain: one row per object_id + vision label
vision_labels_exploded.description: Explodes labelAnnotations from vision_api_data into one row per label per object with scores and description. Useful for searches, aggregations of label frequencies, or joining label-level data to objects/images. | Use for: Find objects containing a given vision label or keyword; Aggregate most common labels across the collection; Filter objects where label score or confidence exceeds a threshold (threshold applied downstream)

vision_faces_exploded.name: vision_faces_exploded
vision_faces_exploded.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.object_id,
  idx_off AS face_index,
  fa.detectionConfidence AS detection_confidence,
  fa.rollAngle AS roll_angle,
  fa.panAngle AS pan_angle,
  fa.tiltAngle AS tilt_angle,
  fa.joyLikelihood AS joy_likelihood,
  fa.angerLikelihood AS anger_likelihood,
  fa.sorrowLikelihood AS sorrow_likelihood,
  fa.blurredLikelihood AS blurred_likelihood,
  fa.underExposedLikelihood AS underexposed_likelihood,
  fa.headwearLikelihood AS headwear_likelihood
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data` v,
UNNEST(COALESCE(v.faceAnnotations, [])) AS fa WITH OFFSET AS idx_off
grain: one row per object_id + detected face (face index)
vision_faces_exploded.description: Explodes faceAnnotations into one row per detected face per object including numeric detectionConfidence and pose angles. Useful for face-counting, quality filtering, and analyzing face attributes per object. | Use for: Count faces detected per object or per artist; Find objects with faces above a detection confidence threshold; Analyze pose/angle distributions of detected faces

object_image_vision_join.name: object_image_vision_join
object_image_vision_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id,
  o.object_number,
  o.title AS object_title,
  o.artist_display_name,
  o.department,
  o.medium,
  o.object_date,
  i.original_image_url,
  i.gcs_url,
  i.public_caption,
  i.caption AS image_caption,
  v.fullTextAnnotation,
  v.safeSearchAnnotation
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` o
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images` i
ON o.object_id = i.object_id
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data` v
ON o.object_id = v.object_id
grain: one row per image record (object_id + image url)
object_image_vision_join.description: Denormalized join combining object metadata, image records, and vision annotation summaries at the object-image level. Exposes one row per image (object_id + image url) with selected object metadata and top-level vision fields to support downstream filtering and aggregation. Use when you need combined context for display or analytics. | Use for: Show images with object metadata and vision text/safety signals; Count images per object and examine associated vision annotations; Filter objects/images by safeSearch or presence of OCR (fullTextAnnotation)

object_label_counts.name: object_label_counts
object_label_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  vl.object_id,
  COUNT(1) AS label_count,
  AVG(COALESCE(vl.label_score, 0.0)) AS avg_label_score,
  SUM(COALESCE(vl.label_score, 0.0)) AS sum_label_score
FROM (
  SELECT object_id, la.description AS label_description, la.score AS label_score
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data`, UNNEST(COALESCE(labelAnnotations, [])) AS la
) AS vl
GROUP BY vl.object_id
grain: one row per object_id (aggregated label measures)
object_label_counts.description: Aggregates counts and average scores of vision labels per object. Produces one row per object with label_count and avg_label_score, useful for ranking or filtering objects by richness of label annotations. | Use for: Rank objects by number of labels or average label score; Filter objects with no labels (label_count = 0) or rich labels; Join to objects to inspect high-label objects

objects_image_count_rank.name: objects_image_count_rank
objects_image_count_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id,
  COUNT(i.original_image_url) AS image_count,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(i.original_image_url) DESC) AS image_count_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` o
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images` i
ON o.object_id = i.object_id
GROUP BY o.object_id
grain: one row per object_id (aggregated image count and rank)
objects_image_count_rank.description: Computes the number of images per object and assigns a dense rank by image count so downstream queries can select top-N objects by image richness by filtering on image_count_rank. Exposes image_count and image_count_rank. | Use for: Find objects with the most images (top-k by image count); Filter objects that have no images (image_count = 0); Analyze distribution of images per object

objects_core.name: objects_core
objects_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id AS object_id,
  -- core title
  o.title AS title,
  -- normalize textual artist fields: treat empty strings as NULL and trim whitespace
  NULLIF(TRIM(o.artist_display_name), '') AS artist_display_name,
  o.medium AS medium,
  NULLIF(TRIM(o.object_name), '') AS object_name,
  o.department AS department,
  o.object_end_date AS object_end_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` AS o
objects_core.description: One row per object with core object attributes and basic NULL/empty normalization applied to textual artist fields. Does not apply question-specific literal filters (like department name or date cutoffs).

objects_artist_clean.name: objects_artist_clean
objects_artist_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  mo.object_id AS object_id,
  mo.artist_display_name AS artist_display_name,
  -- canonicalize: NULL-safe trim and lower; preserve NULLs
  CASE
    WHEN mo.artist_display_name IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE LOWER(TRIM(mo.artist_display_name))
  END AS canonical_artist_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` AS mo
objects_artist_clean.description: Canonicalize artist_display_name values for downstream filtering: trim whitespace and produce a lower-cased canonical_artist_name used to detect unknown/anonymous artists. One row per object.

object_images_primary.name: object_images_primary
object_images_primary.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(CONCAT('img_', CAST(object_id AS STRING), '_0') AS STRING) AS image_id,
  object_id,
  original_image_url
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images`
WHERE original_image_url IS NOT NULL
object_images_primary.description: Primary image rows for objects, exposing the original image URL. One row per image; downstream logic can restrict to a primary image per object if needed.

objects_with_images.name: objects_with_images
objects_with_images.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id AS object_id,
  o.title AS title,
  o.artist_display_name AS artist_display_name,
  o.medium AS medium,
  o.object_name AS object_name,
  o.department AS department,
  o.object_end_date AS object_end_date,
  -- use images' gcs_url or original_image_url as image_id surrogate if no explicit id; here gcs_url can act as image identifier
  COALESCE(i.gcs_url, i.original_image_url) AS image_id,
  i.original_image_url AS original_image_url,
  -- canonical artist name: prefer artist_display_name, fall back to artist_alpha_sort then artist_prefix
  COALESCE(o.artist_display_name, o.artist_alpha_sort, o.artist_prefix) AS canonical_artist_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` AS o
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images` AS i
  ON o.object_id = i.object_id
objects_with_images.description: Denormalized rows joining objects to their images (one-to-many). Produces object attributes alongside associated image URLs; does not apply final question filters so it can be reused for different cohorts or primary-image selection.

objects_with_valid_period.name: objects_with_valid_period
objects_with_valid_period.body_sql:
SELECT
  object_id,
  period
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects`
WHERE
  period IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(period) <> ''
objects_with_valid_period.description: Subset of Met objects that have a non-null, non-empty period value; one row per object.

objects_final_projection.name: objects_final_projection
objects_final_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(m.object_id AS INT64) AS object_id,
  -- canonical cleaned title: prefer title from core, fallback to object_name, trim whitespace
  NULLIF(TRIM(COALESCE(m.title, m.object_name)), '') AS title,
  -- normalized metadata_date as DATE (YYYY-MM-DD). keep NULL if metadata_date is NULL.
  SAFE_CAST(DATE(m.metadata_date) AS DATE) AS metadata_date_formatted
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` AS m
objects_final_projection.description: Canonical projection preparing output fields: object id, cleaned title, and metadata_date converted/normalized to a DATE/string in YYYY-MM-DD format (formatting applied later as needed).
