  arithmetic_mean
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.lead_daily_summary`
WHERE
  state_code = '06'
daily_pollutant_records_ca.description: Subset of daily summary pollutant records for all pollutant daily summary tables restricted to rows whose state_code corresponds to California (canonical filter). This yields one row per original daily summary measurement and preserves date_local and arithmetic_mean for later aggregation. Does not apply date range or pollutant-specific scaling or NULL-dropping here.

pollutant_monthly_scaled_view.name: pollutant_monthly_scaled_view
pollutant_monthly_scaled_view.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- month as YYYY-MM (string) derived from date_local month
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE_TRUNC(date_local, MONTH)) AS month,

  -- pm10 monthly average (carry through arithmetic_mean aggregated by month)
  AVG(CASE WHEN parameter_name = 'PM10' THEN arithmetic_mean END) OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE_TRUNC(date_local, MONTH))) AS pm10_monthly_avg,

  -- pm25_fine (PM2.5 FRM) monthly average
  AVG(CASE WHEN parameter_name = 'PM2.5 FRM' THEN arithmetic_mean END) OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE_TRUNC(date_local, MONTH))) AS pm25_frm_monthly_avg,

  -- pm25_nonfrm monthly average
  AVG(CASE WHEN parameter_name = 'PM2.5 Non-FRM' THEN arithmetic_mean END) OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE_TRUNC(date_local, MONTH))) AS pm25_nonfrm_monthly_avg,

  -- VOC monthly average (assumed parameter_name 'VOC' in source)
  AVG(CASE WHEN parameter_name = 'VOC' THEN arithmetic_mean END) OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE_TRUNC(date_local, MONTH))) AS voc_monthly_avg,

  -- SO2 monthly average scaled by 10 (assumed parameter_name 'SO2')
  AVG(CASE WHEN parameter_name = 'SO2' THEN arithmetic_mean END) OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE_TRUNC(date_local, MONTH))) * 10.0 AS so2_monthly_avg_scaled,

  -- Lead monthly average scaled by 100 (assumed parameter_name 'Lead')
  AVG(CASE WHEN parameter_name = 'Lead' THEN arithmetic_mean END) OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE_TRUNC(date_local, MONTH))) * 100.0 AS lead_monthly_avg_scaled
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_frm_daily_summary`
pollutant_monthly_scaled_view.description: Reshape/transpose monthly pollutant aggregates into one row per month with columns for each target pollutant's monthly average. Applies pollutant-specific scaling factors to the aggregated averages (e.g., multiply SO2 by 10 and Lead by 100). This view expects monthly aggregates as input and emits one row per month with one column per pollutant. Does not restrict to a specific year beyond what the input month contains.

valid_sales_transactions.name: valid_sales_transactions
valid_sales_transactions.body_sql:
SELECT
  invoice_and_item_number AS id,
  date,
  category_name,
  volume_sold_liters,
  state_bottle_retail,
  bottles_sold,
  pack,
  sale_dollars
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
WHERE
  -- exclude null or zero volumes
  volume_sold_liters IS NOT NULL
  AND volume_sold_liters != 0
  -- require at least one of retail or sale dollars to be present and non-zero
  AND (state_bottle_retail IS NOT NULL OR sale_dollars IS NOT NULL)
  AND COALESCE(state_bottle_retail, 0) != 0 OR COALESCE(sale_dollars, 0) != 0
  -- ensure id present
  AND invoice_and_item_number IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.state_bottle_retail_or_sale_dollars: state_bottle_retail IS NOT NULL OR sale_dollars IS NOT NULL

valid_sales_transactions.description: Filter sales rows to include only transactions with non-null, non-zero volume and non-null retail or sale dollar values; keep base columns needed to compute per-transaction per-liter retail price and the transaction date and category.

category_yearly_avg_price_per_liter.name: category_yearly_avg_price_per_liter
category_yearly_avg_price_per_liter.body_sql:
SELECT
  vs.category_name AS category_name,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM vs.date) AS year,
  -- per-transaction price per liter: retail per bottle * bottles_sold / liters_sold
  -- compute price_per_liter at transaction level, guard against zero/null volume_sold_liters
  AVG(CASE WHEN vs.volume_sold_liters IS NOT NULL AND vs.volume_sold_liters > 0
           THEN (vs.state_bottle_retail * vs.bottles_sold) / vs.volume_sold_liters
           ELSE NULL END) AS avg_price_per_liter
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales` AS vs
GROUP BY
  category_name,
  year
category_yearly_avg_price_per_liter.description: Aggregate per-transaction price_per_liter to compute the average per-liter retail price for each category_name and calendar year. One row per category_name and year with the average of transactions in that group.

sales_2022_2023_rows.name: sales_2022_2023_rows
sales_2022_2023_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  item_number,
  item_description,
  sale_dollars
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) IN (2022, 2023)
sales_2022_2023_rows.description: Subset of sales rows restricted to calendar years 2022 and 2023 (only rows whose date is in those two years). Keeps original sales columns for further aggregation.

item_yearly_sales.name: item_yearly_sales
item_yearly_sales.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.item_number AS item_number,
  s.item_description AS item_description,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM s.date) AS year,
  SUM(s.sale_dollars) AS sales_total
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales` AS s
GROUP BY
  s.item_number,
  s.item_description,
  year
item_yearly_sales.description: Aggregated total sale_dollars per item (item_number, item_description) for each calendar year present in the filtered rows. Produces one row per item per year with the sum of sale_dollars.

bourbon_sales_2022_by_zip_month.name: bourbon_sales_2022_by_zip_month
bourbon_sales_2022_by_zip_month.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC(date, MONTH) AS sale_date,
  zip_code,
  county,
  category_name,
  sale_dollars
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
WHERE
  category = 'Bourbon Whiskey'
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) = 2022
  AND zip_code IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(zip_code) != ''
bourbon_sales_2022_by_zip_month.description: All Bourbon Whiskey sales transactions in the year 2022, filtered to non-null/non-empty ZIP codes and restricted to the year; keep columns needed for monthly and ZIP-level aggregations (sale_dollars, sale_date, zip_code, county, category_name).

zip_population_by_age.name: zip_population_by_age
zip_population_by_age.body_sql:
SELECT
  zipcode AS zip_code,
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN minimum_age IS NULL AND maximum_age IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN minimum_age IS NULL AND maximum_age IS NOT NULL THEN 0
        WHEN minimum_age >= 21 THEN population
        WHEN maximum_age >= 21 AND minimum_age < 21 THEN population * ( (maximum_age - 20) / NULLIF((maximum_age - minimum_age + 1),0) )
        WHEN maximum_age IS NULL AND minimum_age >= 21 THEN population
        ELSE 0
      END) AS population_21_plus
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2000' AND '2010'
GROUP BY
  zipcode
zip_population_by_age.description: Canonical population counts per ZIP code by age groups from the population_by_zip_<N> tables; normalize/union the various population_by_zip_<N> tables into one relation and produce a single 21_plus_population per zip_code (sum of residents aged 21 and older where age buckets exist).

monthly_bourbon_sales_by_zip.name: monthly_bourbon_sales_by_zip
monthly_bourbon_sales_by_zip.body_sql:
SELECT
  zip_code,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month,
  SUM(sale_dollars) AS total_bourbon_sale_dollars_in_month
FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
WHERE category_name = @category_name  -- e.g. "Bourbon"
GROUP BY zip_code, year, month
monthly_bourbon_sales_by_zip.description: Aggregate Bourbon Whiskey sales to monthly totals per zip_code and year-month using filtered transactions; yields one row per zip_code per month with total sale_dollars for that month and a year and month column for ordering.

providers_practice_location_cohort.name: providers_practice_location_cohort
providers_practice_location_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  npi,
  provider_business_practice_location_address_city_name,
  provider_business_practice_location_address_state_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nppes.npi_optimized`
WHERE
  -- keep only rows with at least one non-null practice location field to represent a practice-location cohort member
  (provider_business_practice_location_address_city_name IS NOT NULL
   OR provider_business_practice_location_address_state_name IS NOT NULL)
providers_practice_location_cohort.description: Cohort of providers (rows from npi_optimized) with practice location information canonicalized; one row per NPI representing the provider's business practice location attributes used for geographic filtering. This isolates providers by their practice address fields so downstream steps can join to taxonomy mappings.

taxonomy_code_specializations.name: taxonomy_code_specializations
taxonomy_code_specializations.body_sql:
SELECT
  code AS taxonomy_code,
  TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(specialization), r'\s+', ' ')) AS specialization
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nppes.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_set_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '090' AND '170'
  AND specialization IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(specialization) <> ''
GROUP BY
  code,
  specialization
taxonomy_code_specializations.description: Normalized mapping of taxonomy codes to specialization strings (specialization cleaned/canonicalized). One row per taxonomy_code / specialization combination from the healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_set tables, with empty/null specializations normalized out at this stage (but not filtering by city/state).

provider_specialization_cohort.name: provider_specialization_cohort
provider_specialization_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  npi,
  specialization
FROM (
  -- start from optimized NPI table which has one row per provider (joinable by npi)
  SELECT
    npi,
    TRIM(specialization) AS specialization
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.nppes.npi_optimized` AS n
  -- unpivot the repeated taxonomy code fields to get all taxonomy codes per npi
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST([
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_1 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_2 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_3 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_4 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_5 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_6 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_7 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_8 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_9 AS taxonomy_code),
    STRUCT(n.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_10 AS taxonomy_code)
  ]) AS unnested
  -- join taxonomy code lookup (the sharded taxonomy set) to get specialization text
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.nppes.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_set_*` AS t
    ON unnested.taxonomy_code = t.code
    AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '090' AND '170'
  -- prefer specialization from the lookup; fall back to empty string (will be filtered)
  WHERE unnested.taxonomy_code IS NOT NULL AND unnested.taxonomy_code != ''
)
-- deduplicate to one row per (npi, specialization)
WHERE specialization IS NOT NULL AND specialization != ''
GROUP BY npi, specialization
provider_specialization_cohort.description: For each provider NPI and specialization, a deterministic single row indicating the provider is associated with that specialization. This aggregates/join-resolves multiple taxonomy-code rows per provider into distinct (npi, specialization) pairs (deduplicated). One row per (npi, specialization) to enable counting distinct providers per specialization after applying geographic filters.

female_name_state_year_cohort.name: female_name_state_year_cohort
female_name_state_year_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  state,
  year,
  gender,
  number AS count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
WHERE
  gender = 'F'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  name,
  state,
  year,
  gender,
  number AS count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_2013`
WHERE
  gender = 'F'
female_name_state_year_cohort.description: One row per given name, state, year, and gender with the raw count of occurrences (a cohort filtered to female names). This captures counts of each given name by state and year for gender 'F'.

female_name_us_year_totals.name: female_name_us_year_totals
female_name_us_year_totals.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  year,
  SUM(number) AS us_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
WHERE
  gender = 'F'
GROUP BY
  name,
  year
female_name_us_year_totals.description: Aggregate to one row per given name and year for females: the total US count (summing counts across all states).

female_name_wy_year_counts.name: female_name_wy_year_counts
female_name_wy_year_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  name,
  year,
  SUM(number) AS wy_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
WHERE
  state = 'WY'
  AND gender = 'F'
GROUP BY
  name,
  year
female_name_wy_year_counts.description: One row per given name and year for females restricted to the state of Wyoming, providing the Wyoming count for each name and year.

female_name_proportion_by_state.name: female_name_proportion_by_state
female_name_proportion_by_state.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(wy.name, us.name) AS name,
  COALESCE(wy.year, us.year) AS year,
  wy.wy_count AS wy_count,
  us.us_count AS us_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current` AS src
-- derive Wyoming female counts per name/year
-- state code for Wyoming is 'WY'; gender for female is 'F'
-- Use aggregation to produce wy_count to ensure one row per name/year
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    name,
    year,
    SUM(number) AS wy_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
  WHERE state = 'WY' AND gender = 'F'
  GROUP BY name, year
) AS wy
ON src.name = wy.name AND src.year = wy.year
-- derive US female totals per name/year
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    name,
    year,
    SUM(number) AS us_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
  WHERE gender = 'F'
  GROUP BY name, year
) AS us
ON src.name = us.name AND src.year = us.year
-- restrict drive rows to female records to ensure correct grain and avoid duplicates
WHERE src.gender = 'F'
GROUP BY COALESCE(wy.name, us.name), COALESCE(wy.year, us.year), wy.wy_count, us.us_count
female_name_proportion_by_state.description: Denormalized row per given name and year combining Wyoming counts and US totals for females, so proportions (wy_count / us_count) can be computed. Does not apply final filtering or top-k selection.

ccrcc_proteome_samples.name: ccrcc_proteome_samples
ccrcc_proteome_samples.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.protein_abundance_log2ratio AS protein_abundance_log2ratio,
  q.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  q.aliquot_submitter_id AS aliquot_submitter_id,
  a.sample_submitter_id AS sample_submitter_id,
  a.sample_type AS sample_type_name,
  a.case_submitter_id AS case_submitter_id,
  f.file_id AS file_uuid
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.quant_proteome_CPTAC_CCRCC_discovery_study_pdc_current` AS q
LEFT JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.PDC_metadata.aliquot_to_case_mapping_current` AS a
ON
  q.aliquot_id = a.aliquot_id
LEFT JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.PDC_metadata.file_metadata_current` AS f
ON
  q.sample_id = f.file_id  -- lift file_uuid via file_id; adjust join key if a different mapping is used
WHERE
  q.protein_abundance_log2ratio IS NOT NULL
ccrcc_proteome_samples.description: Subset of proteome quantification rows for the CPTAC CCRCC proteome study with non-null protein_abundance_log2ratio and associated sample identifiers and sample_type metadata. One row per proteome measurement (peptide/protein-level row as present in the proteome table).

ccrcc_rnaseq_samples.name: ccrcc_rnaseq_samples
ccrcc_rnaseq_samples.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.fpkm_uq_unstranded AS fpkm_unstranded, -- lifted: use fpkm_uq_unstranded if intent was FPKM-UQ; user requested fpkm_unstranded so map directly from that column
  r.gene_name AS gene_symbol,
  atm.aliquot_submitter_id AS aliquot_submitter_id,
  atm.sample_submitter_id AS sample_submitter_id,
  r.sample_barcode AS sample_barcode,
  r.sample_type_name AS sample_type_name,
  atm.case_submitter_id AS case_submitter_id,
  pm.file_id AS file_uuid
FROM `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.RNAseq_hg38_gdc_current` r
JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.PDC_metadata.file_associated_entity_mapping_current` fam
  ON fam.entity_submitter_id = r.aliquot_barcode AND fam.entity_type = 'aliquot'
JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.PDC_metadata.aliquot_to_case_mapping_current` atm
  ON atm.aliquot_submitter_id = fam.entity_submitter_id
JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.PDC_metadata.file_metadata_current` pm
  ON pm.file_name = r.file_gdc_id OR pm.file_id = r.file_gdc_id
WHERE r.fpkm_unstranded IS NOT NULL
  AND r.sample_barcode IS NOT NULL
  AND r.sample_type_name IS NOT NULL
ccrcc_rnaseq_samples.description: Subset of RNA-seq expression rows for CPTAC samples (hg38 GDC RNAseq) with non-null fpkm_unstranded and associated sample identifiers and sample_type metadata. One row per RNAseq quantification per aliquot/sample and gene.

gene_sampletype_pearson_correlations.name: gene_sampletype_pearson_correlations
gene_sampletype_pearson_correlations.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  p.sample_type_name AS sample_type_name,
  COUNT(1) AS num_samples,
  CORR(p.protein_abundance_log2ratio, LOG10(r.fpkm_unstranded + 1)) AS pearson_correlation
FROM
  `ccrcc_proteome_samples` AS p
JOIN
  `ccrcc_rnaseq_samples` AS r
ON
  p.aliquot_submitter_id = r.aliquot_submitter_id
  AND p.gene_symbol = r.gene_symbol
  AND p.sample_type_name = r.sample_type_name
GROUP BY
  p.gene_symbol,
  p.sample_type_name
HAVING
  COUNT(1) >= 3
gene_sampletype_pearson_correlations.description: For each gene_symbol and sample_type_name, compute the Pearson correlation and count of matched samples between protein_abundance_log2ratio and log10(fpkm_unstranded + 1). Do not apply the abs>0.5 filter here; include only groups with at least 3 samples.

patient_annotations.name: patient_annotations
patient_annotations.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_barcode,
  COALESCE(case_gdc_id, case_barcode) AS entity_id,
  entity_type,
  category,
  classification,
  PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%E*S%Ez', date_created) AS annotation_date
FROM
  `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Annotations`
WHERE
  entity_type = 'Patient'
  AND category = @category
patient_annotations.description: Rows from the Annotations table for annotation entities of type 'Patient', retaining annotation fields needed to assess category and classification for each patient annotation.

participants_with_gene_mutation_flags.name: participants_with_gene_mutation_flags
participants_with_gene_mutation_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  ParticipantBarcode,
  MAX(CASE WHEN Hugo_Symbol = 'KRAS' AND FILTER = 'PASS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_KRAS_pass,
  MAX(CASE WHEN Hugo_Symbol = 'TP53' AND FILTER = 'PASS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_TP53_pass
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample`
GROUP BY
  ParticipantBarcode
participants_with_gene_mutation_flags.description: For each ParticipantBarcode, produce boolean/indicator flags (or equivalent rows) saying whether the participant has at least one passed mutation in each gene (e.g., KRAS, TP53). This rolls up mutation rows to one row per participant with per-gene presence indicators.

paad_participants_with_followup.name: paad_participants_with_followup
paad_participants_with_followup.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ParticipantBarcode
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_EBpp_AdjustPANCAN_IlluminaHiSeq_RNASeqV2_genExp` AS p
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_TCGA_RPPA_pancan_clean` AS r
ON
  p.ParticipantBarcode = r.ParticipantBarcode
WHERE
  p.Study = 'PAAD'
GROUP BY
  p.ParticipantBarcode
paad_participants_with_followup.description: All unique TCGA participant records that belong to the PAAD study and have an associated clinical follow-up record, one row per ParticipantBarcode.

high_quality_somatic_mutations_kras_tp53.name: high_quality_somatic_mutations_kras_tp53
high_quality_somatic_mutations_kras_tp53.body_sql:
SELECT
  ParticipantBarcode,
  Hugo_Symbol,
  Variant_Classification,
  FILTER,
  CONCAT(ParticipantBarcode, ":", Tumor_SampleBarcode, ":", CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ParticipantBarcode, Tumor_SampleBarcode, Hugo_Symbol, HGVSc, HGVSp_Short, Variant_Classification, FILTER ORDER BY ParticipantBarcode) AS STRING)) AS mutation_record_id
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample`
WHERE
  ParticipantBarcode IS NOT NULL
  AND Hugo_Symbol IN ("KRAS", "TP53")
  AND FILTER = "PASS"
  AND Variant_Classification IS NOT NULL
high_quality_somatic_mutations_kras_tp53.description: Somatic mutation records for genes KRAS and TP53 that meet high-quality variant criteria and have a non-null ParticipantBarcode; one row per mutation record (not deduplicated to participant).

imaging_level2_htan_center_filtered.name: imaging_level2_htan_center_filtered
imaging_level2_htan_center_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  entityId,
  HTAN_Data_File_ID,
  Imaging_Assay_Type,
  Component,
  HTAN_Center,
  -- carry other level2 columns commonly used for joins (Id and Filename when present)
  Id AS other_level2_columns_needed_for_joins,
  Filename AS other_level2_filename_for_joins
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level2_metadata_r*`
WHERE
  -- ensure this row has a center and a non-null component
  HTAN_Center IS NOT NULL
  AND Component IS NOT NULL
imaging_level2_htan_center_filtered.description: All Level2 imaging files (rows) from imaging_level2_metadata shards, filtered to rows that belong to any HTAN center (center column present) and that have a non-null Component value. Do not apply study-version-specific shard filters or exclude assay types here; just produce the filtered Level2 rows for later narrowing.

id_provenance_links.name: id_provenance_links
id_provenance_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  ip.entityId AS entityId,
  ip.HTAN_Data_File_ID AS HTAN_Data_File_ID,
  ip.HTAN_Parent_Data_File_ID AS HTAN_Parent_Data_File_ID,
  ip.HTAN_Assayed_Biospecimen_ID AS Parent_EntityId,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS provenance_shard
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.id_provenance_r*` AS ip
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '3' AND '5'
id_provenance_links.description: Provenance mapping rows that link derived entities/files to parent HTAN data files or entityIds. Include both child and parent identifiers and the provenance shard identifier; keep rows so they can be used to determine derivation relationships between Level2 and Level3/Level4 rows.

converted_regions_with_cytoband.name: converted_regions_with_cytoband
converted_regions_with_cytoband.body_sql:
SELECT
  cc.RefNo AS ref_no,
  cc.CaseNo AS case_no,
  cc.InvNo AS inv_no,
  cc.Clone AS clone_no,
  cc.Chr AS chromosome,
  cc.ChrOrd AS chr_ord,
  cc.Start AS start_pos,
  cc.`End` AS end_pos,
  cc.Type AS region_type,
  cc.CellsPresent AS cells_present,
  cb.cytoband_name AS cytoband_name,
  cb.hg38_start AS band_start,
  cb.hg38_stop AS band_stop,
  CASE WHEN cb.hg38_start IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS overlaps_cytoband
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` cc
LEFT JOIN
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38` cb
ON cc.Chr = cb.chromosome
  AND NOT (cc.`End` < cb.hg38_start OR cc.Start > cb.hg38_stop)
ORDER BY ref_no, case_no, inv_no, clone_no, chromosome, start_pos
grain: one row per converted genomic region (with possible multiple rows if region overlaps multiple cytobands)
converted_regions_with_cytoband.description: One row per converted cytogenetic region (from CytoConverted) annotated with hg38 cytoband overlap. Exposes genomic coords, chromosome, type, cells_present and matched cytoband_name and overlap flags/counts. Useful for region-level summaries, mapping abnormalities to cytobands, or aggregating recurrent hotspots. | Use for: aggregate regions by cytoband to find recurrent hotspots; filter regions overlapping specific cytobands or chromosomes; join to KaryAbnorm/KaryBreak to connect textual breakpoints to genomic coordinates

cohort_samples_cytogen.name: cohort_samples_cytogen
cohort_samples_cytogen.body_sql:
-- View body: one SELECT that defines the view cohort_samples_cytogen (category SEL)
-- Lifts literals: none (criteria are explicit: Morph = '3111' OR Topo = '0401')
SELECT
  CAST(c.RefNo AS INT64) AS RefNo,
  c.CaseNo AS CaseNo,
  i.InvNo AS InvNo
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.Cytogen` AS c
JOIN
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytogenInv` AS i
ON
  c.RefNo = i.RefNo
  AND c.CaseNo = i.CaseNo
WHERE
  (c.Morph = '3111' OR c.Topo = '0401')
GROUP BY
  RefNo, CaseNo, InvNo
cohort_samples_cytogen.description: Identify the cohort of distinct samples (investigations) that meet the clinical inclusion: parent Cytogen rows where Morph = '3111' OR Topo = '0401'. One row per distinct sample investigation (RefNo, CaseNo, InvNo) that should be considered in downstream denominators and joins.

canonical_cytoconverted_rows.name: canonical_cytoconverted_rows
canonical_cytoconverted_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  RefNo,
  CaseNo,
  InvNo,
  Clone,
  -- Normalize chromosome: trim, upper, map common alternatives (e.g., '23' -> 'X', '24' -> 'Y')
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(Chr) IS NULL OR TRIM(Chr) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(Chr)) IN ('23','X') THEN 'X'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(Chr)) IN ('24','Y') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE UPPER(TRIM(Chr))
  END AS Chr,
  ChrOrd,
  -- Ensure numeric start/end, coerce negatives/nulls to NULL
  NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(Start AS INT64), 0) AS Start,
  NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(`End` AS INT64), 0) AS `End`,
  Type,
  -- Normalize alteration_type to 'loss', 'gain', or NULL
  CASE
    WHEN Type IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(Type), r'\bloss\b|\bdel\b|\bdeletion\b|\bmonosomy\b|\b-') THEN 'loss'
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(Type), r'\bgain\b|\bdup\b|\bduplication\b|\bamplif|amp\b|\b\+') THEN 'gain'
    ELSE LOWER(TRIM(Type))
  END AS alteration_type
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted`
canonical_cytoconverted_rows.description: Normalized/cleaned CytoConverted rows with canonical chromosome, numeric start/end, and a normalized alteration_type label (e.g., 'loss' or 'gain') suitable for filtering and joins.

cytobands_chromosome_bounds.name: cytobands_chromosome_bounds
cytobands_chromosome_bounds.body_sql:
SELECT
  chromosome AS Chr,
  -- derive ChrOrd as integer ordering where possible: try numeric chromosome, else keep common X/Y as 23/24, others NULL
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(chromosome, r'^(chr|CHR)', '') AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
      THEN SAFE_CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(chromosome, r'^(chr|CHR)', '') AS INT64)
    WHEN LOWER(chromosome) IN ('x','chrx','CHR X','CHR X','X') THEN 23
    WHEN LOWER(chromosome) IN ('y','chry','CHR Y','Y') THEN 24
    ELSE NULL
  END AS ChrOrd,
  MIN(hg38_start) AS BandStart,
  MAX(hg38_stop) AS BandEnd
FROM `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38`
GROUP BY chromosome
cytobands_chromosome_bounds.description: Reference cytogenomic band/coordinate bounds per chromosome as available in CytoBands/hg tables (useful for canonical chr ordering or validation).

trips_with_station_join.name: trips_with_station_join
trips_with_station_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id,
  t.subscriber_type,
  t.bike_id,
  t.bike_type,
  t.start_time AS start_timestamp,
  DATE(t.start_time) AS start_date,
  t.start_station_id,
  t.start_station_name,
  ss.name AS start_station_name_official,
  ss.address AS start_station_address,
  ss.council_district AS start_station_council_district,
  ss.number_of_docks AS start_station_number_of_docks,
  t.end_station_id,
  t.end_station_name,
  es.name AS end_station_name_official,
  es.address AS end_station_address,
  es.council_district AS end_station_council_district,
  es.number_of_docks AS end_station_number_of_docks,
  t.duration_minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT * EXCEPT(modified_rank) FROM (
      SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY modified_date DESC) AS modified_rank
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations`
    ) WHERE modified_rank = 1
  ) AS ss
ON SAFE_CAST(t.start_station_id AS INT64) = ss.station_id
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT * EXCEPT(modified_rank) FROM (
      SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY modified_date DESC) AS modified_rank
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations`
    ) WHERE modified_rank = 1
  ) AS es
ON SAFE_CAST(t.end_station_id AS INT64) = es.station_id
grain: trip_id, one row per trip with station metadata columns
trips_with_station_join.description: Trips joined to start and end station metadata (latest station record by modified_date). Preserves trip-level grain and station ids/names for both ends. Useful for origin-destination analyses and for attaching station attributes like council_district or number_of_docks to trips. | Use for: OD matrices weighted by duration or trip counts; Analysis of trips by station attributes (e.g., council district, dock counts); Mapping trips with station coordinates after joining to station metadata

crime_events_daily_summary.description: Daily aggregated counts of crime incidents by primary_type and council district (when available). student_electric_long_trips.name: student_electric_long_trips

  duration_minutes,
  bike_type,

Station-name exclusions are not applied here to keep this cohort reusable.

trips_excluding_maintenance_stations.name: trips_excluding_maintenance_stations
trips_excluding_maintenance_stations.body_sql:
SELECT

  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`

daily_trip_counts.name: daily_trip_counts

trips_with_station_districts.name: trips_with_station_districts
trips_with_station_districts.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id AS trip_id,
  t.start_station_id AS start_station_id,
  t.end_station_id AS end_station_id,
  s_start.council_district AS start_council_district,
  s_end.council_district AS end_council_district
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s_start
ON
  t.start_station_id = s_start.station_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s_end
ON
  SAFE_CAST(t.end_station_id AS INT64) = s_end.station_id
WHERE
  s_start.status = 'active'
  AND s_end.status = 'active'
  AND s_start.council_district IS NOT NULL
  AND s_end.council_district IS NOT NULL
trips_with_station_districts.description: Trips joined to their start and end stations (restricted to active stations) to attach council_district for both ends; only rows where both stations have non-null council_district are retained.

trips_same_district.name: trips_same_district
trips_same_district.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id AS trip_id,
  s_start.council_district AS council_district
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s_start
ON
  CAST(t.start_station_id AS STRING) = CAST(s_start.station_id AS STRING)
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s_end
ON
  CAST(t.end_station_id AS STRING) = CAST(s_end.station_id AS STRING)
WHERE
  s_start.council_district IS NOT NULL
  AND s_end.council_district IS NOT NULL
  AND s_start.council_district = s_end.council_district
trips_same_district.description: Subset of trips where the start and end council_district values are equal (one row per trip), preserving the shared district value for aggregation.

daily_incident_counts_by_date.name: daily_incident_counts_by_date

molecule_properties_norm.name: molecule_properties_norm
molecule_properties_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key column: keep original molregno (string)
  CAST(s.molregno AS STRING) AS molregno,
  -- canonical_smiles comes from compound_structures (use wildcard across shards per DDL guidance)
  cs.canonical_smiles AS canonical_smiles,
  -- heavy_atoms: numeric-casted integer from compound_properties sharded tables (prefer numeric column if available)
  CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) AS heavy_atoms
FROM
  -- molecule_dictionary (non-sharded canonical identifiers). Use the unsharded base as a driving table to ensure one row per molregno.
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.molecule_dictionary` AS s
LEFT JOIN
  -- canonical smiles may be in either sharded or unsharded compound_structures; prefer the canonical (unsharded) and fall back to sharded latest-range if needed.
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_structures` AS cs
ON CAST(s.molregno AS STRING) = CAST(cs.molregno AS STRING)
LEFT JOIN
  -- compound_properties are sharded across suffixes '23' to '33' per DDL; join using wildcard to get numeric properties.
  -- Lift suffix range literals out of the view (caller should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX externally if needed),
  -- but to be reusable we include the wildcard and allow external filtering by _TABLE_SUFFIX.
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_properties_*` AS cp
ON CAST(s.molregno AS STRING) = CAST(cp.molregno AS STRING)
WHERE
  -- keep one row per molregno by preferring rows where at least the molregno matches; de-duplication across shards should be handled by downstream consumers.
  s.molregno IS NOT NULL
molecule_properties_norm.description: Normalized molecule-level properties and canonical identifiers, with numeric-casted fields for filtering (e.g., heavy_atoms as integer) and canonical_smiles.

activity_rows_sel.name: activity_rows_sel
activity_rows_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  activity_id,
  molregno,
  assay_id,
  standard_type,
  CAST(standard_value AS FLOAT64) AS standard_value,
  standard_relation,
  CAST(pchembl_value AS FLOAT64) AS pchembl_value,
  doc_id,
  potential_duplicate
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.activities_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '23' AND '33'
  AND standard_value IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(standard_value AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(pchembl_value AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND assay_id IS NOT NULL
  AND molregno IS NOT NULL
  AND doc_id IS NOT NULL
activity_rows_sel.description: Activity-row cohort filtered to rows with non-null standard_value, numeric-parsable standard_value, numeric pchembl_value, and containing linking keys to assay, molregno, doc_id; potential_duplicate preserved for later counting.

activity_counts_per_mol_assay.name: activity_counts_per_mol_assay
activity_counts_per_mol_assay.body_sql:
SELECT
  ar.molregno,
  ar.assay_id,
  COUNT(1) AS activity_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ar.potential_duplicate = '1' OR ar.potential_duplicate = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS potential_duplicate_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.activities_*` AS ar
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '23' AND '33'
  -- lift any question-specific filters (e.g., on standard_type) out of the view
GROUP BY
  ar.molregno,
  ar.assay_id
activity_counts_per_mol_assay.description: Per-molecule-per-assay aggregated counts from the filtered activity cohort: total activity count and count of potential_duplicate-flagged activities; used for eligibility filters (counts threshold) and to join back to eligible molecules.

fec_individual_contributions_2020_clean.name: fec_individual_contributions_2020_clean
fec_individual_contributions_2020_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  tran_id AS contribution_id,
  -- standardize ZIP to 5-digit string: take left 5 of zip_code if present and length>=5, else NULL
  -- Leave literals out of view (none here)
  CASE
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(COALESCE(zip_code, ''), r'^\d{5}') THEN SUBSTR(zip_code, 1, 5)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS donor_zip,
  -- state already provided as two-letter code in source; coerce empty -> NULL
  CASE WHEN TRIM(state) = '' THEN NULL ELSE state END AS donor_state,
  transaction_amt AS contribution_amount,
  -- contribution_date: ensure transaction_dt is DATE; if not, try PARSE_DATE
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(transaction_dt AS DATE) IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(transaction_dt AS DATE)
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(CAST(transaction_dt AS STRING) AS DATE) IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(CAST(transaction_dt AS STRING) AS DATE)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS contribution_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.individuals_ingest_2020`
WHERE
  -- only individual donors: entity_tp commonly 'IND' for individual; exclude committees/orgs (e.g., 'COM', 'ORG'), treat NULL as include only if name looks like person? Use entity_tp = 'IND'
  entity_tp = 'IND'
  -- non-null, non-zero amounts
  AND transaction_amt IS NOT NULL
  AND transaction_amt != 0
  -- contribution_date in calendar year 2020: filter by transaction_dt year = 2020 (use SAFE_CAST)
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM SAFE_CAST(transaction_dt AS DATE)) = 2020
  -- ensure contribution_id present
  AND tran_id IS NOT NULL
fec_individual_contributions_2020_clean.description: Individual-level FEC contribution records for calendar year 2020, filtered to individual donors (exclude committees/organizations), with non-null, non-zero contribution amounts, donor ZIP5 and donor state standardized (5-digit zip as string, state as two-letter code) and contribution_date parsed to date.

individual_contributions_2016_small.name: individual_contributions_2016_small
individual_contributions_2016_small.body_sql:
SELECT
  tran_id,
  cmte_id,
  transaction_amt,
  transaction_dt AS tran_date,
  other_id AS contributor_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fec.indiv*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '00' AND '98'
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM transaction_dt) = 2016
  AND transaction_amt > 0
  AND transaction_amt < 200
individual_contributions_2016_small.description: All individual contribution transactions from 2016 where each transaction amount is strictly greater than 0 and strictly less than 200. Keeps one row per contribution to allow later aggregation by committee.

fda_food_enforcement_core.name: fda_food_enforcement_core
fda_food_enforcement_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  recall_number,
  event_id,
  center_classification_date,
  report_date,
  termination_date,
  recall_initiation_date,
  SAFE_CAST(postal_code AS STRING) AS postal_code,
  UPPER(TRIM(state)) AS state_abbr,
  TRIM(city) AS city,
  TRIM(recalling_firm) AS recalling_firm,
  TRIM(product_type) AS product_type,
  TRIM(product_description) AS product_description,
  TRIM(distribution_pattern) AS distribution_pattern,
  TRIM(reason_for_recall) AS reason_for_recall,
  TRIM(status) AS status,
  UPPER(TRIM(classification)) AS classification,
  TRIM(product_quantity) AS product_quantity,
  IFNULL(NULLIF(TRIM(distribution_pattern), ''), NULL) IS NOT NULL AS has_distribution_pattern,
  IFNULL(NULLIF(TRIM(product_quantity), ''), NULL) IS NOT NULL AS has_quantity,
  COALESCE(country, '') AS country,
  address_1,
  address_2,
  more_code_info
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_enforcement`
grain: recall_number, event_id — one row per enforcement/recall event record
fda_food_enforcement_core.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of FDA food enforcement (recall) records. Use this as a canonical enforcement-event relation for counts, joins to geography, time-series, and text analysis. Preserves recall identifiers and key descriptive fields, converts date strings to DATE (already DATE in schema), canonicalizes status/classification casing, and exposes simple derived flags (has_distribution_pattern, has_quantity). | Use for: counts of recalls by state, country, classification, or status; time-series of recall activity (by report_date/recall_initiation_date); text searches on product_description or reason_for_recall; joins to geographic tables via state_abbr or postal_code

fdic_branch_locations_core.name: fdic_branch_locations_core
fdic_branch_locations_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  fdic_certificate_number,
  institution_name,
  branch_name,
  branch_number,
  main_office,
  TRIM(branch_address) AS branch_address,
  TRIM(branch_city) AS branch_city,
  SUBSTR(TRIM(zip_code), 1, 5) AS zip5,
  TRIM(branch_county) AS branch_county,
  NULLIF(TRIM(county_fips_code), '') AS county_fips_code,
  UPPER(TRIM(state)) AS state_abbr,
  TRIM(state_name) AS state_name,
  TRIM(institution_class) AS institution_class,
  TRIM(cbsa_fips_code) AS cbsa_fips_code,
  TRIM(cbsa_name) AS cbsa_name,
  cbsa_division_flag,
  cbsa_division_fips_code,
  cbsa_division_name,
  cbsa_metro_flag,
  cbsa_metro_fips_code,
  cbsa_metro_name,
  cbsa_micro_flag,
  csa_flag,
  csa_fips_code,
  csa_name,
  fdic_uninum,
  service_type,
  date_established,
  last_updated
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations`
grain: fdic_uninum or (fdic_certificate_number, branch_number) — one row per branch location
fdic_branch_locations_core.description: Cleaned projection of FDIC branch location rows. Use for spatial aggregations, institution-level rollups, CBSA/CSA analysis, and linking to FIPS/state tables. Preserves FDIC identifiers, institution name, address fields, geography codes, class flags, and exposes a main_office boolean and normalized ZIP and county FIPS. | Use for: branch counts per state/city/CBSA; identify main office vs branch locations; time-based queries on date_established or last_updated; join branches to state/FIPS crosswalks or to enforcement records by state

utah_zip_codes.name: utah_zip_codes
utah_zip_codes.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonicalize ZIP to 5-digit string (preserve leading zeros)
  LPAD(TRIM(z.zip_code), 5, '0') AS zip_code,
  z.state_code,
  z.state_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
WHERE
  -- select only ZIPs located in Utah (state_code 'UT')
  z.state_code = 'UT'
utah_zip_codes.description: One row per ZIP code for ZIPs located in Utah according to the ZIP codes boundary/table. Canonicalize ZIP to 5-digit string if needed. Does not apply question-specific literals beyond state selection.

utah_zip_fdic_counts.name: utah_zip_fdic_counts
utah_zip_fdic_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  z.state_code AS state_code,
  COALESCE(b.fdic_branch_count, 0) AS fdic_branch_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
JOIN
  -- restrict to Utah by state_code to get Utah ZIP list
  (SELECT DISTINCT zip_code, state_code, state_name
   FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes`
   WHERE state_code = 'UT') ut
  ON z.zip_code = ut.zip_code AND z.state_code = ut.state_code
LEFT JOIN
  -- aggregate FDIC branch counts by ZIP5 from FDIC locations
  (
    SELECT
      branch_zip AS zip5,
      COUNT(1) AS fdic_branch_count
    FROM (
      SELECT
        fdic_certificate_number,
        branch_number,
        -- FDIC table uses zip_code (5-digit); alias to branch_zip for clarity
        zip_code AS branch_zip
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations`
      WHERE zip_code IS NOT NULL
    )
    GROUP BY branch_zip
  ) b
ON z.zip_code = b.zip5
GROUP BY z.zip_code, z.state_code, b.fdic_branch_count
utah_zip_fdic_counts.description: Join of Utah ZIP code list to FDIC branch counts to produce one row per Utah ZIP with its FDIC branch count (zero if no matching FDIC rows). Keeps Utah ZIPs even when fdic_branches_by_zip has no row (left join semantics).

food_event_normalized_text_fields.name: food_event_normalized_text_fields
food_event_normalized_text_fields.body_sql:
SELECT
  report_number,
  -- split reactions and outcomes on commas into arrays, trimming whitespace and removing empty strings
  (SELECT ARRAY_AGG(TRIM(x) IGNORE NULLS) FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(COALESCE(reactions, ''), ',')) AS x WHERE TRIM(x) <> '') AS reactions_array,
  (SELECT ARRAY_AGG(TRIM(x) IGNORE NULLS) FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(COALESCE(outcomes, ''), ',')) AS x WHERE TRIM(x) <> '') AS outcomes_array,
  -- products_brand_name: keep original string and also split into array, but only replace comma+space not between digits before splitting
  products_brand_name,
  (
    SELECT ARRAY_AGG(TRIM(x) IGNORE NULLS)
    FROM UNNEST(
      SPLIT(
        -- replace comma+space sequences that are NOT between digits with ' -- '
        REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(products_brand_name, ''), r'(?<!\d),\s+(?!\d)', ' -- '),
        '--'
      )
    ) AS x
    WHERE TRIM(x) <> ''
  ) AS products_brand_name_array,
  -- products_industry_code, products_role, products_industry_name: replace ', ' with ' -- ' and then split on '--'
  products_industry_code,
  (
    SELECT ARRAY_AGG(TRIM(x) IGNORE NULLS)
    FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(products_industry_code, ''), r',\s+', ' -- '), '--')) AS x
    WHERE TRIM(x) <> ''
  ) AS products_industry_code_array,
  products_role,
  (
    SELECT ARRAY_AGG(TRIM(x) IGNORE NULLS)
    FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(products_role, ''), r',\s+', ' -- '), '--')) AS x
    WHERE TRIM(x) <> ''
  ) AS products_role_array,
  products_industry_name,
  (
    SELECT ARRAY_AGG(TRIM(x) IGNORE NULLS)
    FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(products_industry_name, ''), r',\s+', ' -- '), '--')) AS x
    WHERE TRIM(x) <> ''
  ) AS products_industry_name_array,
  -- consumer demographics unchanged
  consumer_gender,
  consumer_age,
  consumer_age_unit
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_events`
food_event_normalized_text_fields.description: Normalize and canonicalize textual product and event fields: split reactions and outcomes into arrays by commas; replace ', ' with ' -- ' in products_industry_code, products_role, and products_industry_name and expose them as arrays; transform products_brand_name by replacing only comma+space sequences that are not between digits (i.e., preserve digit,comma,digit patterns) with ' -- ' and expose both the original and the processed split-as-array; also expose consumer demographic fields unchanged. Does not apply date filters.

fdic_locations_fl_rows.name: fdic_locations_fl_rows
fdic_locations_fl_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- location_id: use branch_fdic_uninum if present, else compose from fdic_certificate_number + branch_number
  COALESCE(branch_fdic_uninum,
           CONCAT(fdic_certificate_number, '-', SAFE_CAST(branch_number AS STRING))) AS location_id,
  fdic_certificate_number,
  institution_name,
  zip_code,
  state AS state
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations`
WHERE
  -- exclude null/empty zip codes; lift any specific zip literal filtering out of the view
  zip_code IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(zip_code) <> ''
  -- lift state of interest out of the view (no hard-coded state filter here)
fdic_locations_fl_rows.description: Subset of FDIC branch location rows limited to the state of interest and excluding rows with null/empty zip codes; one row per raw location record.

filtered_banks_by_state.name: filtered_banks_by_state
filtered_banks_by_state.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name,
  SUM(total_assets) AS sum_total_assets,
  COUNT(1) AS filtered_institution_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.institutions`
GROUP BY
  state_name
filtered_banks_by_state.description: Per-state aggregated measures for institutions that will be filtered by name prefix and established_date later. Produces sum of total_assets and count of filtered institutions grouped by state_name. This aggregation expects its input to already be the filtered cohort (name/date filters applied later when composing final query).

institution_counts_by_state.name: institution_counts_by_state
institution_counts_by_state.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name,
  COUNT(1) AS total_institution_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.institutions`
GROUP BY

institution_counts_by_state.description: Total count of all institutions per state (no additional filters). One row per state_name with the total number of institution rows in that state.

colorado_zip_codes_geom.name: colorado_zip_codes_geom
colorado_zip_codes_geom.body_sql:
SELECT
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  z.state_code AS state_code,
  z.state_name AS state_name,
  z.zip_code_geom AS zip_code_geom
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
WHERE
  z.state_name = 'Colorado'
colorado_zip_codes_geom.description: All ZIP code polygons that are located in Colorado, with their canonical ZIP code identifier and geometry. This selects ZIP code rows for the state of Colorado but does not perform any spatial joins or aggregations.

us_blockgroups_geometries.name: us_blockgroups_geometries
us_blockgroups_geometries.body_sql:
SELECT
  geo_id AS blockgroup_geo_id,
  blockgroup_geom AS blockgroup_geom,
  area_land_meters AS area_land_meters,
  area_water_meters AS area_water_meters
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_blockgroups.blockgroups_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '78'
us_blockgroups_geometries.description: All US census block groups with their blockgroup identifier, geometry, and component area measures. Provides area_land_meters and area_water_meters so consumers can compute total blockgroup area.

zip5_blockgroup_overlaps.name: zip5_blockgroup_overlaps
zip5_blockgroup_overlaps.body_sql:
SELECT
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  z.zip_code AS zip5,
  bg.geo_id AS blockgroup_geo_id,
  ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(z.zip_code_geom, bg.blockgroup_geom)) AS intersection_area_m2,
  ST_AREA(bg.blockgroup_geom) AS blockgroup_area_m2
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_blockgroups.blockgroups_*` AS bg
ON
  TRUE
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '78'
  AND z.zip_code_geom IS NOT NULL
  AND bg.blockgroup_geom IS NOT NULL
  AND ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(z.zip_code_geom, bg.blockgroup_geom)) > 0
zip5_blockgroup_overlaps.description: Pairwise spatial intersections between ZIP5 polygons and census block group polygons: for each ZIP5 and blockgroup that overlap (non-zero intersection), include intersection area in square meters and the blockgroup total area in square meters. Does not apply state filtering or bank-count weighting; it expects canonical ZIP geometries and blockgroup geometries as inputs.

reactome_physical_entity_to_lowest_level.name: reactome_physical_entity_to_lowest_level_tas_pathway_mappings
reactome_physical_entity_to_lowest_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  pe.stable_id AS physical_entity_id,
  p.stable_id AS pathway_id,
  pe_to_pathway.evidence_code AS mapping_evidence_code,
  p.stable_id AS pathway_stable_id,
  p.name AS pathway_name,
  p.lowest_level AS pathway_lowest_level
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` AS pe_to_pathway
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` AS pe
ON
  pe_to_pathway.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` AS p
ON
  pe_to_pathway.pathway_stable_id = p.stable_id
WHERE
  pe_to_pathway.evidence_code = 'TAS'
  AND p.lowest_level = TRUE
reactome_physical_entity_to_lowest_level.description: Select mappings from Reactome physical entities to pathways restricted to mappings whose evidence_code is 'TAS' and to pathways marked as lowest_level = TRUE. One row per physical_entity to pathway mapping.

human_target_to_reactome_physical_entity.name: human_target_to_reactome_physical_entity_mapping
human_target_to_reactome_physical_entity.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.interactionID AS interaction_row_id, /* carry a key to keep joinable; not in final required CSV but kept for view reuse */
  t.targetID AS targetId,
  pe.stable_id AS physical_entity_id,
  pe.name AS target_symbol,
  COALESCE(t.target_uniprotID, pe.uniprot_id, pe.ensembl_id) AS target_uniprot_or_identifier
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1` t
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.target_synonyms_v1` s
ON
  t.targetID = s.targetID
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
ON
  -- match by UniProt if available, otherwise by Ensembl; this preserves many-to-many mapping where present
  (t.target_uniprotID IS NOT NULL AND t.target_uniprotID != '' AND pe.uniprot_id = t.target_uniprotID)
  OR
  (t.target_uniprotID IS NULL OR t.target_uniprotID = '' ) AND (pe.ensembl_id IS NOT NULL AND pe.ensembl_id != '' AND pe.ensembl_id = s.synonym)
human_target_to_reactome_physical_entity.description: Canonical mappings linking human targets (Targetome target identifiers) to Reactome physical_entity rows; one row per target-to-physical-entity mapping. This enables joining drug-target cohorts to Reactome pathways.

health_nutrition_population_latest_by_co.name: health_nutrition_population_latest_by_country_indicator
