grain: one row per original observation (augmented with rank) — partitioned by country_code + indicator_code
health_nutrition_population_latest_by_co.description: Per (country_code, indicator_code) returns the most recent observation (highest year) with its value and a rank. Use to get latest available indicator values or to filter to top-K most recent by year. | Use for: retrieve latest indicator value per country; trend analysis using latest-available datapoints; filter to most recent N observations per indicator/country

indicator_series_catalog.name: indicator_series_catalog
indicator_series_catalog.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.series_code AS series_code,
  s.topic AS topic,
  s.indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  s.short_definition AS short_definition,
  s.long_definition AS long_definition,
  s.unit_of_measure AS unit_of_measure,
  s.periodicity AS periodicity,
  s.source AS source,
  csd.country_code AS country_code,
  csd.description AS country_series_description,
  st.year AS year,
  st.description AS year_description
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.series_summary` AS s
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.country_series_definitions` AS csd
  ON s.series_code = csd.series_code
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.series_times` AS st
  ON s.series_code = st.series_code
grain: one row per series_code x country_code x year (when series_times has multiple year rows)
indicator_series_catalog.description: Denormalized catalog of indicator metadata by joining series_summary to country_series_definitions and series_times. One row per series_code with descriptive fields and available time descriptions. Use to enrich indicator codes with human-readable definitions and available years. | Use for: lookup indicator metadata for code; join metadata to fact tables for labeling; list available years/descriptions for a series

wdi_indicators_data_clean.name: wdi_indicators_data_clean
wdi_indicators_data_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name AS country_name,
  country_code AS country_code,
  indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  indicator_code AS indicator_code,
  SAFE_CAST(value AS FLOAT64) AS value,
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  IF(value IS NULL, TRUE, FALSE) AS value_is_null
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
grain: one row per original indicators_data observation
wdi_indicators_data_clean.description: Cleans and normalizes the WDI indicators_data table: preserves core columns, casts value/year to consistent types and exposes a flag for missing values. Use as a canonical fact table for WDI indicators. | Use for: time series queries on WDI indicators; joining WDI data to other series by country/year; filtering or imputing missing indicator values

international_debt_rows.name: international_debt_rows
international_debt_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name,
  indicator_name,
  year,
  value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
WHERE
  value IS NOT NULL
international_debt_rows.description: All raw rows from the international_debt table with NULL values filtered out for the numeric value column. This is the cleaned cohort of debt observations to use for aggregation or ranking.

country_indicator_max_values.name: country_indicator_max_values
country_indicator_max_values.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name,
  indicator_name,
  MAX(value) AS max_value,
  ANY_VALUE(year) AS year_of_max
FROM (
  SELECT country_name, indicator_name, value, year FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_education.international_education`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT country_name, indicator_name, value, year FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT country_name, indicator_name, value, year FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT country_name, indicator_name, value, year FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
)
WHERE value IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY country_name, indicator_name
HAVING COUNT(1) > 0
country_indicator_max_values.description: Per country and indicator, compute the maximum observed numeric value and one corresponding year when that maximum occurred.

country_cohort.name: country_cohort
country_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Canonical country name for joins; lift any selection literals out of the view
  cs.long_name AS country_name
FROM
  -- Use wildcard to cover all shards; caller can restrict _TABLE_SUFFIX in queries against this view if needed
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.country_summary*` AS cs
WHERE
  -- Keep only rows that look like actual countries: have a non-null two_alpha_code or country_code and a non-empty long_name
  (cs.two_alpha_code IS NOT NULL OR cs.country_code IS NOT NULL)
  AND cs.long_name IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(cs.long_name) <> ''
GROUP BY
  cs.long_name
country_cohort.description: Cohort of countries of interest (canonical country_name rows). This isolates rows for a single country when joining with aggregated indicator metrics.

health_country_2017_2018_wide.name: health_country_2017_2018_wide
health_country_2017_2018_wide.body_sql:
SELECT
  h.country_code AS country_code,
  h.country_name AS country_name,
  MAX(CASE WHEN h.year = 2017 THEN h.value END) AS health_2017,
  MAX(CASE WHEN h.year = 2018 THEN h.value END) AS health_2018
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population` AS h
WHERE
  h.indicator_name = 'Current health expenditure per capita (current US$)'
GROUP BY
  h.country_code,
  h.country_name
health_country_2017_2018_wide.description: One row per country with per-capita current health expenditure (PPP) values pivoted to columns for year 2017 and 2018 (health_2017, health_2018). Only structural reshaping; do not apply numeric filters here.

population_health_join.name: population_health_join
population_health_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  h.country_code AS country_code,
  h.country_name AS country_name,
  p.population_2017 AS population_2017,
  p.population_2018 AS population_2018,
  h.health_2017 AS health_2017,
  h.health_2018 AS health_2018
FROM (
  -- source: world_bank_global_population.population_by_country unpivoted into year rows then pivoted to 2017/2018
  SELECT
    country_code,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2017 THEN population END) AS population_2017,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2018 THEN population END) AS population_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`,
    UNNEST([
      STRUCT(1960 AS year, year_1960 AS population),
      STRUCT(1961 AS year, year_1961 AS population),
      STRUCT(1962 AS year, year_1962 AS population),
      STRUCT(1963 AS year, year_1963 AS population),
      STRUCT(1964 AS year, year_1964 AS population),
      STRUCT(1965 AS year, year_1965 AS population),
      STRUCT(1966 AS year, year_1966 AS population),
      STRUCT(1967 AS year, year_1967 AS population),
      STRUCT(1968 AS year, year_1968 AS population),
      STRUCT(1969 AS year, year_1969 AS population),
      STRUCT(1970 AS year, year_1970 AS population),
      STRUCT(1971 AS year, year_1971 AS population),
      STRUCT(1972 AS year, year_1972 AS population),
      STRUCT(1973 AS year, year_1973 AS population),
      STRUCT(1974 AS year, year_1974 AS population),
      STRUCT(1975 AS year, year_1975 AS population),
      STRUCT(1976 AS year, year_1976 AS population),
      STRUCT(1977 AS year, year_1977 AS population),
      STRUCT(1978 AS year, year_1978 AS population),
      STRUCT(1979 AS year, year_1979 AS population),
      STRUCT(1980 AS year, year_1980 AS population),
      STRUCT(1981 AS year, year_1981 AS population),
      STRUCT(1982 AS year, year_1982 AS population),
      STRUCT(1983 AS year, year_1983 AS population),
      STRUCT(1984 AS year, year_1984 AS population),
      STRUCT(1985 AS year, year_1985 AS population),
      STRUCT(1986 AS year, year_1986 AS population),
      STRUCT(1987 AS year, year_1987 AS population),
      STRUCT(1988 AS year, year_1988 AS population),
      STRUCT(1989 AS year, year_1989 AS population),
      STRUCT(1990 AS year, year_1990 AS population),
      STRUCT(1991 AS year, year_1991 AS population),
      STRUCT(1992 AS year, year_1992 AS population),
      STRUCT(1993 AS year, year_1993 AS population),
      STRUCT(1994 AS year, year_1994 AS population),
      STRUCT(1995 AS year, year_1995 AS population),
      STRUCT(1996 AS year, year_1996 AS population),
      STRUCT(1997 AS year, year_1997 AS population),
      STRUCT(1998 AS year, year_1998 AS population),
      STRUCT(1999 AS year, year_1999 AS population),
      STRUCT(2000 AS year, year_2000 AS population),
      STRUCT(2001 AS year, year_2001 AS population),
      STRUCT(2002 AS year, year_2002 AS population),
      STRUCT(2003 AS year, year_2003 AS population),
      STRUCT(2004 AS year, year_2004 AS population),
      STRUCT(2005 AS year, year_2005 AS population),
      STRUCT(2006 AS year, year_2006 AS population),
      STRUCT(2007 AS year, year_2007 AS population),
      STRUCT(2008 AS year, year_2008 AS population),
      STRUCT(2009 AS year, year_2009 AS population),
      STRUCT(2010 AS year, year_2010 AS population),
      STRUCT(2011 AS year, year_2011 AS population),
      STRUCT(2012 AS year, year_2012 AS population),
      STRUCT(2013 AS year, year_2013 AS population),
      STRUCT(2014 AS year, year_2014 AS population),
      STRUCT(2015 AS year, year_2015 AS population),
      STRUCT(2016 AS year, year_2016 AS population),
      STRUCT(2017 AS year, year_2017 AS population),
      STRUCT(2018 AS year, year_2018 AS population),
      STRUCT(2019 AS year, year_2019 AS population)
    ]) AS y
  GROUP BY country_code
) AS p
FULL JOIN (
  -- source: health_nutrition_population table filtered to relevant indicator(s) if needed outside view;
  -- here we aggregate per country_code to get health values for 2017 and 2018 (per-capita value column)
  SELECT
    country_code,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2017 THEN value END) AS health_2017,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2018 THEN value END) AS health_2018,
    MAX(country_name) AS country_name
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
  GROUP BY country_code
) AS h
ON p.country_code = h.country_code
population_health_join.description: Denormalized one-row-per-country join of population_years (2017/2018) and health per-capita (2017/2018) using country_code as the key, producing the paired numeric columns needed to compute percent changes and qualifying logic.

country_long_term_debt_totals.name: country_long_term_debt_totals
country_long_term_debt_totals.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  ANY_VALUE(country_name) AS country_name,
  SUM(value) AS total_long_term_external_debt
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
WHERE
  indicator_name = 'Long-term external debt' -- lift literal: indicator identifying long-term external debt
  AND value IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  country_code
country_long_term_debt_totals.description: Per-country aggregated total long-term external debt: sum of numeric 'value' across all years for the long-term external debt indicator. This produces one row per country_code and preserves country_name where available. It does not yet apply region-based exclusion.

international_debt_raw_rows.name: international_debt_raw_rows
international_debt_raw_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name,
  country_code,
  indicator_name,
  indicator_code,
  year,
  value,
  NULL AS unit,
  NULL AS source
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
international_debt_raw_rows.description: Row-level subset representing the raw rows from the international_debt table with no aggregation; serves as the base cohort for further cleaning and filtering.

international_debt_normalized.name: international_debt_normalized
international_debt_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonicalized country_name: trim whitespace and NULL-safe cast to STRING
  TRIM(CAST(country_name AS STRING)) AS country_name,
  -- canonicalized country_code: upper-case, trim; keep NULL if absent
  UPPER(TRIM(CAST(country_code AS STRING))) AS country_code,
  -- indicator_name normalized: trim
  TRIM(CAST(indicator_name AS STRING)) AS indicator_name,
  -- indicator_code normalized: trim and upper
  UPPER(TRIM(CAST(indicator_code AS STRING))) AS indicator_code,
  -- year cast to INT64
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  -- value cast to FLOAT64
  CAST(value AS FLOAT64) AS value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
WHERE
  -- exclude rows where value is NULL (lifted out of view so reusable)
  value IS NOT NULL
international_debt_normalized.description: Canonicalized/cleaned version of international_debt rows: casts numeric fields, normalizes country name/code fields, and excludes rows where value is NULL. Does not apply question-specific literal filters (e.g., specific country or value=0) so it can be reused.

debt_indicator_rows_for_country_cohort.name: debt_indicator_rows_for_country_cohort
debt_indicator_rows_for_country_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name,
  country_code,
  indicator_name,
  indicator_code,
  year,
  value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
WHERE
  -- Lifted parameters: replace the literals below with the desired country name or code.
  -- Match rows for a cohort identified by either country_name OR country_code.
  (country_name = 'REPLACE_COUNTRY_NAME' OR country_code = 'REPLACE_COUNTRY_CODE')
debt_indicator_rows_for_country_cohort.description: Cohort of normalized international_debt rows that identify a given country by either country_name or country_code. This sub-goal is parameterizable by country_name or country_code values.

rows_with_value_exact_zero.name: rows_with_value_exact_zero
rows_with_value_exact_zero.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name,
  country_code,
  indicator_name,
  indicator_code,
  year,
  value
FROM (
  -- international_education table
  SELECT
    country_name,
    country_code,
    indicator_name,
    indicator_code,
    year,
    value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_education.international_education`
  WHERE value = 0

  UNION ALL

  -- world_bank_wdi indicators_data table
  SELECT
    country_name,
    country_code,
    indicator_name,
    indicator_code,
    year,
    value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
  WHERE value = 0

  UNION ALL

  -- international_debt table
  SELECT
    country_name,
    country_code,
    indicator_name,
    indicator_code,
    year,
    value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
  WHERE value = 0

  UNION ALL

  -- health_nutrition_population table
  SELECT
    country_name,
    country_code,
    indicator_name,
    indicator_code,
    year,
    value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
  WHERE value = 0
)
rows_with_value_exact_zero.description: Subset filter that selects rows where the numeric value is exactly zero (value = 0). This is a reusable filter to apply to any numeric-valued indicator cohort.

country_gdp_values.name: country_gdp_values
country_gdp_values.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  year,
  value
FROM (
  -- World Development Indicators GDP series (multiple indicator_codes for different GDP measures)
  SELECT country_code, year, value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
  WHERE indicator_name LIKE '%GDP%' OR indicator_code LIKE 'NY.GDP%'

  UNION ALL

  -- International education dataset may contain GDP-related entries rarely; include if labeled
  SELECT country_code, year, value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_education.international_education`
  WHERE indicator_name LIKE '%GDP%' OR indicator_code LIKE 'NY.GDP%'

  UNION ALL

  -- Health & population dataset sometimes includes GDP per capita related indicators; include GDP labels
  SELECT country_code, year, value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
  WHERE indicator_name LIKE '%GDP%' OR indicator_code LIKE 'NY.GDP%'

  UNION ALL

  -- International debt dataset may reference GDP ratios; include GDP-labeled series
  SELECT country_code, year, value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
  WHERE indicator_name LIKE '%GDP%' OR indicator_code LIKE 'NY.GDP%'
)
-- Ensure canonical per-country/year rows (keep all GDP-value rows for later aggregation)
country_gdp_values.description: All GDP data values for each country-year retained as rows (prepared for further aggregation). This groups/organizes GDP value rows per country and year but does not compute summary statistics; it ensures a clean per-country-year value set for median calculations.

canonical_feature_toggle_library_list.name: canonical_feature_toggle_library_list
canonical_feature_toggle_library_list.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry-through keys for joinability
  rd.repository_name_with_owner AS artifact_name,
  -- Canonical library name: lifted literal should be set when creating the view; placeholder here uses repository owner/name lowercased as a best-effort canonicalization
  LOWER(rd.repository_name_with_owner) AS canonical_library_name,
  rd.host_type AS platform,
  -- library_languages: use repository_language from projects table when available, else NULL
  pwf.repository_language AS library_languages
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.repository_dependencies` AS rd
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.projects_with_repository_fields` AS pwf
ON
  rd.dependency_project_id = pwf.id
canonical_feature_toggle_library_list.description: Canonical list of feature-toggle/feature-flag client libraries (external knowledge) with their known artifact/project names, canonical library name, supported platform(s), and languages. Used to map dependency artifact names and platforms to a canonical library and its languages.

repositories_with_fallback_project_field.name: repositories_with_fallback_project_fields
repositories_with_fallback_project_field.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.id AS repository_id,
  COALESCE(r.name_with_owner, pwrf.repository_name_with_owner) AS repository_name_with_owner,
  COALESCE(r.host_type, pwrf.repository_host_type) AS repository_host_type,
  -- size in KB in tables; user requested repository_size_kb
  COALESCE(r.size, pwrf.repository_size) AS repository_size_kb,
  COALESCE(r.language, pwrf.repository_language) AS repository_language,
  COALESCE(r.fork_source_name_with_owner, pwrf.repository_fork_source_name_with_owner) AS repository_fork_source_name_with_owner,
  COALESCE(r.updated_timestamp, SAFE_CAST(pwrf.repository_last_synced_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) AS repository_updated_timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.repositories` AS r
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.projects_with_repository_fields` AS pwrf
ON
  r.id = pwrf.repository_id
WHERE
  COALESCE(r.host_type, pwrf.repository_host_type) IN ('GitHub', 'GitLab', 'Bitbucket')
repositories_with_fallback_project_field.description: Repository rows using repositories as primary source; when repository columns are missing for a repository_id, fall back to projects_with_repository_fields.repository_* fields. Includes only repositories/projects that represent code hosts of interest (host types like GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket).

fire_calls_core_events.name: fire_calls_core_events
fire_calls_core_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  incident_number,
  date_of_call AS call_date,
  timestamp_of_call,
  time_of_call,
  cal_year,
  hour_of_call,
  incident_group,
  stop_code_description,
  special_service_type,
  property_category,
  property_type,
  address_qualifier,
  postcode_full,
  postcode_district,
  borough_code,
  borough_name,
  proper_case,
  ward_code,
  ward_name,
  ward_name_new,
  easting_m,
  northing_m,
  easting_rounded,
  northing_rounded,
  frs,
  incident_station_ground,
  first_pump_arriving_attendance_time,
  first_pump_arriving_deployed_from_station,
  second_pump_arriving_attendance_time,
  second_pump_arriving_deployed_from_station,
  num_stations_with_pumps_attending,
  num_pumps_attending
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls`
grain: incident_number (one row per fire brigade call)
fire_calls_core_events.description: Normalized event-level fire brigade calls with canonical timestamp, date parts, and preserved location identifiers. Use this as the cleaned fire-call base for filtering, aggregations, and joins. | Use for: Filter recent or historical fire calls by date/borough/postcode; Aggregate response times or pumps attended by borough/year; Join to crime aggregates by borough and year

crime_monthly_by_geography.name: crime_monthly_by_geography
crime_monthly_by_geography.body_sql:
SELECT
  lsoa_code,
  borough,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  year AS crime_year,
  month AS crime_month,
  SUM(value) AS crimes_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  lsoa_code,
  borough,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  year,
  month
grain: one row per (lsoa_code OR borough) x major_category x minor_category x year x month
crime_monthly_by_geography.description: Monthly crime counts aggregated at the available geography rows (preserves both lsoa_code and borough). Produces totals per major/minor category and exposes year/month for time-based joins and aggregations. | Use for: Time series of crime counts by borough or LSOA; Compare crime counts to fire incidents by month/year and geography; Roll up monthly counts to yearly or category-level summaries

borough_monthly_fire_summary.name: borough_monthly_fire_summary
borough_monthly_fire_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough_name AS borough,
  cal_year AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATE(timestamp_of_call)) AS month,
  COUNT(incident_number) AS fire_calls_count,
  AVG(num_pumps_attending) AS avg_pumps_attending,
  AVG(first_pump_arriving_attendance_time) AS avg_first_pump_arrival_secs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN first_pump_arriving_attendance_time IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS first_pump_arrival_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls`
GROUP BY
  borough_name,
  cal_year,
  month
grain: one row per borough x year x month
borough_monthly_fire_summary.description: Aggregated monthly counts and average response metrics for fire calls at the borough and year/month level. Useful to compare with crime aggregates or to rank boroughs by fire activity/response. | Use for: Compare monthly fire call volume across boroughs and years; Correlate borough-level fire activity with crime counts; Rank boroughs by average response time or pumps attending

borough_crime_yearly_totals.name: borough_crime_yearly_totals
borough_crime_yearly_totals.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough,
  year AS crime_year,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  SUM(value) AS crimes_count_yearly
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  borough,
  year,
  major_category,
  minor_category
grain: one row per borough x year x major_category x minor_category
borough_crime_yearly_totals.description: Yearly totals of crimes aggregated to borough level. Aggregates both when rows are at borough granularity or when LSOA rows contain borough and should be summed up. Exposes major/minor categories for category-level comparisons. | Use for: Annual crime comparisons across boroughs; Join yearly crime totals to yearly fire summaries by borough

fire_calls_with_crime_borough_join.name: fire_calls_with_crime_borough_join
fire_calls_with_crime_borough_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.incident_number,
  f.timestamp_of_call,
  DATE(f.timestamp_of_call) AS call_date,
  f.borough_name AS borough,
  f.postcode_district,
  f.ward_name,
  f.easting_m,
  f.northing_m,
  c.major_category,
  c.minor_category,
  c.crime_year,
  c.crime_month,
  c.crimes_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls` AS f
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    borough,
    major_category,
    minor_category,
    year AS crime_year,
    month AS crime_month,
    SUM(value) AS crimes_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
  GROUP BY
    borough,
    major_category,
    minor_category,
    year,
    month
) AS c
ON
  f.borough_name = c.borough
  AND f.cal_year = c.crime_year
  AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATE(f.timestamp_of_call)) = c.crime_month
grain: one row per fire incident (enriched with 0-or-more matching crime category-month rows; because join is on category too, each incident may appear multiple times if multiple crime categories are present for the borough/month)
fire_calls_with_crime_borough_join.description: Left join of normalized fire calls to borough-level monthly crime aggregates. Preserves event-level fire rows enriched by matching borough and year/month crime counts (NULL when no matching crime row). Useful for incident-level analysis that needs corresponding borough-month crime context. | Use for: Study relationships between fire incidents and crime categories in the same borough-month; Build per-incident features that include borough-month crime counts for modeling

borough_yearly_rank_by_crimes.name: borough_yearly_rank_by_crimes
borough_yearly_rank_by_crimes.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough,
  crime_year,
  total_crimes,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY crime_year ORDER BY total_crimes DESC) AS crimes_rank_in_year
FROM (
  SELECT
    borough,
    year AS crime_year,
    SUM(value) AS total_crimes
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
  GROUP BY
    borough,
    year
)
grain: one row per borough x year
borough_yearly_rank_by_crimes.description: Yearly rank of boroughs by total crimes (all categories). Exposes borough, year, total_crimes and rank to support Top-K borough analyses without hardcoding K. | Use for: Get top-N boroughs by crimes for a given year (downstream WHERE crimes_rank_in_year <= N); Trend rank changes of boroughs across years

borough_fire_monthly_running_counts.name: borough_fire_monthly_running_counts
borough_fire_monthly_running_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough_name AS borough,
  cal_year AS year,
  month,
  SUM(1) AS monthly_calls,
  SUM(SUM(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY borough_name, cal_year ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_calls_year_to_date
FROM (
  SELECT
    incident_number,
    borough_name,
    cal_year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATE(timestamp_of_call)) AS month
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls`
)
GROUP BY
  borough_name,
  cal_year,
  month
ORDER BY
  borough_name,
  cal_year,
  month
grain: one row per borough x year x month
borough_fire_monthly_running_counts.description: Running cumulative count of fire calls within each borough for each year ordered by month. Useful for visualization of cumulative incidents through a year and comparisons across boroughs. | Use for: Plot cumulative fire calls across months within boroughs; Compare speed of accumulation of incidents between boroughs

crime_minor_category_pivot_by_borough_ye.name: crime_minor_category_pivot_by_borough_year
crime_minor_category_pivot_by_borough_ye.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough,
  year AS crime_year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN minor_category IS NOT NULL THEN value ELSE 0 END) AS total_crimes_all_minor_categories
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  borough,
  year
grain: one row per borough x year (aggregated across minor categories)
crime_minor_category_pivot_by_borough_ye.description: Pivot-style reshape: wide counts of crimes by minor_category per borough-year using conditional aggregation. Useful for comparing category mixes across boroughs without external pivot operations. | Use for: Create downstream pivots by replacing the conditional aggregation with explicit minor categories; Compare borough-level category mixes when expanded

fire_incident_response_quality_flags.name: fire_incident_response_quality_flags
fire_incident_response_quality_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  incident_number,
  timestamp_of_call,
  borough_name AS borough,
  CASE WHEN first_pump_arriving_attendance_time IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_first_pump_arrival_time,
  CASE WHEN second_pump_arriving_attendance_time IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_second_pump_arrival_time,
  CASE WHEN num_pumps_attending > 1 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS multiple_pumps_attended
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls`
fire_incident_response_quality_flags.description: Derived flags indicating whether first pump arrival time is recorded and whether multiple pumps attended. Use for filtering or feature creation to indicate notable response characteristics. | Use for: Filter incidents with missing arrival times; Identify incidents with multiple pumps for operational analysis

minor_category_totals_by_year.name: minor_category_totals_by_year
minor_category_totals_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  minor_category,
  SUM(value) AS category_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  year,
  minor_category
minor_category_totals_by_year.description: Total crime counts (sum of value) per year and minor_category across all boroughs and lsoa_codes — one row per year and minor_category for ranking and percentage calculation.

crime_incident_rows.name: crime_incident_rows
crime_incident_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  borough,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
WHERE
  year IS NOT NULL
  AND major_category IS NOT NULL
  AND minor_category IS NOT NULL
  -- NOTE: Lifted filter literal: categorize "Other Theft" incidents outside the view; view returns standardized rows.
crime_incident_rows.description: Row-level subset of crime_by_lsoa with non-null year and standardized category columns; a basic cohort of crime incidents before any aggregation.

crime_category_canonicalized.name: crime_category_canonicalized
crime_category_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  borough,
  TRIM(LOWER(major_category)) AS major_category,
  TRIM(LOWER(minor_category)) AS minor_category,
  CAST(value AS INT64) AS value,
  CONCAT(CAST(CAST(year AS INT64) AS STRING), '|', IFNULL(borough,''), '|', TRIM(LOWER(major_category)), '|', TRIM(LOWER(minor_category)), '|', CAST(CAST(value AS INT64) AS STRING)) AS row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
crime_category_canonicalized.description: Normalized/cleaned projection of crime rows with trimmed/canonicalized major and minor category text and integer-cast year and value.

crime_yearly_totals_by_borough_category.name: crime_yearly_totals_by_borough_category
crime_yearly_totals_by_borough_category.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  borough,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  SUM(value) AS total_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  year,
  borough,
  major_category,
  minor_category
crime_yearly_totals_by_borough_category.description: Aggregated totals of value per year, borough, major_category and minor_category (one row per grouping key).

images_with_original_url.name: images_with_original_url
images_with_original_url.body_sql:
SELECT
  image_id,
  original_url
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images`
WHERE
  original_url IS NOT NULL
images_with_original_url.description: All image rows that have a non-null original_url; one row per image_id including its original_url and any other identifying image metadata.

labels_for_images.name: labels_for_images
labels_for_images.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.image_id AS image_id,
  l.label_name AS label_name,
  l.confidence AS confidence
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels` AS l
labels_for_images.description: All label rows for images, preserving label_name and confidence for each image_id and label instance.

images_with_cat_label_candidates.name: images_with_cat_label_candidates
images_with_cat_label_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.image_id,
  i.original_url,
  l.label_name,
  l.confidence
FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` AS i
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels` AS l
  USING (image_id)
grain: one row per image_id, label_name, confidence
images_with_cat_label_candidates.description: Join of images (with original_url) to their labels to associate each image_id and original_url with any matching label rows; used to determine presence/absence of a specific label for each image.

state_corn_production_rows.name: state_corn_production_rows
state_corn_production_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(NULL AS INT64) AS year,
  state_name,
  state_alpha,
  commodity_desc,
  group_desc,
  unit_desc,
  CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64) AS value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
WHERE group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
  AND commodity_desc = 'CORN'
  AND unit_desc = 'BU'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  CAST(NULL AS INT64) AS year,
  state_name,
  state_alpha,
  commodity_desc,
  group_desc,
  unit_desc,
  CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64) AS value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.census*`
WHERE group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
  AND commodity_desc = 'CORN'
  AND unit_desc = 'BU'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  CAST(NULL AS INT64) AS year,
  state_name,
  state_alpha,
  commodity_desc,
  group_desc,
  unit_desc,
  CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64) AS value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.census_*`
WHERE group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
  AND commodity_desc = 'CORN'
  AND unit_desc = 'BU'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  CAST(NULL AS INT64) AS year,
  state_name,
  state_alpha,
  commodity_desc,
  group_desc,
  unit_desc,
  CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64) AS value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.economics`
WHERE group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
  AND commodity_desc = 'CORN'
  AND unit_desc = 'BU'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  CAST(NULL AS INT64) AS year,
  state_name,
  state_alpha,
  commodity_desc,
  group_desc,
  unit_desc,
  CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64) AS value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.environmental`
WHERE group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
  AND commodity_desc = 'CORN'
  AND unit_desc = 'BU'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  CAST(NULL AS INT64) AS year,
  state_name,
  state_alpha,
  commodity_desc,
  group_desc,
  unit_desc,
  CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64) AS value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.demographics`
WHERE group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
  AND commodity_desc = 'CORN'
  AND unit_desc = 'BU'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
state_corn_production_rows.description: Subset of the state-level production rows representing corn measured in bushels (unit_desc = 'BU') from the FIELD CROPS group for any year. Keeps rows at the same per-row grain for later aggregation by state and year.

activity_rows_upto_cutoff.name: activity_rows_upto_cutoff
activity_rows_upto_cutoff.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  `by`,
  timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
WHERE
  timestamp <= @global_cutoff_timestamp
activity_rows_upto_cutoff.description: All activity rows from the source table up to and including the global cutoff timestamp. This is the canonical input cohort for downstream month-based computations.

user_monthly_presence.name: user_monthly_presence
user_monthly_presence.body_sql:
SELECT
  ar.by AS `by`,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ar.timestamp) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM ar.timestamp) AS month,
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(ar.timestamp, MONTH, "UTC") AS month_start_utc
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full` AS ar
GROUP BY
  ar.by,
  year,
  month,
  month_start_utc
user_monthly_presence.description: Normalized rows indicating, for each user and calendar month (UTC year+month derived from timestamp), whether the user had any activity in that month. One row per user per month that appears in the data (only months with >=1 record are emitted).

irs_990_filtered_rows.name: irs_990_filtered_rows
irs_990_filtered_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  CAST(tax_pd AS INT64) AS tax_pd,
  totrevenue,
  totfuncexpns
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '990_2012' AND '990_2017'
  AND totrevenue IS NOT NULL
  AND totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL
  -- carry key columns for grain (ein and sub_id). sub_id is not a named column in this table;
  -- if a secondary id is needed downstream, users should JOIN on `ein` and any other identifier from `irs_990_ein`.
irs_990_filtered_rows.description: Subset of IRS Form 990 filing rows kept for analysis: only include rows from the 990 yearly shards (all per-year tables) with non-null values for total revenue and total functional expenses, and canonicalize/cast the key year column. Does not apply top-k or ordering.

channel_country_counts.name: channel_country_counts
channel_country_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  channelGrouping,
  COUNT(DISTINCT country) AS country_count
FROM
  `data-to-insights.ecommerce.all_sessions`
WHERE
  -- lift any date or other literal filters out of the view; include all rows
  TRUE
GROUP BY
  channelGrouping
channel_country_counts.description: For each channelGrouping, count the number of distinct countries that have transaction records (based on the aggregated transactions_by_channel_country). Returns one row per channelGrouping with the distinct country count.

normalized_transactions.name: normalized_transactions
normalized_transactions.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  visitStartTime,
  SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) AS transactions_int
FROM
  `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
normalized_transactions.description: Normalize and cast the transactions field to an integer per web_analytics row; treat non-numeric or null totals.transactions as NULL and ensure a canonical column name for transaction counts.
